very moist and easy to make, will make again and again, thanks for posting
Very good and easy! We used  Pork, Mushroom and Soy Sauce Meatballs recipe #120300 (which were frozen) and provolone cheese. Thanks for sharing this super easy recipe which we will be having often!
I roasted these for the recommended 45 minutes and they were beginning to brown.  I think I would have liked them even more had I roasted until they were carmelized a bit.

This was good...I thought that the Thousand Island sandwich spread was a little too sweet for our tastes, but overall, it was a good recipe.  I did add a package of taco seasoning mix to the beef as it was cooking, and I would probably use shredded cheddar cheese next time.  Thank you for sharing this recipe....It was tasty and very easy to put together.
Interesting.  Real bacon would be better I think.  Tell your DH thanks.
This didnt work for me at all.  The cakes came out with a crispy sugary top crust, which I had to remove before frosting.
YUM!  Thanks.

This was a very good dense bread.  We really enjoyed this!!!  The directions are perfect!!
Thanks for posting
Karen

These were so delicious and  very easy.  I was making them for dinner when the kids stopped by and they had to sample them.  Everyone loved 'em and I'll definitely be making them again.  I prefer using fresh ingredients rather than frozen products...  and I love that the peel isn't removed.... very tasty!  Perfect combination of spices, too!  Thanks for sharing this recipe!

I made this last night after seeing a similar recipe in Family Circle magazine.  I made it using tomato soup instead of cheddar soup, I added tomato sauce and kicked it up by adding some hot pepper sauce. I didn't add pepperoni but next time I will make it I will add turkey pepperoni to make it lighter.  This recipe is easy to make and delicious!

This is the first marmalade I've ever made;  I chose this recipe mainly because it proceeded in a manner that I could follow.  Some of the others were far too intricate and complicated for me!  The directions were easy to follow,  and the results were admirable.  I made it exactly as the recipe states and it is lovely, clear with bits of peel floating in a amber jelly.  Not too sweet,  just right.  Thanks for an excellent recipe.  This is my marmlade recipe from now on;  no others need apply. All best from BB.

DH and I had to start the South Beach diet after eating all the goodies on this site. This is a tasty little dish. Fills you up so you aren't hunting for you next meal. It's easy to prepare and does reheat well. I top mine with other piece of Canadian bacon before reheating to keep everything in it's place and it becomes a hand held meal.

Such a wonderfully moist cake this is. Served it at a birthday party and everyone one took a bite and said " this must be made from scratch"  Loved the carmel icing but look forward to topping it with  chocolate icing at another time. Baked it in a 9x13 pan. It rose perfectly even.   Just a fabulous cake, Thank-you Roosie!
This a light dish, yet very tasty. The sauce is what makes the difference. I used asparagus instead of the snowpeas and everyone thought it was a great combination.

We thouroughly enjoyed this quiche.  I didn't have egg whites, but substituted Egg Beaters (which really is the same thing).   I thought the texture was very pleasing, and the spinach and cheese made a nice combination.  Served with some garlic crostini, and we had a very nice meal.  Thanks for posting this recipe.  It goes into my t&t cookbook.

Great recipe Raxyl. I cooked 300g of Tasmanian scallops as a single serve but used the same amount of herbs and spices but with only 20g of butter. This gave a quite a powerful flavour which I liked but other's might like to stick with the original proportions. Otherwise I used the original recipe with the exception I replaced the lemongrass with lemon thyme just because a few places I checked didn't have any lemongrass. For the rice at the centre of the plate I didn't have Basmati so used a generic long grain rice cooked with a little Turmeric, along with a light salad. Made a great meal and I enjoyed along with some Penfolds Koonunga Hill Semillon Chardonnay.

So easy and fun to make, I made them yesterday and confess there aren't many left.  It's a quick and tasty yeast bread so I can make more as needed.  Thank you for sharing it.  I think I'll try some of the suggestions of substituting whole wheat bread for some of the white next time.  And there WILL be a next time.

This was very good, and easily doubled for my 6 pound turkey. I added a chopped onion. This was hard to wait for because the smell of this cooking is wonderful. I would definitally stop cooking at 7-8 hours. I did mine for 9, and some of the meat was a bit dry. Thanks for a great easy mid-week meal.
These ribs were the damn bomb and those words are not in my vocab, that damn good.I let the ribs tenderize a bit more 30mins. I will be makin again. I used kansas city masterpiece barbque sauce.
Excellent scallops!  I did have lemongrass--pared everything down to make a single serving.  So easy to put together and such great flavor!  I also had it with a Chardonnay.

So happy to find a savory side using acorn squash. This was so easy to prepare with easy and accurate directions. I loved the was filling flavors worked together with the squash and seemed to make it taste that much sweeter but in a natural, supple sort of way.  Added a teaspoon of dried sage, and though I thought this was a bit too much, it was the right spice for bringing the other flavors together.  Thanks Dancer.
I was craving an iced coffee and this one hit the spot.  I think I'll be sure to have a pitcher of it in my fridge from now on!
I followed the recipe exactly. My family and I just didn't care for it. For us something was missing...can't figure out what.

Very good.  The aroma while cooking was wonderful and the chops were moist. Baked for about 1 hour at 375. I added 2 Tbl Worchestershire, 2 tsp dry mustard, 4 tsp cider vinegar and 4 cloves garlic plus doubled Katha's recipe.  Family and guests gave it 5 stars.
Thanks for an easy and delicious dinner.
Of course, 5 stars!!! Piled it high-high. Who could go wrong with YOUR directions and those yummy ingredients. Delish!! Hope you like the photo. Hugs, Caroline

After looking through the snickerdoodle recipes and thinking mine wasn't here, I found your which is the same as mine to the letter.  SO, I'm giving this one 5 stars as I think it's the best out there.  They stay soft, have a great flavor.
These were yummy and look so pretty too. I didn't have any allspice so I used a combo of cloves & ginger along with the nutmeg. Thanks for the great recipe!

I prepared this to spread on rye crackers for the Canapé Challenge.  The blend of flavors was excellent.  As the other reviewer stated, this is made up of ingredients that I always have on hand.  A perfect staple for drop in guests.
This was fun!  We made a "whole mess" of noodles yesterday.  Just in time for "St Patty's Day"  Serving them with alfredo sauce - - smooth.

WOW! That is all I can say!! I was worried that there was too much dry ingredients, but it all worked out, and I think I have a new favorite cookie, and next time I will need to make 2 batches, one to cook, and one to eat the dough!!!
The sauce was fantastic.  A little hot, but it was still fantastic.

I agree with Merlot. Have the ingredients on hand and assorted crackers.Here is the exception, I use pimento stuffed olives drained and sliced, since MH won't eat black olives. I like both and sometimes make both. Good recipe!Gives it a little color too.
This smelled really good, but unfortunately we found it to be a little bland. Also, though I drained everything really well, the dish was a little watery...
Awesome idea! We often eat "plain" meat because we don't have time to marinate ... will definitely be doing this! Thank you so much for sharing! :)
Just WOW! I made this for a crowd of 70 with mozarella and it was gobbled up.  Someone took the left over sauce and marinated a chicken! It was just so good. Thank you!

This makes lovely fluffy tender bread. I had no idea what to expect from shredded wheat, but I am very happy with the results. I used 2 or 3 Italian dressing mix recipes on Zaar for reference to make my own approximation of the dressing mix. What I used turned out to be a little strong, so I will adjust it next time, but it's still very good. Oh, and my oven isn't the right shape for long loaves, so I made 16 rolls, 45 to 50 grams each. Thank you so much for this recipe. It's wonderful.

OMG!  This was a wonderful sandwich, and although I stone ground mustard with horseradish in place of the mayo, I did add the turkey as well and could not have been more pleased. I may add some dill pickles next time too!  :) Very big sandwich, so bring your appetite with this one!  Thanks so much for a simple recipe but oh so good.

I made this for #84750 and it worked extremely well. It is perfect for a tropical climate as the extra cornflour stops the icing from falling off within 5 minutes of taking it out of the fridge. It is  very easy to make and even tastes good.
BIG OLE yummy for this recipe.  I have made this two times already, and a friend asked me to make it for her daughters 16th birthday party coming soon.

I made this recipe almost as written....I left out the salt as I usually find that anything with a seasoning packet usually packs enough salt for me....if I needed more I could add it at the table. I did put the bacon into the microwave for 1 1/2 minutes. I then cut the bacon into 1 1/2 inch pieces so I could distribute it over the pie more evenly. When I removed the pie from the oven, I let it set for about 10-15 mins. so it would set up and hold its shape for cutting. Because the bacon had some precooking...it did crisp up very nicely in the oven. The recipe was okay, husband thought it was very good. I will probably make it again when something quick is needed.

This is the real deal, not one of those faux "soda bread" recipes with additional ingredients.  (They might be tasty but they are not real soda bread.)  Let the bread cool and rest a few hours if you want the slices to hold together.  I never can though.  It's too good warm!  Thanks for posting this authentic recipe.
These had a nice texture but I think that next time I'll cut back on the spices in the batter and add some cinnamon.   I was wanting a bolder cinnamon flavor than what I got from this.
Another favorite that I really like.  I have dry skin (28 years old) and this works great!

This is good, hearty. I used 2 portabellas instead of one, and after I assembled the sauce, I left it on low in the crock-pot for a few hours until dinner. I felt it needed more spice, and although there is a lot of meat, I felt the sauce part was really thin. I'll make this again, but I'll likely add oregano and other spices as well as tomato paste to thicken it. Also, this made waaayy more than 4 servings, I think it is at least 6.

I used beef shortribs and was fantastic ! I Just wish I knew what to do with the Dr.Pepper 'soup' cause I don't want to throw it away :(  I also feel so sorry for those who don't know about this recipe, that's a shame. Thanks for sharing this recipe !

This is the second time I've made these, and LOVE them!  I used frosting recipe #19649 and they work great together!  I love the fact that you don't have to wait for the dough to chill, and that they roll out so easily.  Be sure to take the cookies out of the oven before they begin to brown, for the best flavor.  I submitted 2 photos of the spring flower cookies I made this afternoon!  They look like they are from a nice bakery!  Enjoy!

I love these mints.  They were very easy to make and tasted great.  I did change the recipe slightly by adding 1 1/2 T cocoa and 1 tsp of vanilla, so I could have chocolate mint patties.  I also used the microwave to melt the chocolate chips.  Like one of the other reviewers, I rolled the dough into balls.  Everyone who has tried them has really enjoyed them.
This is 5+ stars! It is very easy to prepare. It reminded DH and myself of meatloaf we had in grade school. It will be made over again and again. Thank you for sharing this wonderful meatloaf recipe.

SO IMPRESSIVE, elegant looking, and so easy!!!  For me, I would have liked it a little sweeter, but for my husband it was perfect (he likes desserts not too sweet). I personally preferred eating it cold rather than warm.  Great recipe.
Tasty recipe! Thanks!

Mmm...liked it. This dressing is like hot mayo, but instead of oil it's made in milk. I served it over salad greens, half a thinly sliced  red onion and double bacon. Some boiled eggs and red pepper wouldn't go amiss, either.

Very good, but I think that I'll peel my eggplant before I start the cooking process.  My oven would only allow me to cook them about 8 minutes on each side.  Will definately make again.  I had some leftover cheese and spaghetti sause from Pizza Spirals OAMC Recipe #136550 that I heated up and put on top of the eggplant.  Very yummy!!

Tasty, easy, and cheesy. I used a 10 oz. can of biscuits so they'd be a little bigger and easier to press into shape, and was able to get two batches of these in the oven in no time. My only complaint is that they came out really salty, probably from the cream of chicken soup.

Northernmom,the recipe does say to use a 9x9 pan.I dont think you read it correctly.Anyways,this recipe is delish!!!!I was looking for a recipe that was similar to a childhood one my mom used to make and this was it.YUM!!

Good and easy.  Used the pan juices to add to the gravy bag that came with the turkey to make a tasty gravy.  Turkey might have actually been a tad dry without it.  But a good recipe when you're in a hurry!
wonderfull recipe I also grate the apples  will make again & again
I'm giving this 5 stars, but my picky husband and daughter didn't care for it.  I thought it was excellent and can't wait to use the leftovers for cuban sandwiches.

A super easy, delicious from scratch cake!  I iced the two-layer cake with the Really Easy and Good Chocolate Buttercream Frosting Recipe #89207.  It was a great combination.  My friends thought it was a store bought cake.  I used whole milk to ensure moistness.  I'm not sure if this was necessary but I wanted to be safe.  The 30 minutes of bake time was perfect.

This recipe was GREAT!  The only change I made was to use 3 lbs of imitation crabmeat instead of 1 lb.  When I made it with 1 lb, the sour cream and other vegtables overpowered the taste and I did not taste any of the crabmeat!  With 3 lbs it was OUT OF THIS WORLD!!!

My husband made this for us and it was delicious!  He used celery, a teaspoon of fennel seeds, and orzo pasta. He also cut back a little on the sundried tomatoes since we only have the kind in oil and he thought it might be too salty. The soup was thick and flavorful, but the hint of fennel was was what made it phenomenal!

This was so good and surprisingly easy. Instead of deep-frying the wings I coated them with flour, salt, pepper, a little bit of cayenne powder and garlic powder and baked them on a cookie sheet at 400 degrees for an hour then moved them to a deeper dish, mixed them with the prepared sauce, and baked them for an additional 10 minutes. Will be making these again, and will make sure I have extra napkins as they are tasty but messy.

These ROCK! I don't usually like sugar cookies. I made them for my DH. They are light and buttery. I frosted them with recipe #19649. I love that the dough doesn't have to be refrigerated first and is very forgiving. I did have to mix the last of the flour in with my hands (when she says by hand she means it! LOL.) Excellent! Thank you!
I too made these for mexican night and they were the star of the menu...I am going to make them again for euchre next month
My family loved this recipe.  Instead of water I used 2 bottles of Lager.  Thank you for making a wonderful fast meal
I made this and the fish balls fell apart.So I added crushed crackers to the balance of the fish mixture and it stayed together as fried fish patties, not balls.

Dough is easy to make, especially in the KitchenAid, and easy to work with. No chilling is a huge bonus. Buttery cookies, best when not allowed to brown. I needed round sugar cookies for a project, so rolled the dough into a log and sliced like the refrigerated stuff (which I refuse to use). Would be fabulous with cookie icing. Thanks for sharing your recipe!
My husband and I really enjoyed the taste of this dish.  Next time I will add more soy sauce, though. Thanks for sharing this.
I was looking for a Catalina dressing recipe to go with taco salad. This was great!! I actually used 6 packets of Splenda instead of the 4 T. sugar. Worked out great!! Thank you for posting!!
These are the greatest cookies!  I make them year-round!  YUMMY!  They freeze well in between wax paper.  I make smaller cookies, but the BIG ones are good too.

10 stars for this incredible salad - it's like a mouthful of sunshine!  I've made it several times already - we're addicted to it.  I make half a batch, but do admit to adding the raisins and sunflower seeds with reckless abandon. Thank you for sharing this fabulous recipe!

This was wonderful! I used extra spinach, as I had two 10-ounce packages on hand and used them both. Since I used more spinach, I also tossed in an extra clove of garlic. I left the halloumi, feta, and other ingredient amounts the same, though, and it was still plenty rich. I did have to substitute dried oregano for the fresh, since I didn't have fresh available. Great recipe--thanks for posting!

Obviously not the most health-conscious dish around, but a wonderful occasional indulgence. I did use a bit less butter. This simple recipe is great as is, but the garlic-lover in me thinks it would be exceptional with the addition of a few cloves of garlic. :) Thanks for posting!
This marinade is AWESOME!  The only thing I left out was the lemon juice (personal preference).  The chicken was so moist and flavorful.  Thanks so much for sharing.

Excellent! There's nothing quite like those 'grandma recipes' especially when it is a recipe from a grandma that owned a bakery! My only mistake is just making half a recipe! I did weigh the sugar and the flour, also found a simple sprinkling of sugar was the favorite here. As suggested in answer to my inquiry ...I just used a pinch of that mace which worked well for our tastes. I loved the lemon zest but did add a teaspoon of lemon juice as well. I will definitely be making this one again! Thank you Barb for sharing your grandmother's recipe.
Yuck!  I didn't like these at all.  I love cheesecake, but I don't like how these turned out.  If I did make these again, I would use a different crust.

I am getting the hang of this recipe, and enjoying my alterations. This time I subbed 1 c of ww flour, and raw cane sugar for the brown sugar. I'm starting to see that I need 1/4 more flour to start with, that the baking soda should read "salt", and that it takes about 30 minutes at 350 to get these "lightly browned", i.e. "done". Yum.
Dry, and too strong of a wheat taste.  Kind of Chewy.  I'll give it credit for being good for the calories, but I would recomend finding a different recipe.
My DD followed the recipe exact and it was very thick - used 2 kiwis and 1 banana - Would like to make freezer pops out of this - great way to get good vitamins into the kids. thanks

This was very different. I didn't want it to be to sour which i was worried about but it turned out fine. I think it would match well with salmon.
Thanks for this different recipe!

YUM YUM!! I made it last night and there are no leftovers..I baked in a 9X13 and didnt take it out after it cooled fo 10 minutes so it stuck a bit..Next time i will follow directions ;0)It didnt stop them from scraping the bottom of the pan ;0) Will use this recipe over and over again. Thanks for sharing
I tweeked this a bit by adding the whole can of tomato paste and a bit of hotsauce.  I also used yogurt instead of creme fraiche.  It was terrific.  Nice thick comfort type soup. Thanks Chef Dudo

I made these for dinner and followed what coconutcream did, I doubled everything though and used two rolls of 10 oz biscuits. I patted them flat and put them in greased muffin cups and hardly any clean up. I used regular soup though. These were wonderful, The family loved them and definately will make them again. Made a salad and angel hair chicken pasta for a side dish with it. Thank you so much for a wonderful recipe. They were really good..
this is a wonderful recipe for my kids! They absolutely loved it. For a bit of razzle dazzle I suggest to serve with cool whip. It sounds weird but is delicious!~

This is a very nice chocolate cake - very moist & dense w/o being heavy.  I wasn't sure if the brown sugar should be packed or not.   Most recipes call for it to be packed, so I did so.  I did find that the frosting did not obtain the proper consistency with stirring, so I ended up adding more powdered sugar to get it where it needed to be.  I doubled the recipe, and made 2 sheet cakes, one for a c-worker's birthday & one to placate my husband who was moping because I hadn't baked recently.  I used the caramel frosting on  one & white on the other.  Both were enjoyed.
These bars were Awesome!  Everyone loved them.  My MIL does not like too much cheesecake taste. She said it was the perfect amount!!   My DH tore these up!!!!  Thanks Bev... Will make these often!!

Impera_Magna suggested these for my hubby he has heart problems.  He gives them 5 stars, which honestly, amazed me as they don't look like his "normal" fry would.  I realized after I had them cut up that I didn't have any garlic salt so used lite salt.  I really didn't think he would eat them after I saw the finished product but made 2 potatoe's and he ate all! (I am not a fry eatter) Thanks to you for the recipe and Impera_Magna for telling me about it.

W o n d e r f u l !!  I loved this potato salad! Even my husband, who is a confirmed pea-hater, said that the peas in this recipe were just right!  I personally loved the peas in place of celery which would have been the norm in most potato salad recipes.  I had a little trouble with step #4. This time, I cooked the bacon through, removed the bacon from the pan and then cooked the onion which worked perfectly!  Needless to say, this salad was an awesome hit at our table!  Thanks, Jan!

For years I have yearned to be reunited with a very special food...something we Hoosiers call "spanish sauce". I grew up in a small northern Indiana town and we had 3 drive-in hot dog stands...all unique in their own way. Spanish dogs were just a way of life there.  Each of these family-owned hot dog stands had their very own special home-made family recipe sauce and albiet close, each had it's own special taste...but all were great in their own way.  Some people were only "west end" sauce eaters...others strictly "east end".  Then there were those "south side" saucies who dared to cross the tracks to the other side and away from the "standard" sauce of the region.  I know it sounds silly...but hot dog sauce was serious where I grew up.  MY POINT??  I haven't lived in my home town for almost 20 years now...going back only now and then at which time we absolutely do not miss the opportunity to stop and get some spanish dogs.  I DON'T HAVE TO EVER WAIT TO GO HOME AGAIN!! I have attempted 4 other times with recipes that I thought might be a good substitute only to be disappointed.  YOU, my dear dear fellow zaarian, have hit the proverbial nail on the head!  It is not 100%...but let me tell you...99.99876% doesn't get any closer..and we'll take it!!  Ironically...that's the glory of dog sauce.  Each is unique in it's own way and yours falls right into place.  

The night I made this my husband and I sat at the table with our plate of dogs and not a word was spoken.  That said it all!!  With the exception of the ancho chili powder, which I could not find for my first batch but will for future batches, I followed your recipe word for word.  The one thing I did as far as technique was to take my stick blender (motor boat thingy) and make the sauce a smoother consistency to mimic our favorite "south side" sauce from back home. For anyone who wishes to partake in the glory of this dog sauce, may I suggest the traditional long skinnies (type of dog) and very hot steamed buns (slightly open buns, cut side down, wrapped in a kitchen towel on top of a cooling rack that you have placed over the pot of boiling dogs).  

So, in a nutshell I apologize for the book-length review, but there was really no other way to express to you our gratitude for your fantastic "dog sauce" recipe.  My freezer will never be without it for the rest of my cooking life!  Thanks again for your great "trip down memory lane" recipe! :)

This as great. It smelled like apple pie baking but tasted nothing like that. I have made it twice once as is once with giner instead of cardamom. My family prefers the ginger version.
Yummy! We have never eaten at a White Castle before but these were awesome! Kind of reminded us of a Krystal burger. My whole family loved them...especially my 1 yr old son! Thanks for sharing!

Another fantastic recipe from my favorite Zaar chef!  I made a batch of these for my neighbors as a thank you for a hand-me-down bike for my little girl, and they said they definitely got the better end of the deal!  Of course, I saved a couple for my husband and me to sample, too.  My husband, who loves cheesecake, really enjoyed these bars.  Easy to make as well.
I have tried this recipe on countless occasions and every single person I know (save one) think's it is also a very good recipe.  There is no accounting for people's taste.

A definite make-again!  The only thing I did differently was use dry sherry in place of water, and thickend the sauce a tiny bit.  I threw in some thin asparagus for the last minute or two.  I served it with spicy fried rice, and we devoured it all.

I have been wanting, truly wanting, to like eggplant. Until this recipe, I thought I never would. This is awesome! It's so simple, too! The eggplant turns out surprisingly light...almost marshmallowy. Now, that may be because I used full-fat mayo (I know, I know... shame on me). Also, since I'm an avid low-carber and don't eat flour, I exchanged bread crumbs with ground up pork rinds I'd run through the food processor. Heavenly. It truly is. In fact, I'm sitting with a plate of it next to me right now and... oh, darn. I'm gonna go eat. Thanks, James!
Yup!  Thanks for posting!  This is how I've done it for years!  One other tip...when you press it flat, push hard and you will hear the breast bone crack.  It wil lay flatter then.

This is very similar to what my grandmother (baba) used to make for Christmas, Thanksgiving and Easter. She also had a version with bacon, but I prefer it without. Thanks for posting this. It was easy to make and very tasty, bringing back some great childhood memories!

This was a great recipe.  The pumpkin flavor was just right.  I took this to a football party today and there was not a crumb left.  I did kick the pumpkin pie spice up a notch.  I think the next time I make it I will throw in raisins.
My husband and I LOVED this recipe!  I added Basil and Garlic and it was so wonderful.  They came out looking to cute also, I just love them!

These are wonderful.  I rolled them into balls and flattened them with my hand like another reviewer had suggested, worked great.  I will be making these over and over.  After dipping them in chocolate, I placed them in the freezer for a bit to set, I just didn't have the patience to wait to try one.  These taste like they would be so hard to make but they are actually quite simple.  thank you for posting such a wonderful recipe.

Autumn 2006 PAC:

Sherryb is right.  Don't let the long list of ingredients fool you.  This recipe is simple and delicious.
My husband ate 3/4's of the pan by himself (yes, he is a big boy).

I had never made enchiladas with Rotel and they gave the dish a nice kick.

Thank you for sharing this recipe.  I will be making it again.
Very delicious, very easy. I served this with Roasted Broccoli with Gremolata, and it was a delightful hearty vegetarian meal.
This was great!! Would also be good with mandarin oranges instead of pineapple.
Delicious! I used 2 large sweet potatoes and cut them into a little smaller cubes. Loved the spicy flavors, and will make this again. Thanks!
this was so good... I was really surprised! I didn't have enough swiss cheese, so I used some sharp cheddar also, and it was good. I didn't rinse the saurkraut either as I like the tang.

My whole family LOVED these and that is saying A LOT!!!! I used ground turkey as I usually do in recipes. I also didn't have a mini muffin tin so I used a regular one with great results. Thanks so much for the recipe! It is a keeper FOR SURE!
I have very picky kids so I added a little sugar instead of the mustard.. They loved them.

Firstly, I made this Egg Drop soup following the directions to the letter T. The eggs did thread nicely, but I think the milk sort of seperated from the egg white and curddled a tad as there were little curddled milk balls floating at the edges of the pan and later my bowl. Also, it was very bland. I think next time, I will either try homemade broth or canned broth. Sorry this one was just okay.

I think this is really good as written, but next time we will make a few changes. Sautee the pierogis in some butter or oil until they get crispy and just toss with the sauce. They may be messier to eat this way, but as written, they get only semi-crispy in the oven and the sauce really dries up on them, creating a more of a dry coating. They are quite spicy, so if you want to tone it down, leave out the cayenne. We like the heat, so it was fine for our tastes. Served with ranch dressing. Thanks for posting this! This is really fun snack food and a different way to get pierogis!

This was so quick and easy! Everyone loved it. I was surprised that I like the cottage cheese in the recipe. I could only find 16 ounce boxes of lasagna noodles and I used all but 4 of them. I also boiled the noodles because they were not oven-ready. This recipe really fills the pan! Thanks NurseDi!
This was a truly delicious meal.  I have made other RR recipes, but this was by far the best!  My family really enjoyed this one.

I used butter rather than margarine.  These are tasty, but not quite like Paradise Bakery's molasses cookies. This is a keeper for us.  Have some of the dough in the freezer.  Will let y'all know if it works out when we get around to using it.
Very easy and very tasty! I especially liked that were no eggs in the batter so I could lick the beaters!!!! I didn't use a glaze on mine, I just dusted it with the powdered sugar. YUM!

Delicious and hearty chowder!  It's one of the best chowders I've ever had. The corn gave it a nice sort of sweetness.  I used green bell pepper in place of red and frozen corn for the 1 can of whole corn.  I'll definitely make this again.  Thanx for sharing it!
I made this with rotini and Diced Ham Dinner Starter (oamc) and it went together quick and easy. My oldest daughter really enjoyed this and had more than one helping! thanks for sharing this recipe!
I cut down the amount of bananas. The dressing was delicious! Used locally grown apples for this salad!

I didn't add the kidney beans so decreased the amount of tomatoes added. (I just used one large fresh tomato.)  Also took the other reviewer's suggestion and cut back on the bitters.  I'm not sure I would make this again as there are some other chilis I like better, but it was a good warming meal for a cold day.

This soup is really good.  I added a small can of corn and about a 1/2 a cup of chopped ham. All I had was fat free milk and half and half cream. So I used the cream instead of milk. Real easy to make. I love that.

This cake is so easy to put together.  I used a Pillsbury Golden Butter Recipe Moist Supreme yellow cake mix.  As some of the other reviewers suggested, I also doubled the glaze for the top of the cake.  The cake tastes incredible!  It is so moist and tender.  The glaze is buttery and very caramel flavored.  I love this cake and will be making it again soon.  Thanks, Nanita!

I made this with the chili pepper. It was a hearty vegetarian meal. 

This is the first time I have made a curry, but having eaten them at restaurants, I kept feeling something was amiss. Was it ginger? Peas? Cashew nuts? I'm not sure. It was spicy, but not sweet enough. Does it need more sugar? Maybe if I ever make it again I will try adding those, although that is my opinion though. If I made it again, I would probably add the above things.

Also, I think that more water could be added, maybe two to three inches above the veggie level instead of one inch below. Because there wasn't much sauce. Also, when I saved it for the next day, the sauce had nearly dried. So if I made this again, I would add more water.

Anyway, it was a pretty good vegetarian recipe. Thanks for sharing. :)
Greta recipe!! I made it lastnight for something good and simple to make for myself. I couldn't stop eating it!! Thanks for the recipe!!!

OMG this was just outstanding with the asparagus.  I didn't have champagne vinegar so used a lovely rice vinegar that went so well with the other flavors.  This made a lot of sauce but I can see using it on other steamed veggies.  Thanks so much EV.  I got the thumbs up from Dave which is always a good sign.

I was looking for something special to fix for a baby shower and found this recipe on the Cusine at Home website.  They turned out fabulous.  The cake has a nice texture and isn't too sweet.  It is perfectly complimented by the sweetness of the frosting.  I couldn't have been happier.

These were great! Took me awhile to finish because they made so many (at least 90) but it was easy and well worth it! Very popular at the party I served them at. Only thing I didn't like was how dry the insides were. Id rather have it more moist and soft. So next time I'll probably not dry them out as much. I had no trouble dipping them at all and they ended up perfectly round. I rolled the sugar mixture with a rolling pin and cut circles with a small cookie cutter. I also think that less shortening should be used so the chocolate doesn't get so greasy and is more hard. =) YUM!

Mmmm these are good.  However, I'm missing the full effect because I went to make the frosting and found that I had no powdered sugar!  Argh.  They weren't too bad without the frosting, but I thought they were missing something so I topped it with marshmallow fluff.  Sweet and gooey is oh so good!  Super easy to make as well.  Although I thought this was more of a cake than a brownie - not that I'm complaining!  :)

Wow, this is good!  I had several chicken breasts (maybe a pound and a half) that I had intended to fry, but didn't,  so I used this recipe instead.   Excellent.  I'll definitely make this again with a larger amount of chicken.

Great, this is one of the best and traditional recipes my mom makes EVER Y SINGLE DAY but as saffron is expensive outside the middle east i dont think people would acctuatll afford it. but as my mom gets her saffron cheaply from saudi arabia. its so cheap seriously there. it isnt very valuble in the middle east but it is outside like in europe where i live.

These ribs had an interesting taste from the Dr. Pepper. The meat was VERY tender. The only problem I had was that I used boneless ribs and they were a bit fatty. I am going to try this again with regular bone in ribs. I used minced garlic from a jar and about half a bottle of Bullseye BBQ sauce.  Quite good!!!

This was so good and so easy too! Everybody said the turkey was very tender. I cooked it on low for 5 hours, and then I got nervous because it was still looking pink so I turned it up to high for the rest of the cooking time which was 7 hours total. But it may just be my crockpot is not working like it used to. I used a 7 pound turkey and doubled the other ingredients for the gravy, except the worcestershire. I also added flour to thicken the gravy. And I know this sounds weird, but I had a lot of gravy left over, and my mom tasted some left in the crockpot and she said it tasted like cream of turkey soup. So she took it home, planned to add some rice and make soup! So overall, it was a nice easy to way to make a tender turkey! Thanks

These are fantastic cookies! I've made them many years for Christmas and was happy to see the recipe posted here. The brown butter frosting is so delicious and makes these cookies extra special. I like to garnish the tops with whole cashews before the frosting sets--not only is it attractive, it also gives a hint as to the cookie flavor. Thanks for posting this wonderful recipe!
These were good!  I added some garlic powder and oregano to the parmesan cheese topping.  Had enough left over to freeze for another time.  Thanks!
great

we had 4 power outages in the time this was baking yet despite that it still came out good. the only change i made was to use pecans instead of almonds and 1 tsp of almond extract. i baked this in a silicone pan and it came right out easily. very good with a cup of tea.

My family LOVED this rice.  I had never "baked" rice before (I usually cook it in a rice cooker) and it was surprisingly easy.  I was worried it was a bit too mushy (cooked it for about 5 minutes longer than required).  As with most rices, it firmed up a bit out of the oven with the cover off and a fork run through it.  Surprisingly, my kids love it, too - the jalapenos and onions were undetectable. Very good!

Wow! This was fabulous! All of the picky kids loved it without ever knowing it was fairly healthy. I didn't strain the rind but, yes, you'll know it's there so I probably would next time. We ate ours plain, but the picture has me dreaming of pairing this with fresh raspberries, blueberries or strawberries. Used two large organic lemons, I think they have a better flavor, and the result was a real lemony treat. Not any of that strange yellow coloring or fake tinny lemon flavor, but the real thing! Super easy in the microwave. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

These are good bars. I did make several changes--I used corn syrup, 1 cup of regualr oatmeal and 2 cups quick cooking oats, and only 1 cup of chocolate chips. I think I'll only use 1/2 tsp of salt next time; it's plenty salty. I baked it in a cookie sheet for about 18 min. which made nice, thin, chewy bars.

This was quick when I needed it! I used chicken and it went great. I used 2 cups milk and 1/2 cup fat free half and half. I used a mild salsa but next time I will add in some pickled jalapenos for my husband.  The whole family enjoyed this creamy dish. Thanks CrinV for another yummy recipe.

Roxygirl
My 14 yr old son renamed these dream bars! He is a cheesecake fanatic so I was thrilled to see this easy recipe! Thanks Bev!
I liked it, I had a moment of confusion as to when the egg white was suppose to go in but other wise it was a good recipe

I just made this cake to have something to serve company tonight, It was easy to make, the taste and texture are wonderful, I must have not greased the pan enough or  tried to turn it out too soon or something because it fell apart when I did. I made a box cake mix for the company and we will eat this delicious pile of cake!

we had this last night for dinner and it was great!  I think the sour cream and the green onions are what really set this apart from other tater tot topped casseroles.  Easy to prepare.  I had my older son make this before I returned home from younger son's baseball game. Served with a green salad for a complete, simple meal.  Thanks, Heather, for a recipe that will definitely be reapeated at our house!

Yum!!  This is easy, foolproof, and great.  I added a few drops of cherry extract, and melted the butter instead of softening (accidentally) and it worked out great!  I will try my special dark cocoa powder next time, and I bet it will be even better!  Thanks!

Excellent Recipe! I made this for a quick lunch today but had to use frozen spinach instead of fresh spinach! I loved the flavor and the peanuts on top gave it a nice crunch. I also added a bit more then a pinch of red pepper flakes , to give it some heat. I cut the servings to size to 2 and it was perfect. Thanks Rita!!!

I made these tonight as a sweet treat to take to work tomorrow.  I had all the makings on hand, and thought I should give it a go.  Only change I made was to use a round pan instead of a square one.  Found that the crumbs got a little too brown for me with the full 15 min bake time.   Other than that, no complaints.  Thanks for sharing.

All I can say is, WOW! I love this cake!! It is cheap and easy to make and it tastes soooo good. This is a keeper. Very chocolately, but not sickly. I am making this again on the weekend. Thanks so much for posting this recipe.
Excellent dip!  I followed the recipe without any changes, and my guests raved about the flavor.

DH always orders this at the local Spaghetti Factory. He is so happy that I found this recipe. He doesn't  have to wait hours in line to get this for dinner any more. This is a quick and easy, but high fat dish to prepare. (Who doesn't need a little fat to keep your hair shining.) This is so delicious you must try it at least once. I plan to make it again. Thank's Denver cook for posting.

Yum Jewelies, really enjoyed this one! I couldn't get fresh mango so used a 425g tin of mango, I slowly added the juice to the food processor and tasted along the way and found about half the juice from the tin was to my liking. I really enjoyed the fresh mint taste, however some not so keen on it might like to add smaller amounts and taste along the way.

My two dd's love soft and chewy cookies and I have such a hard time achieving that.  This recipe made them exactly has I had hoped, soft and chewy.  I was pretty worried at first after I added the milk - the dough was pretty runny.  I thought there was no way these were going to become cookies.  So I set it aside for about 10 minutes to just let it rest and it seemed to thicken up fine...still not your typical cookie dough, but good enough to plop on the cookie sheet.  I would highly recommend using a silpat or parchment to bake these on.  I can see where someone could have problems removing them from the cookie sheet w/out.  If they don't have these then grease your cookie sheet generously.  I used the maple flavor instead of vanilla and couldn't really taste it, but smelled it in the house.  This is a keeper.  Thanks Kittencal!

These ribs were okay.  My daughter and boyfriend thought they were good, but they were too sweet for my taste. I think cooking in sweet soda followed by a sweet barbeque sauce such as Sweet Baby Ray's was too much sweetness.  I think I would try a sauce that was spicer or smokier next time.  I was also really put off by the "scum" that formed while simmering the meat in the soda.  It was black and I had a hard time scraping it off before covering with the barbeque sauce. Having said that I think I would try this recipe again using ribs with the least amount of fat and a spicer/smokier BBQ sauce and maybe a clear soda.
These were very good! I doubled the complete recipe for 2 pounds carrots, I also used small baby carrots for this, real butter is a must, great recipe Mimi, thanks for sharing...Kitten:)

I made these for a party for teenagers and they seemed to enjoy them.  I used a mini tin, but had to shop at a specialty market for the wontons wrappers. I like that the filling can be changed for other combinations and will try that next.  They do need to be served immediately as they harden and dry out a little after sitting.
This was GREAT!!!! I seved it for a luncheon and everyone wanted the recipe. Thanks for posting.

The cake is very moist and flavorful, however we found the glaze to be a bit much.   Next time think I'll put the glaze on the inside and dust the exterior of the cake with powdered sugar.
Thanks for sharing.
Most excellent idea. I cooked some crumbled sausage and used that instead of ham and used pineapple tidbits rather than slices. This is one I'll make often when I want something quick and tasty!

I made this cake yesterday and found that it was very good, but not chocolately enough.  However, it was very moist and everyone enjoyed it.  Next time I will increase the cocoa as I liked the texture and the ease in making it.
This was very good, very easy. Thanks for a great recipe.
these were wonderful! i used half brown sugar just because i love brown sugar and cinnamon together, but i will definitely make these again. THANKS!

My family and I loved this recipe.  Since my green and red peppers were jumbo I used two of each.  The recipe turned out great!  I did use hot sausage instead which gave it a nice kick.
Thanks CulinaryQueen

Sorry--I am a southern gal, so I was excited to try these green beans, but these just didn't do it for us.  The seasoning salt gave the beans a taste we just didn't like, and the parmesan doesn't taste right.  I won't be making these again.

Oh man, this was good!  Just what I was looking for.  I grew up in WI, and though haven't lived there for quite a few years, the taste of a good brat is never something you stop craving.  This time I was looking for something different from the usual brat recipe...you know...boil in beer, grill, put on bun with sauerkraut and a good mustard.  This soup fit the bill perfectly!  I made very minor changes, such as adding more cheese and bratwurst.  I used 2 1/2 cups of sharp cheddar, then added a couple of slices processed cheese to thicken it a bit.  I used a hand blender to blend the whole thing right there in the pot, and I'm glad I did since I like a thick and completely pureed soup.  I did 5 brats instead of 3, and you could easily add even more.  I'll slice the brats again next time, but then quarter each slice for smaller pieces and a better presentation.  I topped each with a very small handful of cheese in the center of each bowl.  My husband liked it, but he thought the beer I used was a bit too strong.  I used a Sam Adams lager, but his suggestion would be to use something even lighter, such as a blonde.  I had a bowl for lunch yesterday, and it was even better the next day.  Was it my imagination or did it thicken up a bit more?  I'm planning on making this when my parents come for a visit - they'll love it!  Thanks for sharing this great recipe.

This rice has so many nice flavors and just a bit of spicy hot. I didnt have turmeric so I substituted ground mustard and used 8 ounces of brown rice. The cinnamon is perfect to pull all the flavors together! Thank you LikeItLoveIt for a wonderful side dish. I served this with Braised Pork in Soy Sauce.
This was a good bread, but it wasn't pumpernickel. I guess maybe I'm looking for something darker, I'm not sure.

This was very simple recipe - I "cheated" a little and made seasoned chicken in the crockpot in advance, so that probably made it even easier. These were very tasty, spicy without being HOT. This will definitely go into my normal dinner rotation. Thanks!

Oct. 25- OMGosh! I don't think I have ever liked pumpkin any better! These are MAGNIFICENT!!! I am so glad you shared this recipe! They are a must have for my Thanksgiving Holiday!!! These are going to work with me tomorrow and I am already proud before they get there!!! Thank you jewelz4Jesus!!! *** Edited to add- This is my second time making these cookies. I got 41 this time and 42 the last time. Since the recipe says 5 dozen , I guess I am making them too big, but they are not big at all. I used rounded teaspoons. When you drop them, they stay pretty much true to the size.  Two tips- #1. I don't suggest cooking these on your stone. The bottoms did much better on my pan cookie sheet. #2.  Put the icing on low heat while topping your cookies. The first time I made them the icing got hard before I finished (see pic). This time on low heat, it did great for some nice tops.I also used my melon baller this time and they are came out the same perfect size.

I can see why this recipe has so many 5 star ratings on it! Delcious and moist and full of chocolate flavor! I baked mine in a 13x9 pan and iced with Chocolate Frosting and was a match made in heaven! Thanks for the recipe Marg!

VERY VERY good.  Super easy, great tasting, what more can one ask for.
This is going to be a monthly sandwich in our house. Congrats on winning the football pool!!

I made this as a replacement for storebought caramel ice cream topping in another recipe -- sooo good! Two hours cooking time on low (simmer on my oven dial) produced a nice thick sauce, and I didn't have any trouble with scorching or curdling. The two hours seemed to go by pretty quick, too, because I just put the caramel on to cook while I was cooking other things. I was already at the stove, so it was easy to remember to stir the caramel sauce. Thanks for posting!
Yummy!! I made mine with endive. I love my greens! :)

It is great for a quick lunch when you have leftover chicken.  The lemon juice adds a nice touch.  I thought it could use some onions, so I added some.  Thanx for sharing.  I'll have this for lunch again when I have leftover chicken.

What a simple and tasty little treat to have around.  My grandkids are going to love this.  I used all cashews since that is our favorite, but other than that made as is.  Love the combination of sweet and salty.  Thanks
I used to have this at the Spagetti Factory, and loved it then.....great recipe.

This was so easy to make, incredibly cute and really tasted great depite having very littkle in the way of seasonings.  I also used a lot less whipped cream cheese for the "icing" step than called for, as I didn't think it was needed.

With the potato, this was a bit more work than my other facaccia recipe, but the end result was very good.  I had a bit of a problem with the center not being really done when the edges were quite done.  I am wondering if I should remove the bread from the oven while it preheats up to temperature; or maybe I need to make sure my pan underneath has boiling water in it.  The flavor combination of the rosemary, olives, and parmesan was excellent.

Delicious and very good for you salad. Loaded with vitamins and lean protein. We loved it. I substituted iceberg lettuce with finely shredded cabbage and used dried cilantro and red wine vinegar in the dressing. The dressing came out awesome !! Will make it again.Thank you!
Great tasting noodle dish, very aromatic and spicy. Really enjoyed it. Thank you.
good old-fashioned brownie recipe

Also, I did'nt have whole-wheat flour so I used 1/2 cake flour 1/4 oats and 1/4 digestive bran and they came out great. A really great recipe and definitely one I'll use again. Thanx

I may be biased because I love caramel apple anything, but these were lovely! The phyllo wasn't nearly as difficult to work with as I was expecting, which was nice. I only had small apples, so I used three Gala and three Golden Delicious. I used The Best Caramel Sauce in the World for the caramel sauce. I drizzled the baked pastries with a little honey to moisten them (I didn't have any more caramel sauce left or I would have used that). I didn't have any ice cream on hand, but I definitely think these would be wonderful with ice cream (maybe even with ice cream and a bit of cider sauce). Oh, and just so you know, the rolls were pretty big (I would probably go so far as to say that each roll would serve two people), so the nutrition facts per serving are most likely not nearly as scary as they look here. Great recipe, thanks for posting!
Yum!  This was just the recipe I was looking for.  Sweet, easy, and loaded with the taste of Fall.  Thanks for posting!

I scaled this down so that I used 5 eggs, and that was a good amount for 1 adult, a 2 year old and a 5 year old. Cooktime in a convection oven was 30 minutes.

Good meal choice!

Quite good! Family liked it a lot, thanks for the recipe

this recipe just did not turn out as good as it seemed to for others. it seemed a little bitter, it tasted a lot like the sushi that we make and would have been good inside sushi but i did not care for it much as a dip. but it was a fun alternative to try. i always like something new, and i'm glad it seemed to turn out better for others. maybe i did something wrong. thanks anyway
Excellent use of the butternut squash. Kind of like a sweet potato. Thanks!

Made this using my one small eggplant plucked from a volunteer plant that happened to come up in my back yard - a perfect size for 2 people. Another fabulous recipe from NurseDi...these were so good that I could not believe how simple they were.  They were a big hit with the family.

I am probably the biggest pumpkin lover out there ... pies, cakes, muffins, breads, coffee creamers, etc.  My sister brought me 5 of these cookies & let me tell you there is nothing like it in the world!  I know I polished off 3 before she left the driveway!  It was by far the best cookie I've EVER had!   THUMBS UP ... WAY UP

This is excellent.  I used half the butter as salmon is oily enough.  But otherwise I followed the recipe.  Thanks for the posting

(I'm adding a star to my rating as I figured out it's a matter of taste...Everyone who loves dark chocolate loved this and everyone who doesn't love dark chocolate thought it had a bitter taste.) Really, you won't do any better than this recipe, really top notch for a number of reasons. These are what people say, easy to roll out, without the chilling time as well. The taste and texture is great, buttery, light and crisp without any crumbling or hardness issues. I like to add vanilla bean seeds scraped out of the bean to these, makes it that much more special. Sometimes I ice them with rose water flavored icing, which is just gilding the lily, so good. If you can, try to find a round zippered plastic pastry rolling bag, available at kitchen stores and sites. These are great, keeps all the mess inside and keeps the sticking of dough to a very minimum with so little flour. If all else fails and you are just having a difficult baking day, try rolling out your dough directly on to a very lightly floured baking sheet and cutting the cookies right on it. When done cutting, just remove the scraps off the sheet and you are good to go. Thank you, Crawfish, this really is one of the best recipes around here.

This is a good recipe and results in a very tasty muffin. I too added cinnamon into the batter and skipped nutmeg (personal preference). However, I found that a few changes would serve very well - if you like sweet muffins I would suggest adding an additional 3-4 tbsp of sugar (I added 2 tbsp of brown sugar and it still wasn't quite enough). My muffins were on the dry side and the tops were almost burnt. I would recommend checking on the muffins in about 13 min and covering the top with foil if necessary to prevent excessive browning. Also, test for doneness at about 18 min. A final thought is not quite a suggestion but just information - this recipe makes less than 12 muffins unless your muffin tin is pretty small. I got 6 large ones.

Beach Girl, you got in first with a real winner. I have been making this awesome recipe since the early 1980s (it is the only mayo my family and friends will eat). But my process is slightly different. I always double the ingredients. I put the eggs, hot English dry mustard, salt and vinegar in a food processor and buzz them for 30 seconds. With the processor motor still running, I then slowly add the oil in a fine stream. If you add the oil too fast the whole mixture will curdle. By the way, you can make it with canola, sunflower, vegetable or olive oil...but never use peanut oil. I learned that the hard way...Â?and it tastes terrible. Also, don't worry too much about the raw egg. I have served this recipe to many ages...from 2 to 96...with no ill effects. But I am very careful about my source of eggs. And a last comment, I think a great aspect of this mayo is the lack of sugar. If you must add sugar, add no more than 1 teaspoon per egg used.
