I got ahead of myself mixing the cake mix with the ingredients asked for on my box (1 1/3 cups water, 1/2 cup butter, 3 large eggs), before I realized what I was doing, but I figured it was probably not a problem.  I would definitely make this again! (Picked this one for Zaar Tag and I'm glad I did.)

This recipe is so easy to make and everybody loved it! I will make a little extra "gravy" next time because my husband is a sopper. (he loves to sop) This is a great meal that is filling and not bad for you. I will also try to use the low sodium soup next time to see how that turns out. Clean up was a breeze.

Excellent recipe. Easy enough that my 14 year old son made it without supervision. He doubled the whole thing, but only used 3 cups of hot water at the end because it seemed the pan was very full [it was a 13x9 pan]. However, after baking, the "gravy" was very thick, so I think 4 cups of water will be needed. We are definitely having this again...and again...and again.
By the way, we used one 53g envelope of chicken gravy in the mix, and one 53g envelope of beef gravy at the end.
I followed another cook's lead and added garlic. We also put in bell peppers and onions. Delicious! My oh-so-picky son actually liked them too. Definite keeper!

This is SO good!  I made mine with the Soy Vay Teriyaki Sauce.  On top of that I put some sliced up lettuce, some strips of chicken (that I had coated in some flour and cornmeal before quick frying) and some grated marble cheese.  I didn't spray or grease my tortilla.  Instead, I put some cornmeal on my pizza stone and plunked the tortilla on top of it.  No sticking at all!  I LOVED the edges of the tortilla!  They got all crispy and flaky!  Lovely.  I will use this as a great way to have a quick lunch for myself.  Thanks!
I used sweet potatoes instead of regular white.  It was good, but I also only got 6 instead of 12.  There was a bit too much nutmeg for my taste.

What a great recipe.  I made some changes and could not believe just how delicious they were!  The changes I made were: I added 1/4 c more sugar, added a teaspoon of cinnamon, and put the whole stick of butter in the mix rather than just 1/3 c.  They were moist and yummy and made 12 sweet cinnamon-y muffins. They were gone in about 10 minutes--everyone loved them. Thanks Charlotte!

Hmmm...We thought it was OK - had to add quite a bit of additional salt at the table, in addition to freshly grated Parmesan, to bring out flavor. I think next time we'll try the Rachel Ray Vodka sauce that uses chicken broth to bring up the flavor abit. This would be a really fine sauce for folks on low-sodium diet - I'll be keeping it to serve when some of our friends who watch their salt come over.  Thank you for posting, Heather Feather!

I made this for my four year old daughter.  She LOVED them!  Talk about easy and having all the ingredients on hand already.  These WILL BE made again.  Will have to tweek, my husband is allergic to chicken...should work just fine with beef and cream of mushroom.  It was very creamy and soft...we have three left would love to eat them NOW!!! Great job and thanks for posting it...makes dinner easier now!
I don't really like this recipe from the freezer so instead I make up little baggies of the dry ingredients then when I want rice I just take one bag and add the Water and nuke it. I love the flavor!

I made this for my granddaughter's birthday party:  50 people, so I doubled the recipe; however, since I had to transport it 20 miles to the site, I decided to keep the ingredients separate. I don't recommend doing that.  The jello/sugar/water congealed in the 6 degree weather (in the trunk). A wisk solved the problem, but had I added pineapple juice to that mixture initially, I think I'd have successfully kept it from congealing.  The punch is still superb; and I think it could be tweaked:  how about grape jello/grape juice? Or orange? It would be fun to play around with it and see what the different flavors are like.  This is definitely a keeper! Thanks!
Wilmom
2 "Yums" up! The sun dried tomatoes added moistness and flavor.  I broke this up into two balls and baked it that way. Loved it!

Marinated over Fri. night,and made for Sat. night supper last night. We really enjoyed this one.A good piece of rare beef is one of my favorite things.I used fresh rosemary,thyme,and  parsley. Thanks for sharing a great recipe ElaineAnn, we really enjoyed it.I served it with a green garden salad,beer-dill seared carrots,garlic mashed potatoes,and French bread.What a great meal.(The overnight wait time was hard! Each time I opened my fridge and saw it in a plastic-wrap covered dish, my mouth would start to water in anticipation!)

These bars are really good. I just pulled the pan out of the oven and had to cut into them! I just couldn't wait until they cooled! I did make a few changes (I know.... can ANYONE just follow a recipe??!) I cut the molasses back to 1 Tsp., Didn't add the nuts because I didn't have any and I used 1/2 butterscotch and 1/2 Milk chocolate chips. YUM!!!  I baked them in a 15x10 pan and got a little nervous when I checked on them because they really rose and almost rose right over the sides of my pan. But, it turned out ok and they ended up being a nice, chewy, thin bar. Thank You for sharing!

Hi , 

I made this as a pre  appetizer,appetizer (no not a mistake..)I actually made two appetizers. I think I am going to have to start cooking from my Sonoma diet cookbook again if this keeps up. I cut down on the recipe size as there were only 3 of us. It is awesome. 5 stars all the way. 


P.S. Sorry no picture, the batteries for my camera are in the charger.
Leanne

These were great.  I made them last night for a Super Bowl party and everybody loved them. I could not get the small pepperidge farm rolls and had to use a significantly larger (apparently) dinner roll, because one recipe filled only 12.  Fortunately, I had doubled the recipe or there might have been violent contests of might to determine who got to have them.  As it was, when I brought the second batch out of the oven I had to fight back the hordes to simply get the sliders on a serving plate!

I'm an addict when it comes to a combination of chocolate & orange flavors, so it was very likely that this recipe actually reached out to me! Whatever the case, the resulting 'fantasy bars' were OUTSTANDING! I served them at one of the small group meetings I attend, foolishly expecting to have a couple to take back home with me! Well, I was glad I took 5-6 copies of the recipe, because EVERYONE was asking for the recipe! After I returned home, I made another batch JUST FOR ME [well, mostly just for me]! This is definitely a recipe I'll make again & again! Many thanks!

This is truly comfort in a bowl!  I made a few adjustments because I didn't have chicken pieces. (I would highly recommend using them as they add so much flavor to the broth.)  I used 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts and cut them in bite-size pieces.  I followed the directions exactly as written but added 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp red pepper flakes with the water.  The chicken was tender, the broth was awesome and the noodles soaked up all the wonderful flavors.  Thank you for a great, comforting recipe, Debbie!  I will be making this again!

This was very easy to prepare and tasted pretty good. I thought the poaching liquid which I used as a sauce over the fish when serving was a little too rich tasting and didn't compliment the delicate taste of the fish. I probably won't make this again.

I made these for a SuperBowl party and they were a big hit.  I used Yves veggie ground round instead of the hamburger to vegetarian-ize the recipe.  I also followed other reviewers tips and pre-baked the wonton wrappers (brushed with oil) for 2-3 minutes for an extra crispy shell.  Thanks for posting -I will be making these again.
I added lemon pepper Mrs. Dash and tossed in a few bay leaves to the boiling sauce. Once I was done with the fish I chopped up a few white Mushrooms and let it simmer for five minutes. FANTASTIC!!!

Easy enough recipe. We will likely not make this again. I used an entire can, probably about 4 tbsp of red curry paste and we still found it to be incredibly bland. I think IF I ever used this recipe again, I wouldn't slow cook it. It would be a very easy stovetop recipe. It was just watery and bland. I followed the recipe exactly except for the cut of meat, I used stewing beef instead.
Very good!
I love this recipe!  To make it a good WeightWatchers dessert, I substitute sugar-free vanilla pudding mix, and fat-free cool whip instead of whipping cream.  It is a very satisfying dessert.

This was the first time I had cooked with Tempeh and I love Japanese food so this recipe caught my eye. I liked the taste/textures of the dish a lot. I substituted white cabbage for cauliflower, left out the celery and used cornflour instead of arrowroot. Although it says a meal in one pan I found I used a few as ingredients had to be cooked in batches. Instructions got a little sketchy towards the end, when to add the broccoli,carrot,cauliflower back to the dish? Overall good flavours and good for you.

These tasted almost like candied sweet potatoes, but with a little hint of spice. They were fairly easy and cooked in about 45 minutes in my oven. I cut mine smaller than the recipe instructed, however.

I found it took an interminable time for the potatoes to get soft.  I usually count on 20 minutes of simmer time for potatoes (not 10 as this recipe says), but ended up going for more than 30 minutes. I'm not sure, but I think that frying the potatoes first may have prevented water from penetrating them properly, so if I do this recipe again, I'll saute the onions and spices, then add the stock and lentils and potatoes together. 

Otherwise, this is good, stick-to-your ribs food, and makes great leftovers!

This is now part of our 'make repeatedly' week night list. Even my daughter liked it! I added taco seasoning to the ground beef, and topped with salsa instead of plain tomatos. Oh, and let it stand a bit longer than mentioned for the potatoes to firm up. Thanks for the keeper!

I made this recipe in my crockpot and  it was very good, tender and shredded easily but there wasn't a whole lot of flavor to it. I did not marinade - just threw everything in the crock. If I make this again, I will try that and see if it ends up with more flavor.
Such an easy and tasty way to prepare escarole.  I added a bit more garlic, but just a hint of red pepper.
I had prosciutto left over from another recipe and used this. I think the lemon flavor made it. I can't stand peas so I cut asparagus cut in 1" pieces and it was great! Thank you!

Chef_Eurkle, keep experimenting, cause you are good at it. This recipe gives spaghetti a whole new twist with just enough heat to keep us coming back for another bite. I used recipe #22782 for the sauce. DH loved it and so did I. Thanks for the recipe and keep them coming!
I love this recipe! I'm glad to be able to feed my husband eggplant (most dishes have tomatoes, which he can't have). It's really very easy. Thanks so much!
Love popcorn and this was good stuff. Alittle on the hot side but I enjoyed it. Also had a nice cheesey taste.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.
Absolutely wonderful! DH gobble this up and insists we have it again soon-thanks for posting, we are always looking for more interesting ways to get our veggies

Salt, salt, and more salt and I found it very dry.  Made this a few days ago but, Donna,  gotta give this another try after substituting all those package mixes with fresh onions and 2 jars of gravy plus 1 of water.

Thanks for sharing this and I do promise to try it again.
This recipe sounded great, but the orange flavor was just overwhelming and the orange juice made the oatmeal taste sour.  I'll try it again, but with much less juice and more water.

Miss Annie, this was delicious!  In place of the ham hock, I used about 1/4 package of bacon, frying it well before adding (crumbled) to the pot. I didn't have minced garlic, so I substituted 1/2 teaspoon of garlic powder.  I served the soup with homemade bread.  This really hit the spot on a cold snowy night! Thank you!

We eat at Johnny Carino's a lot and this is similar to their Bacon Spezzie.  Great!  We added a few sun dried tomatoes one time and roasted red peppers another, and a little cayenne for heat.  Lots of leftovers though, as the kids didn't like it.

After I started preparing I realized that we were out of pecans, so I used walnuts instead. It came out pretty well, and worked even though I used only a minimum of olive oil for the skillet. Nice substitute, and I'll definately make this again.
I tried this for a luncheon I had the other day and it was highly complimented. Thanks for the dish.
This was very very good! I did add Tabasco and cajun seasoning and it gave us just enough kick. This is really a great appetizer and good for you too! Thanks for sharing, lazyme.

Delicious! I was looking for a cheesecake type dessert that used only 1 package of cream cheese. I'm so glad I chose this one! We all loved it. We ate them plain the first night, after a meal of chicken soup and Recipe #96447. The second day I had prepared Recipe #15525 for another reason but the kids wanted to try some on the leftover cheesecake cookies. They loved them that way too. This recipe is very easy to fix and I know I'll be making it again. Thanks for sharing, Bev!
Wonderful hot dog sauce...my BF thought this was just great. Will make again. Thanks!
AWESOME sauce!! we all loved it. Thanks bunches for the recipe!

Wonderful, wonderful! Thank you Fiona!!! (I love that) I live in Michigan where there is a foot of snow on top of my grill. My guy wanted steak for Valentines Day, so I had no choice but to cook it in the oven. I wasn't sure it would be as juicy like it is from the grill, but WOW....it was a very delicious steak. Good luck with hubbie..and thanks for posting

My husband and I really liked this.  It was easy to make.  I followed the recipe but added more noodles.  I thought the soup was spicy enough as is.  The only negative thing I have to say is that the soup is very salty mainly due to the fish sauce.  Next time I plan on trying it with low sodium chicken broth.  Thanks for the recipe Sue L.
Chocolate and orange, the best combination! I made this for my DS, so I only got to taste a small end from it, this got 5 stars from everyone, thanks BK!...Kitten:)
I used 3 torpedo rolls cut into 6 small pieces each... worked excellent

Wonderful balance of flavors. 
I used a cinnamon raisin bread which also works great. Love it!

Believe it or not I had to go out & buy myself a springform pan [never used one before!], & it was well worth it! This recipe was made for a potluck & WAS ALMOST ALL GONE before everyone was even through with the main dishes!! As usual, I took along a handful of copies of the recipe & had to promise others I'd get them a copy, too! Got to admit that I doubled the lemon zest & did not use the grapes, but everything else was per the recipe directions!
Many thanks for posting this great recipe!

This was great!  Very easy to make and very tasty.  I used left over ham cut up and only used a total of 4 cups of water as I like a thicker soup. Also, I didn't use salt as others noted it was salty, but I wish I would have put in salt as I didn't find it salty as all.

Here's a very nice, creamy dip that's great with a lot of things! I served it for a group I helped host, & everything was getting dipped into it ~ fruit or all kinds, pretzels, veggies(!) or all kinds, crackers, the works! I'd personally stick with fruits, but there's no accounting for anyone else's taste!! Thanks for sharing!
Very nice cookie it went extremely well with the royal icing recipe.  My kids are enjoying it as I type.  Thank you!
Great recipe. I cut the recipe down to use on ham slices and it turns out great. Thanks for the recipe.

Fantastic recipe.  It is very easy to make.  I took other cook's advice and added another 2 Tablespoons butter and 3/4 cup crushed graham crackers to the crust mix.  The only problem I had was getting it out of the pan, even though I greased the pan first.  Otherwise, excellent.

Now, this is a real chocolate cake!  There is no question when diving into a slice of this dense, moist and deeply flavorful cake that you are eating ~ chocolate!  Easy to follow instructions for the perfect 2 layer chocolate heaven!   I used recipe #89207 using the most cocoa powder (3/4 cup) for the darkest and deepest chocolate frosting.  Thank you, Marg, for a wonderful, chocolate experience : )

I made this for my MIL's birthday and it is definitely CHOCOLATE cake. I followed the recipe exactly and thought this was easy, just as easy as using a box mix. Two things I would have changed - I covered this cake in chocolate buttercream icing and it was so rich no one could eat more than a sliver at a time. We thought it tasted very good, just too rich for more than a bite at a time. I joked it was definitely "Death by Chocolate" with the combo of the cake and chocolate buttercream icing. The second thing I would have changed, also related to the icing - the cake did not hold up to a thick buttercream (was planning to pipe some decorations but used all the icing just trying to "glue" the crumbling cake back together!). When I make this again, I will use a "lighter" icing or glaze that won't destroy the cake or create an overwhelmingingly rich dessert.
I thought these were some good potatoes.  The potato and sauce ratio was perfect.  Definately will make again.

What a yummy wintery treat! I used more sweet potato than white (3 to 1) because we love them so much and they're so healthy. I couldn't get a decent parsnip so had to skip that this time. I think any veggies would be great in here, I may add some stewed tomato next time! We just love soups and this was a winner, easy and hearty, Kudos from the neighbor I shared this with too!

I had about 1/2 leftover large eggplant and prepared it using this recipe.  It was absolutely fantastic!  I even took it out of the oven and let it set for about 10 minutes and it never got soggy!  I grated my own parmesan and used regular mayo as that is what I had.  The outside was crunchy and the interior was "melt in your mouth."  It was easy, to boot!  I'll be buying eggplant more often!
I love roasted veggies and this was great!  A very forgiving recipe as I did not have zucchini & summer squash but subbed carrots and celery.  Turned out perfectly delicious!  Thanks!
Simple and very good
This was excellent. And easy to put together. I used fresh spinach and doubled the cheese. Thanks for such a great recipe.

I LOVE this salad! I keep coming back to it for a quick and easy lunch. It is simply delicious. The flavors are so delicate and refreshing. I've tried to add asparagus in the past but it just throws everything off. Now I make it according to the recipe (minus the olives as I don't like them) and keep it in the fridge to pick at whenever I feel like it! (It never lasts long!!) This is a definite favorite!!

Outstanding! I could not find Tiger sauce, so I used Sweet Chilli sauce instead (MAE PLOY)
No leftovers what so everâ€¦the roast disappeared.

Baby Kato, I really like the combination of chocolate and orange in this dessert! I used macadamia nuts and bittersweet Belgian chocolate. The orange flavor really comes through. This is a rich bar--and rich is what we like. The bar is very fudgey in the middle, not cakelike, which is another plus. This really hit the spot for our sweet tooth tonight. Thanks so much!

This recipe is so close to the one that I received with my Spaetzle maker that I got from a German Store. The only thing different is that mine uses 1/2 cup water and 1/2 cup milk. My spaetzle maker is not a potato ricer. It has large holes. (like little dumplings). DH and I like them fried in butter. We had them cooked this way at a German resturant once and it's the only way we like to eat them now!  Thanks, Melody for posting.
Not like this needs another rating, but this was awesome. It was a very easy dish to serve with my shrimp spring rolls, which took some time. I'll be making this again. Thanks!!

I was in the mood for a good hamburger,and I chose this one.I'm so glad I did.:)I followed the recipe as written except I pan-fried them.The burger was so moist and flavorful,I topped mine with lettuce,tomato,and mayo.My SO thought it could have used some onion,but I really enjoyed it the way it was.I served Recipe#34011 as a side.This will be made again,thank you so much for posting."Keep Smiling :)"
This was a hit last night with my husband! Thank you for sharing!
my comment is as follows:I liked the cake but it was very large and Heavy. I thought it would have been light since the batter was. It did not rise

very good.  although i did have to add additional spices, more garlic, small amount of cumin and some red pepper to spice it up a little.  I will be using this again as I always have these ingredients handy!  thanks

I was really wondering about that jalapeno, worried that the dressing would end up too spicy for the wussy tastebuds at dinner, but it really did not. I used something more than 1/2 a head of romaine and that was enough for the two of us, but I went ahead and made the entire dressing recipe, used all the pumpkin seeds and an entire avocado. I forgot the tortilla chips, even though they were sitting right there in the kitchen. Even without them, the salad was excellent. I'm thinking this dressing might be nice drizzled over cold chicken in a sandwich.

Very good, and the ingredients will be found in cupboard, for sure. There's always sugar, honey and some pecans. No dairy needed here. Keeps well in room temperature for next time and does not harden up, if not cooked any longer than needed.

This is essentially the recipe I use from the same source. Sounds like she was making a little smaller dish on the Today show! It is sooo good and not very difficult once you get the knack of filling the manicotti! The house smells wonderful while it is cooking. Thanks for posting this recipe.
Very good easy to make my husband love them!!!Thank you very good recipe to have handy

This was outstanding!  It was so easy, great for a week-night, but also made a wonderful presentation so it could be prepared for guests.  I omitted the salt but added a bit of coarse ground pepper.  I also used bottled lemon juice, as that was all I had on hand.  Definitely a keeper at our home!
Really yummy! A little different from other tetrazinni recipes. I added a half cup or so of chicken broth and used all mozzerella cheese and it was superb! Thanks. Hubby says this is a keeper!

i don't even like slaw, and i went back for seconds on this one!  i added a little splash of white vinegar and some salt and pepper to the dressing, and i used bacon instead of ham, but that's all i did differently.  THIS IS SUCH AN INCREDIBLE DISH!  and it's so easy!  i'll be making this a lot - thanks so much for posting.

OK, it's about time to admit it! Although I've never been any kind of fan of mushrooms [other than raw], I'm at least able to manage them cooked! This is a 5-STAR rating because the bean dish as a whole has a great taste [& I suppose...perhaps...it might be...maybe...just a little, because of the mushrooms!!! There, I said it!]. Thanks for posting it, & for twisting my arm ~ I'll be making it again!
This was very good and tender, and extremely easy. The only thing I will change next time is to cut the amount of thyme. It was a little too much for us. Thanks.
This was really good, however, my family thought it was too "sweet-tasting" because of the vanilla. I'll probably make it without the vanilla next time. Thanks.

Yummy.  I, too, added a whole stick of butter and an additional 1/4 C sugar and they came out light and fluffy and delicious.  
Thanks for sharing.
Thanks for solving dinner! Easy and delicious.

I chose this recipe to serve on Shrove Tuesday earlier this month, and we enjoyed it very much. A few things I changed: I caramelized the onions, used cheddar cheese that I shredded in place of Velveeta, 1/2 lb sausage instead of 1 lb., and I added 1/2 packet of frozen spinach, thawed.  I didn't quite get my head around heating only on side of the crepe and did give each a flip in the skillet, and I didn't melt the cheese, rather added each ingredient separately onto the crepes and rolled them up.  I also didn't get the chill part, so I didn't chill but popped them into the oven right away and baked about 20 minutes at 375F. I didn't bake uncovered either, but added sour cream at the table. I came up with about 10 large crepes, as opposed to 20 smaller ones.  These were very tasty, and I'm glad I had this recipe as my guideline.

Holy Fabulous!  Thank you for sharing such a flavorful and simple recipe!  With my world with two small kids and carpools galore, I needed something quick.  The only thing I omitted was the red pepper flakes because I knew my kids wouldn't touch it if it was too spicy.  This one's a keeper!  Thank you!  LA :-)
it was outstanding thanks for the recipe! it was so moist mmmmm! thanks!

This got very good reviews from the family.  I too got the recipe from Publix.  I didn't have the Pesto so made it using #8535.  So easy and so very good.  That same Publix flyer called for Tilapia w/Lemon Butter Sauce.  All in all a delicious dinner.  Thanks Mandabears.
This is the greatest pita ever! Made it with some Falafel tonight, and it went over great with everyone!  A really fabulous recipe, just perfect! Thanks for sharing!

This was made for guests tonight and I was informed at the dinner table that the 14 yr old son will not eat green beans. He took the courtesy spoon full and ended up scarfing 3 helpings!! If that isn't a testament to this recipe, I don't know what is. These are wonderful. I have often added mushrooms to peas or green beans but, wow, the chicken stock really adds a flavor punch. This is a keeper Thanks so much Lazyme.

These were terrific.  I followed reviewers' suggestions and added 1/4 c. sugar and an entire stick of butter, as well as 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon to the batter.  Amazing.  I'm tripling this recipe next time.  Thanks so much for posting!

After seeing that it was made from condensed soup I was a little skeptical about this one. I tried it with 1/2 Tbsp onion powder instead of minced onion because we were out. It did have a taste similar to campbells soup but it was quickly removed with a three second squirt of Heinz Ketchup. I am curious to see if a store brand soup would be the same- they seem to be a lttle more "tomato-ey"
These were okay. I thought the ginger flavor was too strong and the marmalade flavor was too sweet. DH thought they were okay too. Next time I'll lessen the ginger and marmalade.

Delicious and fast!  I used grape seed oil and a caste iron pan for frying. Also, I didn't have milk powder, and I decided to add some flax to the mix and they still came out  yummy.  Mine were more irregular and more brown than in the photos.  I will definitely use this recipe again!

I had to make this right after watching Giada make it on the Food Network. I wasn't disappointed except that I didn't have any spinach on hand so had to go spinach-less. My husband thought that was a good thing but next time it will have it in it and we shall see! I also didn't have pancetta so I cooked up some crisp bacon instead. I also wondered if mushrooms would add a nice flavour.
Very good and glad you posted it.

OMG by BF thought these were so good he ate 7 of them an almost exploded, he said this is a definate do again! I thought they were very yummy and easy to make but a little salty so next time i'll use low sodium soup, also I used two cans of soup, 1 can of mixed veg and cooked the biscuits for 4 muniutes first without any filling ( I was afriad the bottom would go all mushy) and then just pushed them back again with the round side of the spoon. Outstanding recipe and so good!!
I made this recipe except substituted strawberry yogurt and jello and it was absolutely delightful! It's a great light dessert, and it doesn't taste low-cal!

I made this as a "dump recipe" to freeze for later.  I made a half recipe of this for about 1 pound of top sirloin steak.  I did not add meat tenderizer because I wasn't sure what the result would be with frozen meat.  After defrosting, we grilled the steak, then boiled the remaining marinade to serve as a sauce over the steak.  Great flavor; makes a nice steak sauce.

This was very nice.  Mine didn't turn out as creamy as the photo shows but had a very nice flavor.  I used cream cheese with onion and chives, which I happen to love, so I don't think that compromised the recipe at all.  Thanks for a keeper.

perfect!!  My mom used to make this all the time in the fall and winter seasons.  My 3 yr old helped make it and thinks its delicious!  *One tip* use the small can of evap milk (5oz) I didn't catch that until the  12oz can was poured into the pumpkin mix..saved it by pouring the extra off before it was stirred in! Smooth and rich! I like mine warmeed a bit.  Its great with coffee.

This recipe uses far too much broth, diluting the flavor of a good bottle of wine. The Thyme is overpowering, especially since the wine taste is weakened by too much broth. Texture and color were fine. Try one can less of the broth, half the thyme.

These are extremely good hot out of the oven...soft and sugary with a nice spice flavor and they melt in your mouth. You can't stop eating them! After they cooled they became firmer and chewy. I liked reheating them in the microwave. If you bake them for a shorter time they will probably stay softer. I scaled down the recipe to 20 servings and it made 44 cookies scooped out with my half tablespoon. I used butter crisco and rounded off the odd measurements. I found the dough to be soft but easy to roll in the sugar. I baked mine for 12 minutes. Thanks for this yummy recipe! Made for 1-2-3 hit wonders.

My husband and I about starved just smelling this cooking.  It was easy and quick and juicy.  We added potatoes and carrots in with the roast, they turned out delicious as well.  My 11 mo old couldn't get enough of the veggies!

This was incredibly easy to make, I was able to throw this together within ten minutes of walking in the house from work as I had all the ingredients already.  Okay, just two substitutions:  I used lemon juice instead of lime, and I used a local white cheese instead of queso fresco (tzfatit cheese, for any Israelis wanting to make this).  I whipped up the dressing with my hand blender.  Bing, bang, supper!  Thanks, now I just have to convince myself that since it's salad, it's diet food, right?????
great recipe!soft, not dry and easy to make. thanks for posting, now i can get rid of my old pita bread recipe.
I made these into mini cupcakes and they were delicious! The glaze has a really fresh flavor. I'll make these again!
sorry, I didn't really like this recipe. I used four cups water, four cups chicken broth so maybe that ruined it. Thank you.

These are really good!  I wasn't sure about the crust at first b/c it seemed so crumbly and didn't want to stick together.  It also didn't really brown much in the oven and came out w/crack. You might already know this, but I thought I'd let brave & unsuspecting 'zaar fans in on an unfortunate piece of info about all the lovely selections of cheese alternatives you might find in your local supermarket: the majority are NOT vegan - they are vegetarian. Many cheeses contain casein and rennet, both of which come from cows' stomachs, so vegetarian alternatives omit these ingredients but still contain milk proteins. It can be a real bummer when you get so excited about all the wonderful options and realize they're still not for you :(
There are some good vegan choices out there. Veganrella is my personal favorite, but I'm going to keep my eyes peeled for rice-based options!

Yummy Yummy Yummy!  Thanks for posting this recipe!  I loved the flavor the garlic/sesame oil/soy sauce and pepper flakes with the mushrooms and green beans.  Nice change from my normal asparagus/mushroom roasting! :)

What a fantastic treat!  It's satisfying and sustaining!  My family and friends couldn't get enough of it!

1) I think it's silly that you reduce the liquid to 2 C. but then only use 1 1/2 C. in the sauce - so I use ALL the reduced liquid and then need about 2-3 T. flour to thicken it to my preference.
2). It is SO important to use low-sodium broths!!  And even still, the resulting sauce will be very salty.  
Serve this with garlic-smashed red potatoes and you will be in heaven.

thanks!

I made this batch last night and froze them.  Today I popped two on the griddle, brushed them with a bit of olive oil, and they were just as good as when I made them fresh last night.  This will go in my cookbook as the only pita bread recipe I need.  Thanks for sharing!
Five stars !Kitten what a fabulous & easy recipe !Thanks a ton !
These were a big hit at a vacation planning get-together.  Couldn't find the Pepperidge Farm rolls but used a Hawaiian Sweet roll. Thanks for sharing..this one is a keeper!

I served this recipe as a side salsa/salad along with a seafood casserole, another salad, garlic rice and roasted asparagus-every one raved about it -  I love the cilantro. I used red, green, orange and yellow peppers in it.  Thanks for posting this delicious recipe Kathy 228

Very different and very wonderful. It is unbelievable that so few simple ingredients can create such a great and complex flavor. ...And it is an impressive! appetizer. To tell the truth, I forgot to put the mint leaves in, and find them not entirely necessary. On the other hand, I put one on top as I consumed my second puff and it added another subtle layer of flavor. I will be certain not to omit the mint next time. And there WILL be a next time. I am so happy you posted this, Mme. Melissa.

Yummy!  I, too, didn't have any macadamia nuts (can't have them, anyway, as I'm allergic to them), but I toasted an equal amount of walnuts with the oats/sesame seed mixture, then followed the rest of the recipe exactly.

A very easy dinner tonight. Very tasty - better than the canned stuff.  I didn't change the taste ingredients, but increased the pasta to 2 cups (dry) and doubled the pasta sauce.  I just like it more saucy.  I used fresh mozzarella cheese on top, yum! - and added a sprinkle of parmesan cheese.
A very easy to make side dish and a nice change from lemon flavoured couscous. A 'keeper' for me :)

Very Good and easy, I made with Rotini noodles and left out the veggies (picky kids) also added some parmesan cheese with the mozzarella, I just took the whole pan and stuck it under the broiler to melt the cheese which kind of browned it a little. Thanks for a great quick meal recipe.

I love these!  I made them two different ways.  I dry fried them in a cast iron skillet and they turned out great.  After I made a half dozen or so the flour started to darken and burn so I thought I would try baking them in the oven.  I baked the remainder at 500 degrees until lightly browned.  They had great flavor using both methods but I really like the way they look when I fried them (like the picture).  Also, the baked ones got a little crisp at the edges, but that could be because I baked them a little too long.  Thanks for the great recipe Najwa.
I'm not much of a cook, and it was very easy to make and very tasty!
We really liked these. I cheated and used pre-cooked chicken but otherwise followed the directions exactly.
Mmmm... This was really good! I cut back on the butter and used whole wheat couscous. I ate this for breakfast with a poached egg on top!
These worked out great for us!  My girls enjoyed these just as much as the fudge pops from the supermarket!  Thanks for posting this yummy warm weather treat!
This was an easy meal and pretty good, the only thing was the meat was kinda tough, but it could have just been the meat that I bought.
WOW!  I just can't describe how much I loved this rice.  Great taste and really easy to make.  Thank you so much.
This was a GREAT simple recipe for my boys.  They had fun making them and eating them.  Everyone could adjust their own additions to them.

My first popovers! Like another reviewer I've always been afraid to try popovers - don't know why. A very easy recipe, but I did over-beat. I used a whisk and next time I'll use a wooden spoon. Otherwise they were great. Thanks MizzNezz!

Made these for the PAC contest and we really enjoyed them.  I used the beef this time and may, as suggested, use chicken next time.  Dave really liked the beef version.  The flavor was right on for us and the meat was fork tender.  There was a lot of liquid in this but that could have been from the added salsa, which was my homemade.  I will definitely make these again in the future.  thanks for sharing.

This was very tasty.  Just the thing for some leftover sauce I had.  My kids missed the meat but it would be nice with some browned ground turkey to keep down the fat if you don't mind meat.  Thanks for the post.

Just made this tonight for my mother's birthday, after her plans were canceled at the last moment. It was GREAT! SO moist and delicious, without being overly sweet. Confession: I accidentally DOUBLED the butter(!!!), but mom was none the wiser-it was still so yummy! I also used half dark brown sugar (no lt.) and half regular sugar. Still ok! I used Rick's Special Buttercream from allrecipes on top. Keeper!

I made this for my birthday cake yesterday, and it was GREAT! Every bite is an experience. My husband - the dessert freak - ate at least 3 pieces.(I'm sure the rest will disappear today...)
My oven runs a little cool, so I baked it at 375 and it was done in about 53 minutes.
Definitely another for my dessert collection.
Thanks!

Very cute, simple, and yummy!!! The only changes i made was i used whole wheat bread and regular butter, so i didnt salt them. Ive used this multiple times, and will definatly keep using them. Thanks for the cute recipe!
These were pretty good.  I like having an alternative to plain old canned green beans.  I made these on the stove top and they were quick and easy.  These definitely stay in my rotation.
Wonderful!  I was surprised at how flavorful this was.  I used chicken tenders, and served with creamed corn, wild rice, and Recipe #85148.  This is going into my favorites file-  thanks for sharing!
I have been making these for a few years now.  They are great frozen.  As for dipping them, I could never get them to look neat, so I just started dipping them half-way so they are half-and-half.

Very good--addicting! Was afraid that there might be "too much going on" with the apricots and the white choc. chips, but the flavors compliment each other nicely.  Next time I'll try adding a bit of cinnamon, they might benefit from some spice.  Would also be good with some added coconut flakes.

These potatoes remind me a lot of the ones my dad made when I was a kid...but he made them in a frying pan and added some onions. They were easy and tasty and cooked up quickly. I made a half batch following the recipe exactly, cut them into about 1 inch cubes and baked them for 25 or 30 minutes.

Very moist and delicious. Super easy! I didnt have enough cocoa or oil so i substituted with chocolate chips and margarine. It didnt come out of the pan well but that may be because of the alterations so everyone grabbed a fork and we ate straight out of the pan! I will definitely make this again and i will try to omit the cocoa all together for a white cake to see how it tastes...Ok ,I made a white cake by omitting the cocoa and it was delicious. I added a bit more flour cuz of he absence of the cocoa and i didnt use baking soda cuz i ran out. It wasnt as moist as the chocolate cake. I would add more sugar and vanilla next time.
Excellent, tender, flavorful.  We used a smaller roast, but folowed the rest exactly.  Will make again, great company worthy dish
Very yummy!  I served this with blueberries and blackberries.  Thanks for such an easy and tasty recipe!

Wow, this is GREAT. This was so simple, followed the directions to the "T" and it came out wonderful. I loved the seasoning and how the whole thing blended. Thank you for sharing, this is a definite *Keeper* in my book. The family loved it. Next time, I need to make more. ~V

Made these for dessert for our 
Sunday dinner.  I had never worked with phyllo pastry before and had a fun time with my son making this yummy dessert.  Like the other reviewer said, whats not to like with this recipe.  I really liked the filling, before it was even cooked in the phyllo pastry, could eat it all on its own.  Thanks for a great recipe JackieMarie.

What's not to love in this?? :)!!  This is perfect comfort food!  We loved the mix of spinach and cheese.  Used low-fat milk and some leeks instead of the shallots.  Can't wait to have the leftovers!! Thanks Cynna!  Made for PAC 2007.

What a great appetizer! The combination of flavors is superb.
I didn't change a thing. Thank you Mme Melissa.

loved these and only thing I did different was instead of returning to crock with sauce I put them in foil and did in oven.  Will make for a party next month and will be great to have already and just do the final part in oven when ready...clean up will be a breeze. I served with smashed potatoes.

To die for! I added 1/2 tsp of baking powder as recomended and it turned out perfect, the right brownie consistency. Next time i will leave off the frosting, it made it too sweet for my taste and took away from the perfect brownies. Thanks!
Lovely

We really enjoyed this Pico De Gallo!  It was easy to make and had outstanding flavor.  My tomatoes were not home grown -- I used the "vine tomatoes" I found in the grocery store.  I can imagine using home grown tomatoes would really take this "over the moon".  Thank you for posting such an outstanding recipe.

I particularly wanted to comment on this recipe because I didn't want Sally B's bad review to be the most recent one! I think she might have used a poor cake mix, because I followed the directions exactly and the cookies came out fluffy and light. I appreciated Muffin Goddess's note on step #9 - this saved a lot of time.  In all, these cookies were very unique - a light, cakey texture with a spicy zing.  The two different chocolates are a must to round out the balance of flavors. I do think that the cookies can do without the drizzle because they're quite sweet as is!

a really creamy, light, delicately flavoured houmous - totally perfect & so easy to make.  I think it's great as is, but my boyfriend decided to pep it up with a few drops of tabasco sauce.  I used 6 tablespoons of water because I like quite a loose houmous.

I have made my own tzatziki before, and it was always disapointing. I loved this recipe, even better than the stuff you get at the restaurant. I cut the recipe in half, reduced the oil to 1 tbsp, and used dried dill weed. I made this recipe the day before I needed it, which I would recomend the flavor was way better the next day. I can't wait to have greek again, just so I can use this recipe, Thanks!!
delicious!! very easy to make, made it with chicken on the side. definitely will make this again.

the only white castle burgers i've tried are the ones you buy at the grocery stores in the frozen/microwavable section. never tried the ones you buy at the restaurant so i can't really compare it to those. but i have to say this recipe is awesome. burgers came out so tasty and delicious. husband was VERY satisfied..loved it..so much so that he said the filling would be great in other dishes. i used dinner rolls that were a little larger than recipe stated. followed everything and will definately use this recipe alot. will go in my favorites cookbook. thank you so much for sharing!
I made this for DH's birthday. Both of us loved it. It was super moist. I used a store-bought chocolate frosting as well as  walnuts. Thank you for the great recipe!
This certainly is a keeper. My daughters loved it. I used half & half, pizza sauce, salami, black olives & cheddar cheese (didn't have mozzarella). I loved how easy it is. Thanks.

Very good and pretty easy, too.  I didn't add pesto, parmesan, or oregano and used regular thyme, but it was still quite flavorful--perhaps because I added a good amount of salt and pepper.  I used small shell pasta, which I cooked separately so my leftovers wouldn't be mushy.  I added a little fresh diced tomato at the end.  I don't like frozen peas and didn't have access to fresh, so I didn't include them.  I think next time I will add some edamame.  White beans would probably be good, too.
Great recipe.  Had an extra zucchini and both were great!
This is one of my kids favorite meals.  We use different fillings depending on our moods, hamburger, pepperoni, onions, mushrooms...It makes a quick and easy meal served with a salad.
This cake was unbeleivable! We could not stop eating it (trust me I tried) including the kids who are usually just nibblers. Make it; you'll love it!
I made this and my whole family loved it!!
very good
This was one of my choices for the Pick A Chef game, and we really enjoyed it. I scaled the recipe down and subbed a serrano for the jalapeno, but no other changes. Thanks for posting the recipe!

Yummy-ola! Very similar to my Recipe #209977...without the raw eggs! Love the mushrooms in there (I used canned--it's what I had on hand), and of COURSE the bacon adds that "extra" depth of flavor that you don't get with other meats...smoky and rich. The only thing I did differently, I added about a teaspoon of red pepper flakes and seeds--wowie kazowie! Oh, and I used fettucini instad of bow-ties. KEEPER!!!


*Made for PAC Spring 2007*

5 wonderful stars! These IMPRESSED our double birthday party crowd, kids and adults alike, all 43 of them!.. ok, discount the 1 baby LOL. I did however need to take some drastic action because I didn't bargain on the difference a small substitution would make. I can't get peppermint Extract here, but did have some imported peppermint ESSENCE... First I added the recommended 1 Tablespoon, and couldn't taste the peppermint at all and needed to add another two tablesppons to make this taste pepperminty enough. The result of this was a very liquid mixture with the condensed milk so I needed an additional two and a half cups of icing sugar to make it anywhere near a firm dough form. After that I used a small wine bottle top to press out the circles and it made zillions of them LOL... Mine turned out small and fatter and extactly bite sized. I dried them overnight under a clean tea towel after drying them for 2 hours  and turning them over, and the next morning they dipped like a dream... considering I'm a messy dipper LOL. If you are using ESSENCE instead of Extract I would *strongly recommend* not using the entire amount of the 14oz condensed milk to compensate for the extra liquid that the essence will make, or halve the recipe becuase I got at least 90 of my small ones from only *half* the mixture I ended up having. Guess what are the Birthday Treats Bags? LOL. That said, I would make these again in heartbeat, they are so well received and people here were amazed that I made them myself and the recipe was demanded several times. Please see my rating system: glitches not withstanding an excellent recipe that family and friends are already demanding that I make again. Thanks!
Simple and easy! I used chicken sausage and added 1 tsp. red pepper flakes. Thanks!
great i used the whipped cream to fill cream puffs and they held up beautifully.

Ooooh, ooooh, oooh! Yummy-ola! Your nana had a very good idea! These are like BETTER than any kind of store-bought granola bar. Great as a snack for the kids in the p.m. or for a breakfast bar with a banana and glass of milk. KEEPER! *Made for PAC Spring 2007*
These are pretty good, a viable option to the fuss of a real cheesecake, but not quite as mouthwatering.

I have made this.  I will never make any other pnutbtr fudge again.  It is smooth and creamy, has a wonderful flavor and is very easy.  I tried a canned frosting and pnutbtr microwave fudge that turned out more like candy once because it was easy... This is true fudge.  It was perfect.  My family an coworkers make me buy a gallon jar of pnutbtr every Christmas and make this fudge until the jar is gone...Lot of fudge, lotta flavor.
Good-very lite. I made them with some dumplings and potstickers. Even my picky husband liked it and he's a meat and potato guy. Thanks!

Very tasty! I made a few adjustments for taste and the size crowd I was working with: I divided the recipe in half; reduced the salt to approx. 2 1/2 teaspoons (instead of 4 1/2); I cooked it in one deep (steam-table) pan; added cooked, chopped bacon; added approx. 39 slices of cheese; also, it was cooked in a convection oven. I stirred the bacon and approx. 24 slices of cheese in at the halfway point (had to double the initial time to 20 min), stirred til melted, then laid the remaining 15 slices on top. I covered it with a lid and put it back in the oven for  approximately 5 minutes, then put it in the steam table (on high) to finish while I finished cooking. They were a huge hit! The kids and staff kept coming in to see when snack was going to be ready...and one of the teens, upon hearing the boy next to him wasn't getting any eggs (seconds) said, "Are you crazy? Those eggs are kickin'!" :D All changes aside...you still have a great recipe, Miss Annie...thank you very much! :D
Almost perfect, may add a teaspoon of sugar next time. Very good tho!

These are really yummy muffins.  The amount of cocoa without the addition of any milk in the muffins give a very rich chocolate flavour.  I actually used even more applesauce in place of half the oil to make them even lower in fat.  I omitted the nuts in the muffins for personal preference, but added the full amount in the topping.  After I had started making these muffins I realized although baking soda was mentioned in the directions an amount wasn't listed in the ingredients.  So I added about 1 1/2 tsp, which was probably a bit too much since the texture was a bit airy and dryish.  None the less, they still deserve 5 stars and I am sure with the proper amount of baking soda these muffins would deserve 5+!!  Thanks for posting such a delish recipe!

Reviewed for RSC # 9. 10 stars ! Rush now and buy oranges and plain cake ! Ouch this was so georgous it was painful to look at the last slice and not go crazy finding a fork quick enoughâ€¦ Please DO increase the orange juice sauce and drizzle it over not only the bottom slice of cake but the top one tooâ€¦ DO increase the amount of oranges and layer them everywhere, in the middle on the topâ€¦ drizzle that white chocolate heavily over the cake make the layers and then beat off the competition and enjoy ! My sister in law makes this recipe and it is wonderful!  I have hers saved on here because I couldn't submit it- and just finally found yours to know why!  Great bread - a little more dense than some - very tasty!!!
Excellent cake! Very simple and gorgeous outcome. I made it today for my friend's birthday. This is worth every extra minute to make. Thanks for the grreat recipe! ^^

I'm not giving stars because I changed it so much.  I halved the recipe, but I actually used a lot more spinach, 10ozs of frozen spinach(defrosted and excess moisture pressed out).  I added 16ozs of sliced browned smoked sausage.  I still mixed it all up together and popped in the oven.  The way I did it, the dish was a total meal in one.  I used regular mozarella cheese instead of the smoked cheddar, but I did use the smoked Gouda.  I really enjoyed the taste the gouda gave it.  This was quick, easy, flavorful, and satisfying.

Oh gosh I can't believe I forgot to rate this!
Excellent homemade cake , it was good enough to eat with no frosting as well! 
My daughter made this one evening when we had friends over playing cards ... she got a late start on it , and our friends said they had to stay long enough to have a piece because it smelled so good baking LOL 
Went over VERY well , thanks for sharing this great recipe!:)

This pudding is delicious!  I reduced the sugar by almost half and it still tasted wonderful. I had only one lemon so had to use lemon concentrate but it didn't hurt the outcome at all.  I love the fact this pudding is nutritional - a wonderful way to get soy into the diet. Thanks for a great recipe!

Really fantastic salad!  I found the cinnamon flavor just a bit overpowering, so I'll do a tad less than 1/8 t. next time.  I took this to a picnic and everyone loved it.  Definitely unique - not for those that don't like to adventure with their food.  Thanks for a great recipe!

The tomatoes are a colorful addition to this salad.  It is easy to make and has good flavor.  I did add salt and pepper in the end.  I'll be making this one again.  Thank you for posting.  I made this for the Spring PAC 2007 game.
I had never made homemade mac and cheese and we will never be going back to the boxed version. This was easy to make, but absolutely tasty!  I doubled the recipe and it came out great.

As I don't like raisins in cookies I omitted them...Otherwise I followed the recipe as written...Can I just say WOW...Until this recipe came along, I never made oatmeal cookies...Didn't much like them even as a kid...But omigod! This recipe is so delicious, so delectable, that I cannot wait to make them again...I'm having visions of Cinnamon Ice Cream served with these cookies for dessert...YUM! Thank you SO much for posting this recipe!

This is a great chocolate cake recipe that is easy to make and incredibly moist and delicious. I made this recipe but substituted very strong boiling coffee for the water, and a specialty dark cacao/cocoa mix for the cocoa, which made the cake come out somewhat bittersweet but still delicious and chocolatey.

Made for PAC, Spring 2007 ~ What a great salad! Taking the intro to this recipe to heart, I made this up a day ahead & served it the next day ~ Can't tell you how it tasted the first day, 'cause I kept my fingers out of it, but the day after, it really was GREAT tasting & something well worth sharing with my diabetic friends!

For perfect, fall-off-the-bone, juicy ribs, use this recipe! I'm not sure why the recipe specifies not to use Diet Dr. Pepper, but I did and my results were fantastic. Honestly, I can't imagine these ribs could've been any better/different with the full sugar version. I boiled the ribs for about two hours and then finished them off on the grill for about 20 minutes. Divine! I also used recipe# 59772 for the barbecue sauce. This will be my permenant go-to recipe for ribs.
A very tasty bread and the one-bowl is a nice twist.  I used sugar which I think I would cut to 3/4 cup - it was a bit sweet for me.  I also use 1/4 cup egg substitute.  Posted for spring 2007 PAC.

I gave this 3 stars. I made these for part of our Sunday Big Breakfast. The kids like them. I thought they were ok. I agree with another reviwer to try cinnamon in the batter next time. I also wanted to mention that the batter seems very thick but that does not affect the muffins they are not heavy. My muffins only took 15 minutes to bake when baked for 20 minutes the bottoms burned. This might be my oven. I will make these again with cinnamon. Thanks for posting a good recipe. Christine (internetnut)
I've been making this for years. At one time Lipton made a spicy onion soup mix, it was particularly good with that. Yummy even with the ordinary mix.

Very good although I will increase the peppermint next time, also I doubled the amount of Oreo cookies, I did not unmold it I just left it in the pan, mine took more than 4 hours to set but that may be because of my fridge temperature, thanks ehco!...Kitten

This was so easy to make.  I served it for Motherâ€™s Day Brunch.  I followed the recipe exactly and took 35 minutes to bake.  This loaf is like a big cheese biscuit... YUMMM!  My mom request a couple of slices to take home.

I like this much better than guacamole. One of my avocados went bad so halved the recipe. It was very easy to assemble, the hard part was staying out of it while it chilled. I served it along side some grilled chicken. I will be making this again for sure.
I love this recipe and so do my kids! I also add a dash of nutmeg in. Delicious!

I really enjoyed the cinnamon and sugar in the omelet. The blueberries on top though turned the egg whites a gross looking green. Maybe that's because I used frozen blueberries, not sure. It tasted good, but I think next time I will leave out the blueberries. Also I used bananas instead of strawberries, I really want to try this recipe with both-I think the two always go great together. Thanks for the recipe!

My family ate it all.  I made this for Mother's Day and it was great.
I did use olive oil instead of mayo but kept everything else the same and it was crispy and flavorful. I didn't expect it to come out so perfect.  I will make this again soon.
Easy, fun and tastes great! Made several times already. fyi - regular muffin tins seem to work just as well (I don't have mini-muffin tins)
I didn't care for this recipe- - I was looking for one that was thicker.
Very good
Lots of better recipes than this one
This was fantastic.  My DB LOVES horseradish and the BBQ so... its a keeper.  I wouldn't change a thing.  Thanks for the post!
The flavor was good, but was covered up by salt.  This was too salty for my taste, so next time I would make it with 1/3 of the salt. Otherwise, the texture and flavor would have been great.
Wow!  This pudding is rich and has a wonderful chocolate flavor.  I used semi-sweet chocolate chips and love the taste.  My boys enjoyed their dessert tonight, thanks, Kitten.

The ingredients are great but there were some key steps left out. You are supposed to mix two eggs, three tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup of parmesean cheese in the spaghetti. This forms the "crust". The other problem is the writer gave no clue if we are to mix the spaghetti sauce and tomatoes togethere or put them on separately. Also, what do we do with the other half of the parmesean cheese in the recipe? Poorly written recipe and wouldn't recommend this for anyone who is not a seasoned cook and has made a spaghetti pie before. Sorry but low marks from me.
My favorite recipe - one my mom made for us 15+ years ago.  I use stew meat instead and eat it like a stew instead of over rice.  You must try this recipe!

My husband enjoyed the recipe very much.  I followed the recipe exactly, except I used fresh rosemary and parsley instead of dried.  I did not see in the directions where to add the garlic, so I added it with the potatoes.  
For my taste, the sauce was too starchy/pasty, and I would cut the amount of olive oil in half.  The puree is pretty thick already, and when combined with starchy vegetables like potato and carrot, and with only a splash of wine for liquid, the result was very heavy.
This is the third rhubarb recipe  tried off RecipeZaar.  We like this one best--no changes made to an already excellent recipe.  Thanks, Kate!
I liked these. I doubled the recipe. My husband is not a big onion fan, that may have been why he did not care for it, but I did. I will make it again. Thanks for posting it!

This was great! I have 4 kids and 3 crockpots, so I obviously like anything using them. This was a great base recipe. Once I tried it and it was good, I tweaked it slightly by using a 6lb breast, adding a small ringed onion, a bit of rosemary and hungarian paprika, and some celery stalks.

This was a winner!  I had never had this before, and I was hesitant.  I was afraid it would be incredibly hot.  As it turns out, the pepper juice just gives everything a really nice flavor.  This was so easy to put together, and I used your suggestion of serving it over the Orzo with Parsley and Lemon Zest.  I could see this becoming one of our go-to meals.  Thanks for posting!

What a wonderful roast beef recipe. The gravey was so tasty and flavourful. The beef was tender, moist and delicious. I added a carrot and 2 shallots to the vegetable mixture. I will definitely be making this again.  I can't wait to use the meat & gravey in a meat pie. Thanks so much for sharing Gail...Kudos Kato

I made this recipe but cut in half because there was only 2 of us eating. I made it as directed. My son and I found it to be a bit bland, and I was worried that the lemon would be too strong. Next time, I would add some garlic, salt or other spice, such as seasoned salt, next time. Thanks for an easy recipe. I would make again but with added ingredients.

This is an amazing coffee cake.  It is soft, moist and utterly delicious.  I was choosing between several recipes and am very pleased with this one.  I am making this again!  I did put this in two bread loaf pans and made an extra graham cracker, butter, brown sugar combination for the topping.  I did however use the original cinnamon sugar combo for the layers in the cake.
Sweet and good! Instead of putting a top crust on this, I baked at 425* for 10 minutes, then added a meringue topping and baked an additional 20 minutes at 350*.  It turned it out very nice.
Great!  Easy to make - maybe next time, add a minced garlic clove.

I didn't have any hot dogs when I made this recipe, but substituted with smoked sausages, just sliced them. This was a really easy and quick meal my family enjoyed. They really liked the sauce. Thank you for the recipe.

This recipe was published in the Pillsbury June 2007 Summer Appetizers little cookbook.  These are very tasty morsels.  I tried them using pepperjack cheese for an extra kick, but had to cook them slightly longer than called for.

Sorry to only give this 3 stars but I followed this recipe and marinated the meat for 8 hours. The aroma while it was cooking was great.  We had to add salt.  My sons used A1 sauce to enhance the flavor. It was OK but not a strong enough marinade for our tastes.  Thanks for posting.

The combination of goats cheese and the sweetness of the onions was great.  I guess results would vary depending on the type of goats cheese you use. This was easy to make and had sophisticated flavours, my guests were impressed.  Will definitely make again.

We made a class cookbook this year where I asked for parents to send in special recipes.  Then we had a potluck where parents could send food in.  This was one of the cakes brought it.  Wow!  It was so flavorful and good.  I thought with all the liquid it would be soggy, but instead it was so moist.  All the kids loved it.

I also had never roasted a chicken before, but used the recipe more for cooking guidelines, and found it very moist and flavorful. Will definitely be roasting chicken more often thanks to this recipe !

Ditto to what everybody else said ... this was just wonderful.  I used two jalapeno chilis -- first time I'd ever used 'em before, believe it or not.  Now I know that one would have been PLENTY for me.  The heat of the jalapenos kind of took over the wonderful flavor, but that's my fault, not the recipe's -- next time I'll cut back to one, or less, and it'll be perfect.  Thanks for posting this!

Easy and fun to make and eat!!! I did put the wonton wrappers in the mini muffin pan (sprayed with PAM) and pre-cooked on 425 for 5 minutes.  Then I put the filling and cheese in and cooked for another 3-4 minutes (until the cheese was melted).  I watched these closely in the oven so that the edges of the wontons did not burn. This recipe is the BOMB....I made it this last past Memorial day and added a few things to it, First I rubbed the ribs down with the following:
1 1/2 tsp.cumin
1 1/2 tsp. chili powder
1 tsp. paprika
1/2 tsp. white pepper
2 tsp. nutmeg
1 tsp. kosher salt
1 1/2 tsp. dry ground musturd
1 tsp. dried basil


I mixed all of this together and rubbed it on the ribs ands let it sit for about 2 hours, then I got a deep sauce pan and placed the ribs in it and poured a 2 liter bottle of Dr.Pepper over it til it was covered....and I let the ribs sit in this marinade bath all nite in the fridge. Delicious!! I've had this before in a restaurant and have always wanted to try to make it at home. ZWT3 gave me a chance to do just that. Although I didn't try to pour the brandy over the citrus peels for dramatic effect, and burn my house down, lol, it was very good. Thanks Annacia.

Wow! This was a real stretch for my family and I honestly was not sure if they would like it or not. Cinnamon and raisins usually mean "dessert" to them. But we all totally loved this, it was delicious, and I am so glad we tried it. Thanks for posting!

I have made this numerous times and it is always excellent and easy!  I get wonderful compliments!  Yum-Yum

Wounderful! I had some blueberries I really needed to use up and I was looking for something I could have for dessert that was a bit lighter and this did the trick. Wen't together in no time and it was absolutely delicious! Thank's!
I had sliced bananas in the deep freeze so I used them.  Was thick like an icecream sundae and so yummy.  Try it, I know you'll like it.

Yummy yummy yum! What can I say... great combination of ingredients. Sun-dried tomatoes, pesto, garlic, butter and cheese. How can you go wrong? Everyone thought it was great. Will make again. Thanks!

I made this for dessert tonight, and boy was it delicious! I made it in an 11x7x2 glass dish, and used 9 ice cream sandwiches. Great dish. I was born and raised in Pittsburgh but have never heard of this before, so I thought I'd give this a try, now that I live an ocean away from my hometown. 

I didn't have any pimiento strips on hand so I substituted a diced, sauteed red bell pepper and it tasted just the same.  I also couldn't bring myself to use processed cheese spread (despite my Pittsburgh roots, I'm a bit of a foodie purist), sorry!  I used a mixture of white cheddar and swiss- this was nice.  

There are two small things that I would do differently when I make this again: I will saute the onion instead of boiling it as the boiled onion lacks aesthetic appeal and does not add as much flavorful punch as it could have.  Also, I am going to top this with at least a cup of breadcrumbs next time; the crispy, crunchy breadcrumbs on top really complete this dish.  I only used a small amount and wish that I had added more. Crushed Ritz crackers would be really good instead of breadcrumbs, too!

All in all, we definitely liked this and it made us feel a little closer to the Burgh! Thanks for posting, yinz!

I made this for my son's graduation party.  It was absolutely FANTASTIC!  It was easy to prepare and I didn't have to worry when I got home from graduation about preparing my meal for our family.  It is already put into my recipe keeper file. Thanks again for posting!

Just like people have said already, it turned out very creamy on the inside with a nice crisp exterior.  I couldn't stop eating them!   This is definitely a keeper, thank you so much!

Loved this recipe, but to make it a little more interesting I add a couple slices of pepperoni, a few sliced olives, couple of sliced mushrooms, and a tablespoon of ricotta cheese to each calzone. I love this cake. So sweet and so moist... I have no problems giving this cake 5 stars or more. I do wish the glaze was thicker, next time I think I will try and find another glaze or just add powdered sugar to this one. Will be making again sometime.

Easy way to fancy up rice for a side dish.  I would add some dried herbs next time, though, for a little more flavor.  Some thyme or rosemary, maybe.  I used toasted almond slivers, instead of cashews.

this was pretty good but a little boring and not much 'crisp' to it at all, more like baked bran apples. i added walnuts and didnt use any butter and it still baked up nicely if i make again i will add some vanilla and maybe some more spices (nutmeg, cloves..ect) but it was a fun and healthy way to use up some apples that were going soft, i used gala and ate it with whipped topping for breakfast!

Thanks for a delicious dinner that helped us beat the heat.

Wow!  Great stuff!!  I'm not a fan of whole wheat pasta or brown rice, so was skeptical about making bulgur; so glad I tried this recipe.  Not "whole wheaty" or dry tasting.  Moist with great flavor; my new favorite, healthy comfort food.

Used about 6 tsp of olive oil (instead of 1/2 Tbsp) in order to get healthy oil in each serving.  Used a yellow bell pepper instead of green.  Chopped the onion and bell pepper into fairly small little pieces.  Used 1 cup of drained canned tomatoes flavored with oregano, basil, and garlic.  Also added 1 Tbsp. fresh, minced oregano.  Used the broccoli from a bag of microwaved steamed broccoli (I steamed it in the microwave, then chopped it into really small bits, just before adding it into the pilaf.)  

NOTE:  I used a bit more water (maybe 1/4 cup) after adding the tomatoes/bulgur/water/salt/pepper, while it was cooking over low heat (somewhere between steps 8 and 9).
Excellent. All I can say is that this recipe for artichokes was both easy, and delicious!! Thanks echo echo! Made for World Tour.
