I loaded a bread bowl with this and it was a big hit with our friends. I consider this recipe a keeper.

This was a huge HIT!  The cake is moist and just fantastic...it reminded me of the cakes my grandma use to make...I used Kittencal's Chocolate Buttercream Frosting/Icing recipe and I doubled that since I like a lot of frosting and it was perfect!  Even my hubby whose not a huge chocolate cake fan came back for seconds

This was SO good! I made it exactly by the directions, and would make it again (soon hopefully!) I used a 2 liter bottle of Dr. Pepper and simmered the ribs for about 1 1/2 hours. They were perfect. Falling off the bone. Thanks for the recipe!

Awesome wings Lynn! I made for supper tonight to go along with some brown fried rice I made. I doubled the sauce recipe so I could have some to go over my rice.  Everything was so good that I couldn't stop eating until I was so full I thought I was going to pop :D The sauce was wonderful! I put these in a safe place, so I won't misplace this one. Thanks for sharing!

Any chef who likes to bake, and especially one who likes the herbal and the cheesy kinds of bread, will not be able to resist this recipe.  The process is a delight, the aroma from the oven a treat, and the product is delicious.  There are some problems, however.  The spiral trapped air and created large voids in the slice, especially at the top, and the spinach looks more like cooked vegetables than herbal decoration.  Great possibilities but needs some refinement.
These were tooo delicious. I added 1 tsp of cinnamon and only had to bake for 15 minutes, as I had smaller muffins. My picky husband even enjoyed them!

Wow -- this is great! This will be wonderful served at my next brunch buffet. I made it exactly as written, and including not cooking the bacon first -- was I supposed to cook it first? If so, at least I used smoked bacon!

I made this cake one morning needing a chocolate fix.  The ingredients were all stock items so it was a very simple recipe to follow.  I baked two 9 inch cakes for 50 minutes in a conventional oven.  They cooled quickly and were very easy to frost.  The cake was very moist and not too sweet.  I am looking forward to having a piece tomorrow (if there is any left over once my Hubby comes home!).  Just kidding.  The portion is huge!  This can easily be used for a family gathering and everyone will enjoy.  Thanks so much for the post.  :)

These came out very good. My dough came out a little wet, but I imagine that was my flour choice. The dough, when I added more flour, was pillowy soft and cut the most perfect looking biscuits. Not one sloped! (thanks for the tip!) and tehy tasted so good that I got up in the middle of the night and ate one! This made a lot of bisuits, I didn't count, but maybe 20.
Literally one of my favorite pizzas.  My finace and I go there all the time to get it!  Thanks for posting the recipe.  I forget that I can make it too.

super good! simple to put together and yummy. I used milk chocolate and they were very rich and creamy I am going to do another batch with dark chocolate to see which one i like better either way fantastic recipe, thank you.

Warning, addictive.  Awesome.  I served this with Recipe #288061 and Recipe #288407.  The key is draining the cucumbers very well and squeezing out the moisture to make a nice thick sauce.  I used dill vs. mint as personal preference.

OMG, WOW!  These were incredibly tender.  I had about 2 lbs country style ribs and boiled them for about 1 hour 30 min.  Then baked them for 45 min.  I slathered them with Sweet Baby Rays BBQ sauce and they came out so tender that they fell apart.  DELICIOUS!  This is going to be the way I make these all the time now.  I made country style ribs a couple other times with some other recipes where you just boil them in water and seasonings, then bake them.  They didn't turn out half as tender as they did in this recipe.  Im so glad that I found this recipe!  Thanks! :)

This cake roll is absolutely delicious!    
It's the perfect springtime dessert, very light and not at all too sweet!  This was a huge hit at my baby shower!

Really a lemony cupcake with strawberry frosting, these really are yummo, and super easy to make. Sour cream in the batter is a really nice touch. We had to bake them over 25 minutes, however, and suggest that times may vary by climate and oven.  Made for OZ/NZ swap, Feb 08.

I followed the recipe exactly. I wasn't expecting this to be the best fry recipe I had ever tried, but it really was. Very tasty with just simple ingredients. Very easy to make. Being healthy is just a bonus. Will definitely make these again. Thanks for sharing.

This had great flavor, but I did have a few problems. I made the bread in the bread machine using the dough cycle and it worked well. The bread rolled out perfectly too. My biggest problem was the bread fell in the middle after coming out of the oven & being brushed with butter. 

I think there was almost too much of the spinach filling. Sprinkling the cheese on top of the loaf & then brushing with butter caused the cheese to fall off. Next time I will add the cheese to the filling & use part of the butter before it bakes. 

This had a nice herby flavor in the bread & the filling was colorful in the swirl. Very tasty! Note: I used the leftover bread to make garlic bread for a meal later in the week. Yummy! 

4 stars method 
5 stars taste

Well, these were nifty little treats!  More like a mashed potato patty than hash browns, but terrific flavor.  Almost a loaded baked potato!  I used fresh parsley and regular bacon (its what we had in the freezer).  I also left out the stock.  I think these would go perfect with grilled steak or roasted chicken.

Boomie, this is a winner. Loved the flavor. I served it along side salsa chicken so I omitted the parsley and added a little cracked pepper. Great and versital side dish. I used 2 %  cheddar. Thanks for posting.
A fun snack!  Kids loved them.
Oh wow ! I made it with 1 cup buttermilk in place of milk. I used 2/3 cup boiling water. I also used cake flour. This cake is so moist. Recipe is a keeper !!

I've been searching for a veggie burger recipe that didn't involve a long list of ingredients, massive prep and cook time, and a blender.  And this is it!  I've been buying veggie burgers occasionally, because I like them, even though I'm not a vegetarian.  After this recipe, I will no longer be buying those expensive tasteless burgers and using this instead!  This took me about 20 minutes to put together and cook, and I added red pepper flakes, cumin, and garlic powder.  I froze a couple of these for a meal later on!  Thanks!

Unbelievable chocolate cake! I was bribed into making a cake for work so home I came and searched this site. After serving this cake, I am now on baking for the rest of the year...people were delighted. This cake came out moist and delicious. I put a little more chocolate in than was required and added a teaspoon of coffee to the water as suggested in other recipes. I also iced it with chocolate ganache but will try caramel next time. No need to look any further than this recipe.
Looks very good.  I'm confused by the title, though.  What makes it Dark Chocolate?  Did you use a specific kind of chocolate powder, or is it just the concentration of it?  Thanks!

This was really excellent.  I've made this 2 times now and would have to say that I like the eggplant sliced 1/4 inch thick vs 1/2 thick and my husband agrees.  Seems to be more like true fried eggplant when done thinly.  I added extra onions to the mayo mix.  i also added crushed red peppers and parmesan to the bread crumb mix.  Really great recipe!

I have made this cake many times, and it's always been a favorite.  I made it today in a 10" tube pan, and baked for 45 minutes.  Not a good idea.  The cake fell, and broke coming out of the pan.  I have one in the oven now in a 13x9 pan.  This is the recipe on the back of the Hershey's cocoa container!
We ejoyed this.  My only change was to use a spicy chili paste instead of the chili paste with garlic.  Very nice, easy.    Well balanced.  Thanks for sharing!
Not so impressed. Maybe I didnt add enough sugar (seemed like a lot) but either way it didnt task much like chocolate. Maybe icing will help but I think I might just start again with a new recipe.
Grilled this tonight- DH liked this- I may have used to much jalapeno - had the taste, not the heat. Marinated over 24 hours. Good recipe- served with the Recipe #154918 El Torito Sweet Corn Cake.

I'd like very much to try out this recipe. However, withouth any mention in the ingredient portion of the recipe of its use, a reference to white chocolate pops up in the directions portion. I'm not sure how to deal with this fact. If you could check the recipe and iron out that wrinkle -- and any others -- I would be much obliged. Thanks!
Delicious comfort food. So easy to make and so very tasty. Poaching the fish in milk will make even non-fisheaters like it!

This turns out great. The first time round I made it with a mix of white flour and brown. Second time all brown. It tastes better, and the texture is softer when you use a mix. Course I forgot the milk powder the second time. All in all a great simple recipe to keep on hand....

this was VERY easy to make, and tastes so good! i excluded the lemon juice, and added a lot more vanilla, and cinnamon powder in the crumbs.  next time i may add crushed oreo to the cream cheese mix too. thanks for this recipe!

I've had a package of drumsticks in the freezer that I'd been meaning to use, so I decided to make these last night. Great recipe, it tasted so much like fried chicken! It was very simple to make and the coating was to die for. I was really surprised at just how juicy these came out. There is no such thing as too spicy for me, so I added a little Frank's hot sauce to the beaten egg (well, eggbeaters). Thanks for this!
excellent repeat recipe in my house 5 stars all the way

Not a bad recipe coming from Hershey!! I had to laugh when I reached for my box of cocoa and there was the recipe almost word for word... Here I was looking for a new recipe!! I love Hershey's but was looking for one with more a dark chocolate taste! Guess if ya can't beatem' you copy them right??? Becareful of copy right laws..

I would have never tried bulgar but this recipe sounded good so I tried it.  It was pretty good!  Nice change of pace from our usual side dishes.
The second time I made it without the green pepper and with pinto instead of black beans and I liked it even more!
Great recipe.  My DH said he felt healthier just be eating it!

this was great! I used it in some coffee, and some milk for the kids. I liked the not so sweet taste of it, My dh said it tasted like chocolate, not something fake. 
I will use a much larger pan then I did this time, as it wanted to boil over all the time. I also will let it cook longer so it will be thicker. Both are my fault and not that of the recpie's

WOW--i love this stuff.  I had it at a carryin at work today (and previously).  I could not stop eating it.  I can't wait to make it and take it somewhere.  I think it would be good with corn chips too!

Very tasty!  Simple and quick to cook.  I bought prawns that were already peeled and deveined, so dinner was on in just minutes.  This will become one of my standard great dinners on a work night.  DS thought it rated 5 stars too.

I loved it! I did cut down on the garlic powder, only 1/4 tsp and added 1/4 onion powder, a personal preference and added 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper. I had a very large egg and so added 1/2 tsp more baking powder and a little more cheese and flour. I made 34 mini puffs. Delicious! Thanks for posting. My pkg of frozen spinach was 10 ozs. so I used it all instead of a 8 oz. cup. 
I will definitely make again.
This is a great teenager snack!

I found this quite nice, although not as sweet as sorbet should be (in my opinion).  Sorbet should be very tangy (and this was excellent), but still leave a sweet after taste.

This is by no means a criticism as sweetness/bitterness is purely a personal taste.  Overall, this sorbet is probably the nicest I've ever had.  It beats commercial sorbet hands down.

I didn't use the rinds at all as I don't like the flavour, so I used an extra lemon instead, squeezed into the boiling sugar solution.  I'd seen this done in other recipes.

Thanks for posting this!

Wow!  I baked this for work, and everybody seemed to love it!  I followed the instructions exactly except at the end I added 1 bag of chocolate chips to add texture to the cake.  After it cooled, I used chocolate mousse in  between the layers and buttercream frosting for the outside.  When we cut into the cake, though, it seemed to crumble pretty easily, although that could be my fault with the mousse.  Next time I try it, I'll be using a chocolate ganache and most likely leaving the chocolate chips out since the cake was flavorful enough and didn't need the extra chocolate.  Overall though, my co-workers thoroughly enjoyed the cake and they've requested it several times, so this is definitely a winner!  Thanks for such a great recipe!

This was very good.  My dh was raving about it.  He said to definetly make it again.  I would have given it 5 stars but it seemed a little dry to me.  Next time i will use more sauce or soup.  Great recipe thanks for sharing!

This was a great cake recipe. I used Ener-G egg substitute, soy milk, and mint extract for half of the vanilla extract as I was making it for a Christmas party. My only problem was that it was very delicate - it fell apart when I tried to remove it from my snowflake-shaped cake pan. I layered the pieces with candy cane ice cream in a trifle bowl and everyone loved it so much we actually ran out! Thanks Marg, for a delicious and versatile recipe!

Excellent! The flavor of the cilantro made this dish outstanding. However, we love cilantro so if you don't care for it, you might want to substitute it with some kind of parsley. The only modifications I made was I used 3 cloves of garlic for two chicken breast (we love garlic, too) and I also left it in the marinade in the fridge for about 2 hours and took it out 30 minutes before grilling. This certainly didn't hurt anything. The chicken was moist and tender. Our new favorite grilled chicken!

I made these the other night and meant to get on and rate them right then, but just now got around to it. As I was cooking the meat mixture I tasted it and already knew these tasted almost exaclty like White Castle's...we've never gotten to eat there...only the frozen ones, but have eated at Krystal Burger..which taste some what like these. I also couldnt find the tiny buns so I bought Publix (our grocery store) brand dinner rolls, which are smaller the hamburger buns but taste just like them. They worked great!! After we made them we dug in...these are yummy!!!!!

Update...I have made this atleast once every two weeks since finding it :D Ty again for sharing it!

5 stars. This was great, my BF and I both liked this a lot. Nuts and beans fell out of the tortillas, but that was okay they cooked separately and I piled them on top with lots of yummy salsa. I found some low-fat gouda so that was a plus too! Thanks! Made for RSC #11.:D

The batter was extremely heavy and the loaves didn't rise as I expected them to; even had to leave them in the oven an extra 10 minutes.  The taste was there, the texture wasn't.  Made for Beverage Tag.  I will try again, it may just have been "that kind of a day" for me.
This chocolate cake is soooo moist. I used it to make Black Forest Cake and everyone loved it.

Made this as a bonus for Recipe Swap #14.  Since I had a Costco package of frozen s/b/thighs, and THOUGHT there were 6, I doubled the ingredients, using 2 cans Cannelloni beans, and @ 1 cup of leftover organic tomato/red pepper soup.  What I THOUGHT was frozen turkey kielbasa, turned out to be chorizo -- but I used it anyway !  I added only a small amount (for me) salt and pepper, expecting DH to want a few shakes of hot sauce - but it was perfect as it was !!  It was a truly winter comfort-food meal, with a refrigerated Pizza dough, prepared as FlatBread, topped with - evoo, garlic, herbs, shallots, and parmesan. Thanks Paula for TWO delicious and easy meals.

omg this was AWESOME! so DELICIOUS but so easy to make. my spice sensitive husband didn't think it was too spicy at all. just perfect for him so i'm glad i chose not to cut back. i did sub chicken w/ super thin slices of beef since my husband loves beef pho. this will definitely go into our favorites folder and will make many times! thanks for sharing!

Wow! These were splendid. I did half a recipe and got 3 burgers. I did use dried beans and lentils, however when I went to mash them with the potato masher I couldn't so I broke out the wand/stick blender (a.k.a. immersion blender) which worked VERY well. These were quite spicy the jalapeno I used ended up providing around 2 1/2 Tbsp of jalapenos. I took the onion, garlic, and jalapeno and whirled them in the mini-food processor until they were as small as it could get them (much smaller than I could cut them). I had a little trouble keeping the patties together :-( but I don't care these were AMAZING! I think I might even serve them as a breakfast sausage alternative with eggs this weekend :-) I used whole wheat buns then put red onion, tomato and mayo on them. I think next time I would use cheddar cheese too.

WOW! This is excellent, as good as any pub in South Boston on St. Patty's Day.  I will never make corned beef and cabbage in a pot or crock pot again.  the only thing I did different was cook the veggies for 10 mins instead of 6.
I'm in the middle of a blizzard here in Ohio and I wanted to make biscuits.  I then realized I had no baking powder.  What a life saver this was!

DBF and I both love this dish.  I am making it for the second time today.  I am using mission figs because that is what I have.  The sauce is so delicious over couscous.  I am thinking of making up ig dump bags of this to freeze so that if I have a busy day I can just put one in the crock pot before I go to work.

I marinated the chicken all day and I think that a bit of salt in the marinade would be a good idea. That said the lemon and oregano flavor is very nice. I used whole,bite size, Yukon Gold's that were perfectly roasted when the chicken came out of the oven.  I used one thigh and had a very nice dinner. Thanks Marra for a small sized meal. Made for Photo Tag.

This recipe certainly gave my spice rack a workout, but amazingly I had everything already and only had to buy the kale.  It was my first attempt at making anything with kale, too, and I was glad to find that it could be eaten raw (as DH hates most cooked veggies).  DH gave it his seal of approval by asking for the leftovers the next day.  Definitely will be making this again. [Edit: After making a second time, and having DH go back for seconds (unheard of for a veggie dish) I've decided to make up a mix of the spices so I don't have to get all 11 spice bottles out every time, since I'm going to be making this a lot.  I multiplied every ingredient from allspice to cloves by 6 (3 tsp, 2 tsp, 1 1/2 tsp, and 3/4 tsp respectively for each set of amounts) and mixed them all together.  For each time I make the recipe, I will use about 4 tsp of the mix.  It will save time, and remove the guesswork involved since I don't own a 1/3 teaspoon.]

Very good!  I substituted a combo of white and peanut butter chips for the butterscotch and it turned out great.  I also sifted it through my colander before putting it into a storage container- just to shake off some of the excess sugar.

Simply delicious!!! My only suggestion would be using a thicker (homemade) crust.  Your 'terminology' had me in giggles as well but your recipe turned out great. Of all the Key Lime Pies I've eaten, tried, created -  THIS particular recipe has the consistency I prefer. (I live in South Florida - Key Lime pie is a MUST, lol) -Thanks!!
I don't know how but my local grocery store had no corn beef, so I had to use turkey.  It still turned out great! I also used my own homemade thousand island dressing! Thanks for posting.

We really liked this soup.  I will definately be making it again.  This time I didn't change anything, but I look forward to experimenting with different flavors of brats and beer.  Thanks for sharing!

I loved the fact that we could have such a hearty, nutritious meal with this on a weeknight!!  It was so easy to prepare.  I used water in place of the white wine but followed the recipe other than that.  The meat was tender & juicy.  Because I had such a terrible cold, I left the flavour rating up to my husband & he gave it two thumbs up!!

The fries tasted great; however, we had problems with the cooking time.  We found that they took 1 hour altogether. 10 minutes covered and 50 minutes uncovered, and even then they could of cooked a bit longer. We are at an altitude of 1,000.  They taste delicious though!

Really delicious, and so simple! I will use this recipe again and again for those busy days when I haven't planned dinner ahead of time. A nice sweet/savory combination (but not too sweet) with the brown sugar and onion soup. My whole family loved this.
Very easy and very good. Next time I'll double the garlic cloves, as suggested by Principessa. I love garlic, and want a stronger garlic presence next time. Thanks for a great recipe!

Excellent quick weekday meal!  I used London Broil instead of flank steak which worked well.  The only difference I made in the recipe was to not cook all the pink out of the beef, just because that's the way we like it!  I think the addition of red pepper flakes is a great idea and will try that next time we make it. Also maybe some mushrooms. A definite keeper.  Thanks for sharing!

great mac and cheese, I used an aged white cheddar and also added in a small chopped onion and a tablespoon of fresh minced garlic to the roux, this is a rich cheesy dish that has a wonderful flavor, thanks for sharing Bird!

I used Smart Balance rather than butter. I also added 1/2 teaspoon baking powder to the recipe. We opted to use pecans. These brownies are fantastic! The best recipe I've ever made! We wanted mocha frosting, so I added 3 teaspoons instant decaf coffee granules to the evap milk for the frosting recipe. Divine!!! Try these. You won't be disappointed!  :)

I made this recipe for dinner tonight, however im not going to rate it because we really didn't like it at all, but I don't think its the recipe..I just don't think we care for the game-ier taste of chicken thighs.  I think next time Im going to use this technique for chicken breasts instead.   Thanks for posting!

Excellent no fuss jam!  I had loads of plums to use up, so I ended up with a mix of Aussiebelle, Tegan Blue, Angelino and Mid Red plums, which I peeled, so the colour came out a bit more of a golden orange than the red/purple of the recipe.  Very tasty!  Thanks Mary!

Excellent rib recipe!!  I used Sweet Baby Rays sauce.  I simmered for only about 40 minutes and then put in the oven to bake.  I was worried because once I had it in the oven I read other reviewer suggestion of simmering at least double the time I had but could put back into the pot because I already had smothered the ribs in my only bottle of BBQ sauce.  I compensated by lowering the baking temp and cooking that an hour and a half and they still turned out tender!  Next time though I will heed other reviewers advice and go longer on the simmering part and I want to try it with Jack Daniels No7 sauce as my husband prefers it.  Really good and this is the way I plan on cooking ribs from now on.  Thank you, JoAnn!!
very good! i sauted it with oil. and lef out the cumin. but will had (didn't have any). thanks for sharing!!!

We loved this black bean burger. Even my  4 yr old daughter ate it and she usually shuns new foods. I mostly followed the recipe, but added a little minced garlic. Next time, I plan to use more salsa. The burgers held together well for me.

What a neat new way to have hamburgers! We loved these! I used 1/2 ground beef  and 1/2 ground turkey to make the patties. As it is still cold out, I broiled the patties instead of using the grill, but otherwise made as directed. I also used whole wheat tortillas and fat free sour cream. Delicious idea for a week-night supper! Thanks for sharing!

This is very good and flavorful.  I followed ingredients as per recipe.  I cooked this in my crockpot while I was away all day.  It was a little watery so I let it thicken before serving it.  I served the gravy over penne pasta. Made for USA Tag.

I made it exactly according to the recipe and it was fabulous.  Great appearance, flavor and texture!  We had it as a midnight snack, but next time, I'll incorporate it into a dinner. This is a keeper!

The soup was a quick and easy way to use up stuff right out of my pantry. But instead of using chicken and cellophane noodles, i just opted for silken tofu which I did fry for a bit before i added the stock. And to my amazement, it tasted just as good. The basil definitely brought the flavors of Vietnam into it.

YUM and so easy.  I did include an additional two cups of water; I was planning on this being a main meal for the three of us and three and half cups of broth didn't look like it was going to go very far.  In any event, this soup was very good and very easy.  This is the first time I have cooked using cellophane noodles and they're quite tasty is soup; DS was perplexed about what they are made of and decided that he really enjoys the mung bean noodles.  The fresh herbs are a must!  Made for Stone Soup Game.

This makes  a very nice french toast LL. It was very quick and easy and the french toast was light and fluffy,  with lots of flavour. I've never made french toast with flour before and wasn't sure what to expect. It gave the french toast a lovely crust. I served mine with a little butter and icing sugar and  I didn't miss the syrup. I will be making these again, soon. Thanks so much for sharing.
I followed the recipe to a T.  Marinated overnight, squeezed fresh orange and lime and all the spices.  However, we all thought it was a good recipe, not great.  Thank you.
I made this for a family dinner with my DD and her boyfriend. I added some chopped scallions, a little sour cream, and parsley. Everyone loved it! Thank you!
Good, but next time I will make sure the butter and sugar melt together before adding the dates.  And I may use less sugar next time as well.
Made this for my customers this week. Everyone loved it!! This is easy and very, very good!!!

Thank you for this recipe! I made the super cut down version. All I had handy was Dr. Pepper and Sweet Baby Rays Bar-b-que sauce. So I went for it with just the Dr. Pepper and sauce, I can't begin to tell you how super yummy these were. Very tender, hint of sweet and melt in your mouth. I'm definately making them again.
This is a great to make when you are running low on groceries or wondering what to have for dinner. It's a quick and delicious dinner with items you always have in the pantry.

Everyone liked these tonight.  I used light sour cream and 3 teaspoons of the taco seasoning.  Since the chicken was cold,  I decided to bake the enchiladas for 45 minutes and I cover the pan with foil.  Thank you for posting.  Made for *Potluck Tag* game 2008 for the *Mexican  Fiesta Party*

This was good and simple to make. I didn't have strawberries or pineapple, so I used mango and dried cranberries. i left out the sugar because I used vanilla rice milk and sweetened dried cranberries. I sprinkled unsweetened coconut on top as a garnish.
I doubled recipe, only used 34 cup of milk, 3 eggs & a little cheese on top ! It's our first taste of spinach like this and we liked it. thanks!

Oh yum!!  I've made this simple recipe several times and have a few tips.  Use red (tart) cherry pie filling; dark sweet cherry filling seems dull compared to the normal red cherry. Be sure to avoid a sugar-free pie filling as the cake won't rise as high or taste as good.    Originally I saw the same recipe in a Cake Doctor cookbook but she called for 1/2 tsp. of almond extract.  I use this and sometimes a full tbs. of vanilla for a cherry-vanilla flavor.  This also works in two 8" or 9" layer pans but reduce oven time by 5-10 minutes.

These really didn't work out for me. While there was a delicious cheesy cumin smell while they were in the oven, the end result was mostly greasy, too short to be pleasant to eat. Obviously some people have made them successfully. I think the problem may be with the "cheese spread" ingredient - there are lots of different sorts of cheese spreads, and probably I picked the wrong one.

I halved the recipe, and made s'kat's "Fresh Baguette" dough for these. I put about 1/6 cup spaghetti sauce and a generous pinch of cheese. These are fabulous! They were super easy to make and freeze, and a great meal. 

The one thing I would be careful of is how much bread you use. The dough I used made the calzones very doughy--five bites before the filling! Next time, I'll make six instead of five. But thanks!

We really enjoyed this, made chicken and rice tacos out of it, added a slight amount of mozeralla cheese on top. Only changes I made were to use black bean and corn salsa (yummy!) and no mushrooms. I also took another reviewer's suggestion and added basil.  I think next time I may try using  shredded rotisserie chicken pieces, or even just plain shredded chicken. Very good recipe!!

This was great rice!  I loved it!  I made this with the green chilies instead of jalapenos because that is what I had on hand and I also microwaved my rice instead of baking because I was in a time crunch to get dinner on the table.  It came out wonderful!  So keep that in mind if your oven is already full.  We had this as a side dish with tacos and it was perfect.  Thank you for sharing!

FANTASTIC!!! I didn't add the melted caramel, but would that add extra pizzazz! I also used Apple Pucker instead of the beretntzens. I made double for each shaker full, and I think I mixed 4 shakers last night. I think we have a new favorite here!

these were yummy.  Tried to put a fancy piping thingy in the bag but it kept popping out so i just piped stright from the bag.  the pickle juice just made it fantaticly different.  
thanks

Delicious and super easy. I have never tried an Irish Soda Bread, so I don't have anything to compare it to, but my entire family LOVED it! I followed the recipe except I did not put on the caraway seeds (I'm not a fan of them). The bread tasted great warm with butter! I can't wait to have some more in the morning! Thanks for the recipe!!

This was really good. Definately a simple way to eat a Pho style soup. I served it with fresh rice (pho style) noodles and used some leftover grilled chicken thighs. That reduced some of the prep and cook time. Was simple and a nice way to "Cheat n' Eat" Pho. Also added some Hoisin w/ the Sriracha. Thanks for sharing. Made for Stone Soup game.

This is definately the best thing that can be done with cucumbers. Next time I will add more chili. I used shallots instead of scallions and a mix of tarragon, oregano and rosemary in the absence of basil. Still loved it.

Rich and delicious dark chocolate cake that turned out as great as all previous 168 ratings! My DD boyfriend loves dark chocolate cake with chocolate frosting so I made this - my very first scratch chocolate cake. It was very easy and although were lots of warnings about the thinness of the batter, I was still surprised and nervous (I used 3.4 cup boiling water) about just how thin the batter is. No need to worry though, this cake turned out great! I frosted it with the medium version of Recipe #89207.
i used non fat spray and not fat butter and grilled in the pan and it turned out great.....thanks
Absolutely wonderful.  So creamy and delicious!  A definite keeper.
I normally make Corned Beef and Cabbage in the crockpot but since making this recipe I won't any more.  The corned beef just fell apart it was so tender. Yummy :)
Super easy to make and a nice alternative to a Reuben sandwich when you have a taste for one.
I didn't have greek oregano so I used plain oregano plus a little bit of greek spices.  It's delicious.  And I will try it on the bbq this summer.  Thanks Toni :)  Made for Zaar Star Game.

This was enjoyable. My only complaint was that the flavor of the dressing was too subtle. I had 2 lbs. of meat, so I doubled the amount of dressing and teriyaki sauce, but you could barely taste either. 
I used thin Chinese noodles instead of the linguine.
I will probably make this again, as it was super easy and tasty, but I will add more dressing.

I've never had strata before and made this as a special brunch for BF and myself.  It was very easy to put together and I made just as written.  I might try to add some fresh herbs to the egg/milk mixture as we felt that it needed just a bit more kick...maybe a little cayenne would be good too.  Or I might double the spinach/pancetta.onion mixuture and do another couple of layers of that.  Very nice dish though.  Thanks for sharing!

This is a great method for preparing corned beef. Make sure the water covers the meat. It is easiest to remove the fat layer after the meat is cooked. I cooked the vegetables separately, so they wouldn't absorb as much fat and salt. Delicious!
I made this for my friend's birthday party and everyone loved it! Now I'm looking for an excuse to make a cake again because this is absolutely delicious!!!!!!!!

I made this yesterday & have just cut it for morning tea.  Made with spelt flour (half white & half wholemeal) & had to add 1/3 cup pineapple juice to give it enough moisture.  Otherwise I followed directions & the result was lovely.  The bread is a beautiful consistency, with the nuts giving it a nice crunch.  The flavour of the spelt flour overpowered the pineapple a bit, but it still tastes great, especially served with cream cheese.  Thanks Elmotoo for sharing this recipe.  Made for Aus/NZ Recipe Swap #14 for the Tassie Devils.

I love eggplant parmigiana, but I've never made anything with eggplant before.  So when I found this recipe that looked so easy and low in fat, I used it as the basis for Eggplant (Aubergine) and Ziti Parmesan
Recipe #3653.

However, do not do as one reviewer suggested and use parchment paper rather than baking spray.  One side of my eggplant slices stuck to the paper and lost all the coating.  Use the spray and put directly on a loaf pan.
What can I say, Looks like a Guinness but taste so much better.  Instead of making the Irish cream foamy, I just layered it like the do in the Irish pubs in Europe. Thanks for such a great shot.
We served this last night for dinner and enjoyed it.  It is an interesting rub.  We followed Uncle Bill's suggestion and added garlic cloves and fresh rosemary. Thanks for posting.
This made a nice light lunch today! I used Recipe#134299 for the salad dressing, couldn't find my roasted almonds, so used sliced almonds instead. Thank you!

Yum! Another Bread winner here. I knew after trying your pumpkin Bread I would love this. Only change I made was added a little cinnamon and sugar to the top of batter before baking! Thanks for another great recipe. (Made for Bevy Tag 3/08) ~V

Absolutely WONDERFUL!  We were blown away by how delicious this turned out.  The ONLY thing I would do differently, would be to add 3-4 more carrots.  The carrots were so delicious but there weren't enough of them!  THANKS for sharing this recipe.

Oh boy. I don't know what I did wrong or if these just weren't our thing, but they did not turn out at all. My husband wouldn't even eat them and he'll pretty well eat anything. Sorry. Just not for us.

This was a very easy to prepare recipe.  I served this to a group from work and it was very tasty.  I did take the liberty of adding 1/4 tsp of basil, 1/4 tsp of oregano and 1/2 tsp of seasoning salt.  I think I also added more orzo then the recipe called for (I just eye balled it).  Instead of the vegetable mix, I just added all frozen corn.  Thank you for sharing your recipe, I will use it again in the future.

I made these as a snack for the family the other night.  We love the combinations of flavor, but I think I squeezed the spinach way too dry, because the puffs weren't as moist as I'd like, so when I make them again I'll make sure the batter has a little more liquid in it.  I also froze some and they came out wonderful after reheating.  Thanks for posting this great recipe.
These were quick and easy and the kids really enjoyed eating them.  The filling possibilities are endless.  Thanks for posting.
These were good. They were easy to make. I didn't have spicy brown mustard, so I used horseradish mustard instead. Thanks CE!! Made for the Mar '08 Bevy Tag game.
So easy to make and absolutely delicous. Made it for St Patrick's Day dinner and my guests absolutely LOVED it. So much so that I've been asked to make it again for an upcoming dinner party.

I love this method of cooking country style ribs.  They were full of flavor, fork-tender and juicy.  I was out of Dr. Pepper and tried this recipe with two bottles of IBC Root Beer.  It was a great substitute, as I have made root beer-based BBQ sauce before as well.  Don't be afraid to try root beer!  I used KC Masterpiece sauce and baked in the oven.  Will definitely make again.  Updated 3-21-08:  I prepared the recipe with a liter of Dr. Pepper (had 5 lbs of ribs) and finished them off in my Cameron Stove Top Smoker using 2 Tblspn mesquite chips, and basted with a light coat of Head Country BBQ sauce for 40 minutes on medium heat.  The result was super smoky, tender, delicious ribs.  YUM.

Even northerners like me will appreciate these tasty greens.  Having never eaten collard greens before, I was a bit skeptical.  But they were yummy.  Thanks, TasteTester, for explicit and easy directions.  Look at how much Vitamin A is in this recipe!
Nice moist texture, but not really sweet enough.

second time that i'm making this week.  absolutely fabulous recipe.  i added onions, cause i love onions, and because i purchased such a large brisket, doubled the spice recipe, with on hand seeds and spices.  THANKS!  was diligently searching for a great corned beef in pressure cooker recipe.  PERFECT!

These are a fun cookie but oh so messy when coming out of the oven.  Just remember to leave on the cookie sheet to cool at least 10 minutes.  I'd say it's from the marshmellows.  Next time I'd cut the amount used in 1/2 or omit entirely.  I had the hardest time getting them off the cookie sheet in one piece.  Still very good despite.  Thanks for posting!
This is a great and easy recipe. I added a layer of melted milk chocolate chips on top when it had cooled in the fridge! Tastes just like the real thing!
WOW!  I love this pudding!  I used just a little bit of sugar and some extra lemon and it turned out great!    Delicious!
This didn't deam much like Tandoori to me.  It dind't even turn red.  I cooked it in my stoneware pan to try to make it more authentic.  the flavors were good, but tandoori is suppose to be red.

Made as directed except I added 1 clove of minced garlic & used cheddar cheese as that is what I had on hand.  I think mine overbaked a little tho, cuz it was drier than I expected.  DH loved it tho and I will absolutely make it again!

This was a wonderful side for the vege fajitas I made for dinner tonight.  I used arborio rice instead of long grain because that is how I usually make risotto.  Quite yummy; I can imagine this with many variations!
Very good.  This is your basic deviled egg and will draw a crowd and no complaints at any potluck.  Made for Beverage Tag's Green, Eggs, and Ham event March 2008.
Great cake all the way around.  I will be making this one often!

First, I think it's unfair for reviews to dock stars on this because it may lack pockets like store-bought pita bread; that's not the point of this bread! That said, this is wonderful, light pita bread like the kind sold at my local farmers' market, but homemade & better! I used 2 cups whole wheat flour, 1 cup white, and olive oil. I used my cast iron skillet, and kept a barely damp towel on hand, thickly folded, to sweep up the burning excess flour after each one. I also dusted  off as much excess flour as I could before putting in the skillet. I think rolling them out thinner (less than 1/4 inch) makes for more bubbles/air pockets.
Baked a ham for Easter enjoyed every bite of it, a great sweet taste spicey favior, added this one to my cookbook.  Thanks ;0)

I love this cake.  It's the first chocolate cake, or any cake for that matter, I've ever made that hasn't come from a box and it turned out beautifully.  I iced it with mint icing and chocolate frosting.  I don't see a reason to ever make another box cake again.  Thank you so very much for sharing such a delicious recipe.

These were delicious and easy ! Took them to Easter and received raves! I did precook the wrappers the nite before, then in the morning I made meat mixture, placed them on a cookie sheet, added the cheese and then transported them and heated them there. Then put them out with the salsa, sour cream, etc. for everyone to garnish their own. How simple and easy ! Not a one left!
Thankyou!

This was easily the most popular dessert I served with my Easter dinner (I made three).  It got comments such as, "best dessert ever", "almost heaven", etc.  It looked perfect and the sauce was fabulous.  Thanks for sharing!
This was fantastic!  I made this today for Easter dinner, and DH just loved it!  (He can be hard to please!)  We will defenitly make this again!  Thanks for the great recipe!  Yum!

This is a great tasting dessert. I had trouble with the sauce, it would not brown up for me. However, after playing around a bit I did end up with a nice sauce that tasted sensational. Not a speck was left on anyone's plate. Thanks for sharing your wonderful recipe.
I added some garlic to the butter and the oysters tasted close to Acme Oyster House in New Orleans. I agree you can use less butter and cheese. These oysters are great!

Oh wow this is an outstanding coffee cake it is so spongey and moist family and friends love it i am baking another one today for easter.ok actually 2 cause im keeping one here and taking one.Very goog thank you for the recipe.Cindy
Just slices of leek and potato swimming in bland milk "sauce". Disappointing :(

These were devileggdelicious!!! I loved the addition of the dill pickle juice. I added a bit of dried chives as well. I will definitely make these again. I made mine using both techniques, adding mixture to a plastic bag with a star tip and piped into the eggs. Made them very pretty and EGGSTRA SPECIAL!
Made For Green Eggs & Ham March Bevy Tag 09 - thanks for sharing! ~V
Very good deviled eggs!  I used just a drip of pickle juice so that it wouldn't overpower, but gave some flavor.  Then I sprinkled with paprika.  Thanks for posting!

I had some crab cakes that I bought from Trader Joe's, but loved the idea of the Basil Aioli to go with it. So, I just made that portion of the recipe. It was really good and complemented the crab cakes nicely! Thank you so much for posting!

Delicious and SO easy!  I used 10 oz mushrooms, and 1/3 cup of barley.  I also used only 1 tablespoon of reduced-fat margarine, to cut out some fat and cals.  This was so wonderful with tuna melts for supper.  DH added parmesan cheese.

This was a good side dish.  I only ended up using 1 1/2 cups cheese as it was enough for our tastes!  I used Italian flavored diced tomatoes and didn't realize I was out of parsley so I just used Italian Seasonings which consisted of Thyme and Oregano.  It was good and a nice change from the rice pilaf I usually make.  I also stirred in some sliced green onions when I stirred in the cheese.  Tasty!
Fabulous sauce that matches Broccoli perfectly. I just love the splash of lemon at the end. Actually this would be excellent over any steamed green veggie.
I liked dipping my baked potato in this sauce!

The dressing is marvelous!  In addition to the mushrooms, I threw in some sliced celery and cucumber for crunch.  I removed the tough stems from the watercress and ran my knife through them.  Thanks for sharing!!
This was very good.  I only had a 29oz can of tomatoes so I made one and a half times the recipe except for the cheese-only had 2 cups.  Thanks for a really tasty recipe!

Excellent!  Tasted exactly like Magic Shell.  I followed the recipe exactly, using 60% cacao bittersweet chocolate chips.  I made this for my sister's birthday party and received rave reviews from adults and kids.  Also, made this for my husband's birthday party with butter rather than margarine and semi sweet chocolate chips.  This was very good, but not as wonderful and exact as the bittersweet and margarine.  Super quick recipe with awesome results!
This recipe really hit the spot with my family for our Easter dinner.  We had along with ham and garlic mashed potatoes, and everyone left the table really happy!  These are a great addition anytime!

This is very similar to a recipe my father gave me and I made last night. Ingrediants are the same, with the exception of 4X the sherry, but I thought mine needed more anyway, so no argument there. I added 1 c. shredded cheddar to the white sauce before folding in the crab, then sprinkled more on top while baking. Also sprinkled paprika just for looks. 

Thanks for saving me the effort of posting it. Can be served as a hearty dip with toasted baguette slices.
The frosting was just heavenly. The cake was a little bit dry, but overall the taste was fabulous. Definitely a keeper!

I made this for Easter/ Birthday for my 8 yr old daughter. It was easy, delicious and impressive looking. My favorite kind of recipe! It is definitely a keeper. I can see myself making it often. I can't wait to try it with other fresh fruits this summer (blueberries, peaches).
I have a simular coating mix but I'll try this one too!

I've made these once before and they were amazing. Like Sharon and LUv 2 BaKE, we changed it up a little. I use Zatarain's yellow rice instead of quiona. We also use Bocca crumbles and salsa in them. I suppose you could use whatever you like best. Thanks for putting your version on here though!

I gotta tell you..instead of chicken wings i used cut up pork tenderloin.  I made the sauce exactly as the recipe says but with the pork and it was fantastic.  I too served it with rice and my father who is hard to please thought it was great too.  Thanks for the recipe.  I will be making it again.  I will also try it with the chicken.  Fantastic.

Wonderful, I used this recipe to make a lime soymilk pudding. The texture is perfect, and you'll know when it's thickened when cooking it, it thickens all of a sudden :). Definitely a favorite and makes a great base for any other soymilk pudding. I served this topped with a couple raspberries and a sprig of mint.

I never write reviews, but this was so goooooood I just had to tell you!  I've cooked for my husband for 27 years and he always eats anything, usually with no comments, but tonight he said "this is really good!"  Flavorful and rich, the spices, fresh asparagus and mushrooms complimented the leftover ham and was wonderful on our pasta.  Thank you!
Made these for Easter, they were very good, though I would have liked them to be a little more soft, though I should have shaken up the coconut milk before opening.

I have tried several cupcake recipes and this one is my favorite. I ended up making them two days in a row because there was so much extra frosting. The only thing I did differently was that I didn't add the coconut to the batter. The texture and flavor is really great. My co-workers devoured them. Thanks for the delicious reipe!
This made a yummy, easy breakfast, Thanks! :)
Thankyou so much I have always wanted to know how to do this. Now my chicken BBQ's will be spectacular!

awesome!!!
i just got done making the fantasic chicken and its absolutly deeeeeelicious!!!
i made strips out of chicken breast and used french herb rub instead of msg cause i dont know were to get the stuff,but all in all this is really "finger licken' good"!!
somehow mine got away with me and the bottom of the pressure cooker burned but it still tasted fabulous after I cut off the burnt fat.

An awesome soup! I made it exactly as written...except for changing the serving for 6 ( we only have 5 in the family, but I wanted to have some the next day for lunch). The fish sauce smells awful, but it tastes great. Don't be deterred...everyone (even the 12 and 3 year old) though it was delicious (except my 11 year old who doesn't like ginger) and we will certainly have it again. Also, this has an amazingly low calorie count, but is surprisingly filling. Fantastic!
I'm sorry...this recipe bombed in my home.  I made it according to the specs. but it just tasted bland.  The chicken needed to be marinated or something ... this was not restaurant quality.

A wonderful flavored dish!  I doubled the garlic, used fat free yogurt and omitted the cilantro as a matter of personal taste.  I prepared the marinade in the morning & let it 'visit' with the chicken until that evening before DH grilled it.  The flavor was subtle but very satisfying and the chicken was perfectly moist and tender.
I froze three cooked breasts and thawed two in the fridge this morning before heating in the microwave for our lunch.  The flavor was just as good as the day they were grilled and DH commented that he often finds frozen chicken to be dry but this one was not.
I probably wouldn't use this as a "dump" OAMC recipe because I'd be afraid the yogurt would separate.  A braver soul might want to try it.
Next time I might double the spices just because we love the combination of flavors.  I bet chicken tenders would be great marinaded in this one, too!
All in all a keeper both for a quick dinner, and I'll make extra knowing the leftovers can successfully be frozen.
Made for "Freezer Tag March 2008"
My DH really liked this pudding..Was easy to make. I used 2% milk and some old hershey kisses that had been lying around,in the cupboard ...It had a nice texture and flavor..I will make this again..

It's recipes like this that make me wonder why people even bother with box mixes! Not only is this cake rich, moist, and delicious, it takes less than five minutes to measure and mix the ingredients and pop it into the oven. I made this cake in a bundt pan and bucking tradition, I frosted it with Recipe #89207. It turned out wonderfully. I will be making this cake for many occasions, thanks sooo much for sharing this quick and simple recipe!

Addition: I made this a second time and replaced the boiling water with boiling strong-brewed coffee and man, it turned out twice as good as the first time around! This time I glazed it with Recipe #89594 using semi-sweet chocolate. Amazing, simple, and tasty!

The family is split on this one. Everyone agrees that the chicken was delicious (DS#1 would have increased the intensity of the flavors if he could). Two of us liked the potatoes. Three thought they were sort of bland and somehow missing something.
I made 9 chicken leg quarters in a quadruple batch of marinade (soaked about 4 hours), and potatoes. The only thing I could think that might have improved the dish would be to add onions as it baked. Note -- It doesn't say whether to cook covered or uncovered so I cooked it covered for half an hour then uncovered it for another half hour to brown.
These were so good. I followed the recipe exactly and it came out perfectly.

We made this to top our Easter dessert & it hardened very nicely & quicker than I thought it would. The taste is better than Magic Shell, so I'll be using this a lot this summer. Thanks for another keeper!
We Love! this recipe, I end up using more mayo, but I buy the heathy stuff so I feel good about it. We serve it with fresh tomato's, onions, and herbs and risotto. So good!

This was very tasty cake! I was a bit worried when I added the water because the batter was quite thin. However, I poured it into the tins and it turned out fine. I did use 8" tins despite the warnings and they didn't overflow (but almost!). I had issues getting one layer out of the tin but that was my fault and not the recipe's. This was very good!
oh these are incredible.  Really tasty, moist and the glaze is great too.  I used 1/2 cup of splenda brown sugar blend instead of the 1 cup brown sugar
forget about the rice! this is a great late night snack!  I did thicken the sauce a bit with some cornstarch and poured over top for dipping! yummy
yummy! thanks for a lovely birthday cake for my friend. used 3/4 cup boiling water, and it was lovely, moist and chocolate-y. =)

I had really mixed feelings about this soup.  On the one hand it was easy to make and I almost always have the ingredients on hand. On the other hand, I had to add a LOT of salt.  First I tried adding more sun-dried tomatoes and some balsamic vinegar but it was still kind of bland, so in went the salt. Also, the farfalle really sucked up a lot of broth.  I think orzo or ditalini would be a better choice for the pasta unless you're going to eat the entire batch right away.
I love this recipe.  I always add lots of banana's and walnuts.  Makes a nice refreshing dessert.

So easy and quick to make.  I used broccoli, carrots, red pepper, and red onions, as well as olives and fresh mozzarella cheese.  I would have used tomatoes and cucumbers as well except that I was serving it alongside another salad that was full of those.  When I first made it and tasted it, the dressing seemed overwhelming, but after it had mellowed in the fridge half the day, it was just barely enough dressing to be nice and flavorful.

I actually got Dh to make this and it was great.  One admonition not to burn the garlic was all the direction it took.  Every man should have a pasta dish in his repertoire, wouldn't you agree, ladies?

I found the ginger bite to be stronger than I really enjoy here. For diabetic reasons I used skim milk and Splenda. Possibly whole milk and real sugar would have tempered it better? I'm glad I tried it and I'll likely make it again but with less ginger. Thanks for posting Bethie.
This was a great salad.  I used craisins, organic pre-made salad mix, and Kraft toasted sesame dressing.  Fantastic!
Nice flavor change from the usual.  I doubled the recipe and DH gobbled them up.  Made for the Beverage Tag Game.

Ive never made salsa before so this was a nice chance in pace (no pun intended lol). I mixed everything up around 10 am and served it on the side of some homemade tacos around 6. I split it up into two batches, one with only alittle bit of a jalapeno and the other with the majority of the jalapeno plus half of another. It was perfect and so much fresher then canned or jar salsa, especially with some produce stand fresh jersey tomatos. Made for Aussie Swap 14

This was a good, quick meal.  I left out the spinach bcz kids hate it and the mushrooms bcz DH hates them, so I used 1/2 of the olive oil, lots of garlic and more mozzarella.  I think we prefer the gnocchi with a red sauce, so would make it again, but adding in the sauce.  Made for Spring '08 PAC.

I'm changing my rating from 4 to 5 stars--this is a dish that I crave regularly. and my family (sister and parents) loved this! I think there will still be some fiddling with the recipe in the future, but it is really good. as suggested by ncmysteryshopper, we added red bell pepper (next time, I'll add more like a 1/2 cup), and then we added about 1/4-1/3 cup of cocktail peanuts just before serving. and for the benefit of new cooks: 1 lime=about 3 tbsp of juice (very important to use enough). also, heating the water for pasta while you cook the chicken seems to work out so that the pasta will be done just as the chicken and sauce is. the sauce should be added to the chicken in the pan and heated just to boiling to thicken the sauce, and then the cilantro and chives should be added.
This cheesecake was so delicious! I had my doubt about how it would turn out, because it was so easy. This is definitely one that I'll make again!

Excellent recipe for a beginning cooker.  I liked it very much, except for the eggplant slices that contained seeds.  These slices had a really bad taste.  Would salting and sweating them help?  I know the problem wasn't the recipe because the slices that I cut from the ends of the eggplant didn't contain seeds, and these slices tasted excellent.

This was so tasty! The 'peanutty' taste was so much better than I expected, since I didn't know what to expect with the peanut butter AND peanuts. As with another comment, checked half way through and I wasn't convinced... but by the end of the 4 hours it was lovely and creamy!! 
I served it with some homemade rustic flatbread and homous.
Probably could do with adding some veg, maybe I'll try it with green beans or something next time.
Quick and delicious. But I'd suggest half the fish sauce.

Thanks Miss Annie!  We love Luby's and their liver and onions is awesome!  My husband said it tasted JUST LIKE LUBY"S! The liver I bought was sliced a little thicker--I think that thinner is better--but it was great anyway.  Thank you!

Really enjoyed the choc cake. and also the baking experience. I use 1 cup of sugar instead of 2 out of preference. and I like it that way. to avoid any sticking on the 13x9, i lined up parchments which get rid of the fuss of sticking batter, and baked for 45 minutes. i added in 2 tbsp of Milo which turns out to be great. The batter was thin after the hot water was added up. if you're scared for the batter to be too thin, then use 3/4 boiling water. beat it, and toss it in the oven. don't think about it. it will turn out great at the end.

Awesome.  I marinated them for about 30 hours and they were so tasty!!!!  I have to admit that I cooked them in the microwave. . .yes the microwave. . .for 11 minutes on power level 7, turning half way.  They were super moist and juicy.  On top of that, they produced a wonderful chicken broth that I thickened up with cornstarch and used as a sauce.  OMG it was so good!  Next time I will have some mushrooms and capers ready to throw in my sauce.  A true keeper!

Nice alternative to broccoli salad!  I substituted low fat mayo and reduced the sugar slightly, and it still came out great.  We loved the flavour the Parmesan added to the salad.  I found that I didn't need all of the dressing.  There's enough left to make another half salad later in the week.  Yum!  Thanks pollyw!  Made for PAC Spring 2008.
This was very good. I omitted the cilantro and used dried tarragon instead. The chicken was very moist and flavorful. Thanks for the recipe!
Nice change from the tomato-paste based sauce that I usually do. I did cook it longer than intended because we are not real chunky tomato fans. Good recipe!

This is similar to the recipe my mom used to make and taught me to make except instead of celery seeds she used diced celery and she'd boil the potatoes with their jackets on. She also said that you couldn't get the right texture if you used a spoon - it had to be with your hands mushing through all the stuff! 
I smiled at how the originator rattled off the ingredients without exact measurements, my mom used to cook the same way.

Truthfully it is the best potato salad EVER!!
Yummy! I used 1/2 the mayo. Skipped the juice. Just a touch of relish which gave a bit of sweetness. Thanks!

just what i was looking for! i used silken style tofu and omitted the 1/2 c water...worked out beautifully.  we enjoyed them as a main meal focus with green salad and hot quinoa.  a couple of choices of chutney and dijon mustard spiced them up a bit...

This was a very flavorful tagine. I only made a couple of changes that didn't affect the integrity of the recipe. I sprinkled paprika, salt, & pepper on the chicken before adding it to the tagine then added the rest of the spices to sauce. I also added potatoes to the dish because my husband likes potatoes in all his tagines. I also sprinkled them with paprika & pepper before adding them.

I love roasted garlic but I never thought of putting the cloves in with the chicken - so easy! I actually just borrowed the idea when roasting a Blasted Chicken (142783) at 425. Unfortunately that was a little too hot and about half the garlic burned, but what was left still tasted great!

Even though I chose to make this recipe (actually I halved it), I had a feeling it'd taste too sweet, but happily I was wrong! It is sweet, but the garlic & lemon blended right in to make this very great tasting! Thanks for sharing! Definitely a keeper! [Made & reviewed for one of my adopted chefs in this Spring's PAC]
This did come out perfect! I used extra virgin olive oil(someday I'll get some grapeseed oil!). Great! Thank you Adams.wifey! Made for Pick a Chef(PAC)!

I was pleasantly surprised!  This is such a great soup, and perfect to suppliment any diet - especially you WW out there!  I like spice, so I used Spicy Hot V8, chopped & de-seeded some jalepenos, extra garlic, and then about 12-14 dashes of Tabasco!  It's a great pick me up!  Thanks for posting!

This was absolutely the best mac and cheese I have ever had.  I loved every bite of it.  I also like the fact that this recipe makes a very manageable amount, unlike many recipes for casseroles that I come across that seem like they came straight out of Elementary School Cafeteria Recipes Monthly. I will be making this one again thanks so much for posting!

I love anthing almond!  These great cookies have a wonderful burst of almond flavor and are slightly chewy.  They brown to a beautiful light golden brown and look so pretty topped with an almond.  Very elegant looking.  I will be adding these to my Christmas baking from now on - this recipe is a winner in my book!

I'm always looking for great tasting ways to get more vegetables into our diet.  This is a really great tasting recipe that not only looks great and tastes great but even gets the kids to eat their vegetables!  I'll be fixing this casserole on regular rotation from now on!
Now this wowed the company! thanks so much for sharing.  used a lb of crabmeat and bit more cream cheese.  YUM YUM

We enjoyed this! I love quinoa and will make it again. I made a couple small changes: 3 cloves garlic, no cauliflower- but more of everything else, real butter, and added a tsp of curry powder and some salt. when i cooked the onion I also added a little sugar to carmelize them- the really had great flavor! I did need to add a whole extra cup of broth to get everything soft and cooked.

This is a delicious soup recipe.  We really enjoyed it and was easy to make.  I did add garlic and nutmeg to taste, otherwise stuck with the recipe.  Thanks so much for posting it, we will certainly be making this again!

Terrific and easy to prepare pie. As you can see from my photo, I made a pie crust instead of the graham cracker crust. I had this dough in the freezer and decided to use it. I also tinted the filling slightly green with just a couple of drops of food coloring. Otherwise, I made it as directed. I adopted velvet_sj as part of the Spring Pick-a-Chef.

yummy! of course, i can't leave anything the way it is, so i added minced garlic, a can of sliced black olives, sliced mushrooms, onion and red bell pepper - i then topped it with shredded cheddar and baked it at 375 until the cheese melted, for about 25-30 minutes. i added in some extra half & half to account for the extra ingredients, used leftover ham and it was delish!  definately a good salsa would make a big difference IMHO. thanks, will make again!
it was good, very moist and soft. i replaced the eggs with 1/2 cup of applesauce and it was still pretty good.

Nice to be able to make a healthier version of mashed potatoes.
I just used the plain cheese and think next time I would use flavoured just to add a little something extra as I felt it was lacking slightly.

I did have to "tweek" it a bit to freeze, based on other freezer pot pie directions I've seen.  To freeze:  First, instead of 1 large pie, I made 4 individual pies, using mini-loaf pans from the supermarket.  Then, I added an extra 1/2 cup of broth (chicken in my case, but vegetable broth would work just fine), for a very liquid-y filling.  Instead of a top and bottom crust, I left the bottom crust off and doubled the top crust - the double crust helped soak up the extra liquid of the filling and, since it was double, still had a chance to get nice and flaky on top, besides. For the double crust:  lay out one crust, brush with beaten egg, and place the second crust over it.  Trace the tins - you can just fit 4 tins on the prepared pie crust; then cut out and cover each individual pie, slash, then brush tops with egg.  Double-wrap with plastic wrap, then place the individual pies in a zip-top freezer bag.  To cook:  Bake directly from frozen on a sheet pan - 40 minutes covered with foil at 375, then uncover and bake an additional half hour.  Let rest 10 minutes before serving.  Very good recipe; we will likely make again.  Thank you.
