The second problem I had was in the frosting.  It was just making a syrup basically and didn't look anything like Lynn's which is what I was basing mine off of lol.  So I added some heavy whipping cream and that really helped.  It also had an odd flavor before adding the cream.  The finished frosting was still on the runny side, but much better.  I also think I could have stretched the batter to make a few more, rather than force it all into 12 liners because I was too lazy to get another pan out lol.  They sorta ran into eachother on top because of this.  For the cupcakes themselves I opted to use the lemon zest as stated, but changed the milk to orange juice as recommended for variations.  The cupcakes had a wonderful flavor with that combo!  Which together with the strawberry icing was phenomenal!  They are a nice moist cupcake thanks to the sour cream.  So as a recap... even though they didn't come out looking perfect, and there were some bumps along the way (possibly my fault) these were still some of the yummiest cupcakes I have tasted!

Quite tasty, easy and creamy, and great with the rice! I did find it rather too gingery, even though I reduced the ginger to about 1 Tbsp or so. But I'm still looking forward to leftovers! I also omitted the chicken for a vegetarian soup. Thanks!
Very, very simple and yummy!  My kids ate it up!

This was so good! Have to admit I was a bit hesitant about doing broccoli this way, but a person must move out of the pot sometimes. LoL! I left out the pepper flakes, as I don't do heat very well. Simple ingredients with maximum flavor. :)

This salad was so delicious! My photo does not come close to doing it justice. The flavor/texture combo is outstanding. Crunchy toasted walnuts, sweet spicy basil, and sharp yummy gorgonzola, with my favorite salad dressing of sweet tangy balsamic drizzled over the top. You might notice the absence of a chicken breast in my photo. I had a beautiful chicken breast cooked off and ready to slice when I went to work this morning. DS stayed home from school, chicken breast disappeared. Do you think there is a connection? ;) Thanks for sharing Sue, all 3 of your recipes I tried for *PAC Spring 2008* were amazing! ~Brenda

These were amazing!
I had gotten coconut milk because my husband wanted to know what it tasted like, and so then I needed a recipe to use it in and this is what he chose.
I made one batch and then he took some to his co-workers and I had to make a second batch because they all wanted some more!  Everything goes together really easily and quickly and the results are wonderful!
I did get 14 cupcakes the first time I made it and then 16 cupcakes the second time I made them... I also only had to bake mine for 20 minutes, but my oven tends to run hot.
The icing was glorious! I had more than I needed for the cupcakes (we aren't big on lots of icing), but that was fine because it tasted great!

This was great! I used small red potatoes and quartered them. They were the perfect size to pop in your mouth. These were as good as I get when I go out to a fancy resturant. Thanks for sharing! This is a new staple in my cookbook!

I made mean chef's version of this with his recipe for chutney. I don't remember where I got it from, maybe recipecircus but this is basically the same recipe and I REALLY love it. I use sweet coconut cause I like most everything sweeter! Great recipe.

Certainly a different egg salad. We enjoyed it warm as well as cold. Both is nice. The caramelized onions makes this little appetizer different and makes you come back for more. Thanks for posting.
made for PAC Spring '08.

Excellent recipe! I used brown rice, wild rice, oats, barley, and flaxseed as the grains, with dried cranberries and whole almonds. I tripled the recipe while using your 3 cups of water to 1 cup of grains rule and it turned out perfectly - it's so great to have a healthy hot cereal before work and not have to spend all morning at the stove. Thanks for the wonderful recipe!
SPRING PAC 2008: I love the simplicity of this dish. The flavor combo is excellent!! Thank you so much for sharing!
Excellent Dish!  Nice and spicy.  I used my iron skillet vs. an electric skillet.  I used part cream and part half-in-half.  We enjoyed truly enjoyed this meal.  Thank you for posting.
Just the way my DH and I like it! I cut the artichokes in half, cut out the fuzzy part and steamed for about 15 minutes. The sauce was very nice! Thank you!
Wow!  Hits the target on all counts!  My name for this is 'Bullseye'.  See my Z-mail Blink.

I made this last night, and we loved it! I loved that it tastes so good, but is so much better for you than frying. I served it with angel hair pasta and marinara sauce, topped with a little extra parmesan cheese. So good, can't wait to make it again. Was quick and easy too--followed the directions to a tee. Thank you for sharing!

I just tried this recipe and can agree on a couple of the previous comments.  They did smell wonderful while baking, and they did taste a lot like cake donuts.  However, something was obviously not right as the batter seemed more like pancake batter than a muffin batter, sothey did not rise up much.  Instead they seemed like little cinnamon hockey pucks...tasty ones tho'.  For those who thought they should taste sweeter, try adding about a teaspoon of vanilla.
Also, if I try these again I would alter it a bit and put a dab of preserves as a middle layer between two blobs of batter.  Then you end up with something tasting like a jelly donut.

Very tasty and oh, so pretty. I did add one can of green chilis (drained) for a little more kick. I'd call this salad "Knockout Salad!" as in it packs a very good punch! I like the beans warm and also room temperature is fine with me.
Perfect!! Made it for my daughter's birthday and it was wonderful.
Very good! I only used a few drops of hot sauce, but my family thought it was still too spicy. Went great with Recipe#18387 and Recipe#284953. Thank-you!

Yes, less is more for this potato salad.   I used red potatoes, but otherwise made this as written.   I insist on eggs and onions in my potato salad, so this was perfect for me, yet without any extra "stuff."  Loved the creaminess from the sour cream.   I'll use this recipe again.  Thanx!

Made for Spring PAC 2008. This was good and easy to make. I followed the recipe exactly as written except I put mine in the baking dish and made on the grill. My chicken was done in about 35 minutes but that might be because of doing it on the grill.

This is a recipe I'll use over and over again as it is just so good and so easy.  I had some very nice tomatoes on the vine and this recipe was a perfect way to use them.  I didn't bother to measure anything and the salad still tasted wonderful.  I wish I had some fresh basil, but used dried oregano instead  and that was just fine.

This was a very nice soup KaDo.  I enjoyed it very much. I especially liked that it was made with chicken broth and not cream.  I didn't have any velveeta cheese so I used a sharp old cheddar. It worked really well in the soup. I will be making this again...Thanks for sharing.

Thanks Kly for sharing this applecrisp recipe.  It reminds me of one my MIL makes.  Yum.  I used Jonathan apples in mine and baked in an 8x8.  Perfect.  
Made for Springs PAC 08'

Seriously yum!  Didn't have white chocolate, so used regular - only hurt the presentation.  The taste was so good that it didn't matter at all.  Also subbed lime juice for lemon.  I will say I had about twice as much frosting as I used.  This is alright though, as its GREAT!  Thank you for such a fab cupcake recipe.

Delious.  I used 2.5 lbs of pork ribs and Sweet Baby Rays bbq sauce.  I loved the heat of the peppers vs sweet bbq sauce.  I served with fresh cut fruit(melons and strawberries).  Heat of the ribs and the coolness of the fruit was a great combination.  Smelled so good when it was cooking.

One word - WOW!!  First off, I loved the ease of preparation of this cake!  Took me minutes to prepare!  Made this for my nephew's baptism and it was a hit!!  Used Marg's recipe #95416 for the icing.  Thanks Marg! :)

Ditto for us.  We agree 100% that these are awesome ribs and not to be reckoned with!  We will treasure this recipe and make it often as it is just plain excellent.  We grilled them and used Sweet Baby Rays BBQ Sauce, which is our favorite. I brought them to a boil and then cooked them on low for about 1 1/2 hrs. then covered with bbq sauce and put them on the grill and kept basting them with the bbq sauce until they were gooey, grilled to perfection and ready to go!  Thanks Joann!  Tony

You have a nice tasting muffin, CalicEe, & easy from start to finish! I used honey Dijon mustard & lemon pepper & was pleased with the results! I'd really prefer a whole egg, but realize this is much healthier to eat! Thanks for sharing! [Made & reviewed for one of my adopted chefs in this Spring's PAC]
I've been making this dish for almost 20 years and am never tired of it.  I serve it on top of mixed greens which goes great with the vinaigrette.
Neither me or my husband are one to order ribs at a restaurant. Never acquired the taste. But these are really good, and so easy!!!
I took other reviewers advice and cooked my syup about 10 minutes to reduce it a bit. I halved the recipe and enjoyed it in Iced Cinnamon Coffee. Thanks Caryn!

This worked great for cupcakes.  It made 24, the second 12 cupcake batch came out fine in spite of the batter sitting for about 20 minutes (the leavening still worked).  I frosted it with some ganache and got rave reviews.  Thanks for a keeper!

Usually I find cake made from scratch dry, however, this recipe is fantastic.  It's very moist and simple to make.  All I had was the Hershey's coco as the time, but it turned out just fine.

Thanks so much for posting this recipe. Love it.

These were a nice change to the pecan crusted sweet potatoes.  We enjoyed these with a nice flat iron steak & potato bread.  I personally would have added a bit more orange juice, but the BH loved them as was.  These were pretty easy to do.  We did change the directions and microwaved in the roasting dish the first 6 ingredients and added a tad more butter.  Worked out great.  Will be keeping this one.

Made this for Spring 2008 PAC.  It was good and I am surprised my husband ate them since he does not like corn bread.  I liked these, never had corn fritters before, seemed more like pancakes; were really good with butter on them.  Will make again.  Thanks!
This was great! I think next time I'll go a little lighter with the cloves. My whole family enjoyed this delightfully rich cake.

Yummy!!  I've made it twice now and the whole family devours it.  I peeled the eggplant and used light mayo instead of fat-free sicne that was all I had.  Turned out fantastic!  Thanks for a great recipe!

Delicious! I love when something so easy tastes so good and is so healthy for you. I used 1 kiwi and 1 large banana, along with about a 1/4 cup of nonfat yogurt and some splenda. About 170 calories for a full glass of delicious! I can't wait to try other fruit combinations. (After I wrote this, I just spilled half of it all over my table! Booo... now I have to go get more bananas!)

I expected to like this a lot more than I did. I followed the recipe exactly and yes it was tasty but somehow I think that I missed a dressing of some sort and that this salad was a little less complete without it.  I would make it again, but would experient with a dressing to go with it. Please see my rating system: personal preference is EVERYTHING, so what might be for me a less than complete recipe could be YOUR next favourite find exactly as it stands. Try it yourself and find out. I was pleased to have had a new salad lunch to try out. Thanks!

WOW!! This is the best thing I've tried in a long time! Who would have thought to put pickled ginger in a salad?! But it's brilliant! Goes perfectly with the cabbage and radish. I did leave the radicchio out (personal preference) but this is SUCH a pretty and yummy salad. Thanks!!!

Thanks English_Rose!
Gravy has always been hit or miss experience for me. I learned two important things from your recipe: first, combine flour and fat (don't dump flour into the drippings); second, add a little wine to the pan to flavor the outcome. Bravo! I know my gravies will improve!

Very nice flavor, easy to prepare.  I enjoyed the lemony flavor and the nuts in this, although next time I would toast the nuts first.  I used some lovely fresh purple sprouting broccoli in this and the sauce was a nice accompaniment.

These wings are excellent! Frying them first in the coating makes the skin very nice. The flavor of the sweet and sour seems like something perfectly Hawaiian to me, and not like a Chinese sweet and sour. Great for a luau! Thanks for sharing! ~Sue

These were really good! I took your advice and froze the leftovers and tried them reheated in the toaster oven. I am glad I did! Yesterday I hadn't liked these as well. The flavor was good, but they seemed a little rubbery. But reheating them in the toaster over left them delicious and crisp. Thanks for posting! ~Sue

I used this in Um Safia's Preserved Lemon Chicken Tagine for the Tagine!, which turned out delicious and saved me from having to make a special trip to the spice store. Very easy to make! Thanks for posting,
Holy Moly Bat Man! This was soooo wonderful! The dressing makes all the difference. I'm so glad you shared this.

This was really good.  I used one large boneless skinless chicken breast instead of thighs and with the sausage, that was plenty of meat for us.  I also added a little salt, but think it would be fine without.  Even though the weather is starting to get warm, I will definitely make this again.  I love that it cooks all day while I have fun.
I thought these were very good, just for personal taste I might like a heavier ratio of feta cheese. But the seasoning on the spinach was very nice and tasty! Thanks so much for posting!!!

This had alot of preparation involved, so it became a little messy for me. I increased the Asiago cheese and put inside with the mixture as opposed to on top, which made the bread taste great. I enjoyed it very much.

We liked this one a LOT! I made half a recipe for 3 people and still had leftover. So a full recipe would feed well over 6. I used a 16oz ribeye sliced, for the meat. I added sliced mushrooms, carrots, and bean sprouts with the leek, but skipped adding the celery. I also used a 9 ounce package of fresh Chinese noodles instead of the spaghetti and it was wonderful. Thanks again for a great recipe and thank your grandmother again as well.

Wow this was great stuff... I followed exactly except that I doubled and baked it in two 8 inch square pans. It took about 45 minutes in my oven to have the best cornbread ever and healthy too. Thanks for the keeper.
This is tasty and flavorful, and definitely a great option for a dieting diner.  It is quite filling for a low cal, low carb meal.

PAC 2008-  This came out moist and delicious. Like Jean I was unsure of the combination but was ready for new chicken recipes that were easy to put together and un to eat.  We all enjoyed this recipe.  I like the nuance of sweet and savory/oniony .  Will make this again. Served with asparagus and pasta with alredo sauce Recipe #111347 another PAC baby.

This is a good base recipe.  The balls have a great texture and are pretty versitile.  I would like to really add some flavor to them.  I'd love to hear suggestions about different spice combinations people have tried.  Thanks for the great recipe!

I loved the onion and the olives in it, it was very spicy but not hot which i really like. I took some left overs to work the next day and it was still goo for lunch. In general i must say that the crust could cave been better, crunchier but that might be a fault of the pizza dough i used.

I cut the recipe in half and made 4 meatballs. After frying I added 2 cups of pasta sauce and served over spaghetti. This made 2 generous servings and the meatballs were very tasty. I will be adding this recipe to my OAMC repertoire. Next time I will try them on a hoagie roll. Made for PAC Spring 08. Thanks for posting Bev.

I think it is a great little change! The bacon made it very tasty. I did however use ground turkey and turkey bacon since I don't eat red meat. I added fresh chopped spinach , sauteed red onions, 1 tsp of dry white wine and real garlic. I would make it again.

Delicious soup. I made it as stated except I used the crockpot to cook the beans, ham garlic and water until almost done, then added the onion and potatoes and finished up. Served with some cornbread muffins. Will definately make this a lot. Will try some other type beans to change it up a bit. Thanks for a delicious recipe.

These turned out very well. The ribs were moist and super tender. My DS gave it more than 5 stars. I used a little over 5 pounds of meat, so I doubled the sauce recipe, and used splenda and low carb ketchup. The sauce thickens nicely and really sticks to the ribs. This is the first time I have ever made them in the oven and am sure it won't be the last. 2 1/2 hrs cooking time was perfect.

We liked this alot....this was our 'meal' tonight!
I tossed the broccoli and onion into the food processor and pulsed it a few times,  dumped it into a bowl and added the remainder of the ingredients and then the 'dressing'. I did use 'McCormick Mayonesa', which contains lime juice.( I love this stuff!!) Thanks for the recipe MsPia
These are great.  I sliced my apple thinly and didn't mash it, just let it cook down with the sauce.  Such an easy dish, and quick, but good enough for company!  Made for Spring 2008 PAC.

If I could give a 10 I WOULD ! We started eating these beans before I got the tomato sauce in. This method of making beans less gassy really-really worked! Now I can make beans any day of the week just not weekends ! The beans sat for more than an hour on step #3.(beer 30 is break time).
Made for PAC Spring 2008

Wow, is this a great cake recipe.  I love how moist it is.  I made mine with white cake mix and put a little almond flavoring in the batter.  I also made it 24 hours before serving and kept it in the fridge.  A perfect ending to a birthday meal.  Thanks for posting!
This was really good and so easy to make!  I used Granny Smith apples and just followed the directions.  Great recipe!  Reviewed for Newest Zaar Tag.

Found this one to be a huge family hit and is now on our "favorites" list. I used an entire one pound package of beans, and increased the recipe accordingly. I also added some bread stuffing mix to help the patties stay together better. With the increased recipe, I was able to feed my wife, my son and the four other members of his band who practice at our house regularly, and then to put about twenty burgers in the freezer to be popped out for a quick and easy (and tasty) meal at will. Won't be buying anymore veggie burgers at the store, for sure.
in my previous review, i forgot to write that i used a spicy green salsa and it was amazing!

Loved the name, loved the the soup.  The broth tasted spicy by itself but once it was ladled over the rice, the flavors mellowed and it was not spicy at all.  Actually, we added extra red pepper flakes at the table.  I loved the cubed cheese instead of shredded; it melted into nice little lumps of gooey goodness.

I agree with your previous reviewers, these are great cookies. Delicious, light and lovely making for one of those "you can't eat just one" kind of cookie. Used packaged ground almonds and made as posted with excellent results. Your photo had me add that little touch - makes for great presentation - and an empty platter. Thank you Roxygirl for another of your recipes that was a winner at our house.

This is a great side dish! It is especially good warm. I might try it with less basil next time, but it is very tasty as is! I made it 3 times and noticed a definite difference in the amount of time it took for the kernels to brown. When the kernels were more spread out, some of them turned brown after about 5 minutes; when they were less spread out (but still one layer), they took about 20 (although I did use a different sheet). I will be making this again! Thanks for the recipe! Made for PAC Spring 2008.
I've made this recipe twice in one week!!  I couldn't find mini pierogi, so I used full-size potato/onion ones.  My DH loves it!! Easy and great tasting.  Thanks for posting.

Wow - I had some sweet potatoes just waiting for a grand experiment, and this recipe was an excellent choice - I didn't change a thing.  And, I'm not even a vegan.  Everyone loved them.  Thanks so much.

This is a great recipe.
I made it several times.
I add 2 Tbs of cassis liqueur.
Allways a hit.
Thank you.

I  made this to go with bbq chicken. I knew when I saw the word Amish in the recipe it had to be good, and I wasn't disappointed. The only change I made was to use mayo instead of salad dressing. This was easy and very flavorful, with using mayo it wasn't too sweet. Thanks so much Kim!

I made a three layer version of this recipe yesterday and it was delicious!  
If you want the cake to turn out moist, be sure not to overcook the cake by even a split second.  I used the buttercream recipe #261024 and it was delish!  
This would also work very well as a cherries jubilee cake.

Cheap + Healthy + Tasty = Inspiring!  We used jasmine rice, which added a deep, almost nutty flavor to the patties, and threw in some fresh chopped tomatoes and cucumber to boost the veggie count. We also spiced it up using extra garlic, Thai chili sauce (Sambal Oelek, ground chili with garlic - available at Asian markets or in the Asian food sections), a few dashes of cumin (powder), and homemade salsa (tomatoes, garlic, fresh jalepenos, salt, and lime juice). We also used the liquid in which the beans were packed, adding approximately 1/2 - 3/4 cup of homemade bread crumbs to soak up excess moisture. Our yield was easily up to 12 hamburger-sized patties. Depending on the amount of rice/bread crumbs used, you may want to use more eggs and/or oil to bind. We drizzled a little lime over our patties and ate them over a bed of jasmine rice.

One of my favorites from childhood. Daddy cooked this for us for breakfast. He didn't use any butter in his. He didn't measure, just went by eyesight, but I don't think he used as much flour. Still drained the beef, so not so much fat. Added flour to cooked, drained beef (I prefer ground round or ground chuck), stirred it well and then added milk and cooked until thickened. I like a lot of black pepper on mine. I was just thinking about making some this morning. Seeing this posted has really increased my craving. LOVE IT!!!  Read in Trisha Yearwood's cookbook that she has this for breakfast every year on her birthday!

You have a lot of reviews but I wanted to post mine with the variations so people would see how versatile the recipe is!

I made this using 1/2 cup potato starter made from #83012 instead of the yeast, reducing the water to 1 cup and omitting the sugar.  For the flour I used 11oz unbleached and 4 oz whole wheat (by weight, which is about 3 cups total).  Divided into 16 balls rather than 18 because I am lazy ;).

Other than letting the balls sit longer to account for a slower rise, the rest was as the recipe stated.  I was worried that to get the sizes I wanted I had to roll them so thin, but pleasantly surprised how they fluffed while cooking.  I wasn't worried about making them perfectly round - practice will help with that.

Excellent recipe, they taste wonderful, and were very easy to make.
A great Soup!! And, thank you for sharing a really wonderful story!!!

Terrific recipe! We loved this as a dip with cheese quesadillas. We made only half the recipe and it was still enough for our family. We didn't have an envelope of ranch seasoning, just the big container of seasoning, so we mashed everything else together first and then added ranch seasoning to it until it had the perfect taste. Thanks for the great dip recipe. Made for AUS/NZ Recipe Swap #16.

Delicious spin on the white sauce that usually acompanies broccoli & cauli. I did this for cauli as the guinea pig had eaten all the broccoli and it went alongside our corned beef dinner beautifully, I did use the lemon juice, it was a nice touch & I baked the cauli & sauce in the oven topped with some breadcrumbs & cheese as I usually do for this dish. Thanks!
This dish is delicious and very easy to make.  The aroma while cooking is wonderful.  It was served with fish tacos and recipe #235555 as part of a Cinco de Mayo dinner.

Yummmm this is soooo good!  I made this last night and we loved it.  I can see why people would be fighting over this!  I sliced a quart of strawberries and covered them in 2/3 cup of sugar.  When I sliced the cake I spooned the strawberries and syrup over the top....to die for!!!
Aussie/NZ Swap #16 - Emily, another awesome recipe of yours!! This soup is so filling - comfort food at it's best!!
What a wonderful little side dish. I served mine with roasted turkey and broccoli. So yummy, quick and easy.

Printed it out and gathered the children and then saw that it had 340grms of BUTTER in it!!  Australia is a country with a HUGE obesity problem (and the US is worse!!).  Is there a clever chef out there who can convert this to a lower fat alternative?  It looks GREAT!

I"m surprised this soup hasn't gotten any reviews yet.  I was looking for a vegetarian soup with a clear broth and some beans and fresh veggies so I decided to try this.  I'm terrible at planning ahead though, so I opted to use canned beans rather than cook my own in order to save some time.  Also, we forgot to buy the fresh parsley so I also used dried leaves.  I cooked the soup as the recipe stated only I added a can of rinsed and drained white beans after bringing the soup to a boil and letting it simmer for approximately 30 minutes.  I pured the beans in and it was ready to serve! I think it turned out great.  

I used 8 cups of water over 6 so ended up needing 2 1/2 cubes of bouillon for the right flavor.  I think to make the recipe more to my liking, I'd lessen the potatoes (I put 4 or 5 small in) and add more beans instead as one can didn't quite make it a "bean" soup.  All in all I really enjoyed this recipe and will use it again for a quick healthy soup.  Thanks for the recipe!

So delicious, even without the frosting!  I made these for my sons 2nd birthday, and I was so impressed with them.  Usually when I think cupcakes I think "dry, too much sugary frosting, and primarily for kids" but these don't fit any of that.  Thanks for this, it's going into my favorites!
We really enjoyed these simple wraps. Thanks for sharing!

Fabulous!!! This is some creation. I used Jose Cuervo Classico tequila which has a touch of lemon flavor. The touch of coconut milk mellows and smooths the tequila ever so slightly. I used quite a bit of ice so I got 2 servings. I'll be making this one for my mom the next time she visits.
I think this had too much cinnamon in it.  No one in our family liked it. It was kind off odd and we werent sure what to pair it with. I put it on a tortilla and my wife put it over rice.

This was fantastic, I would definitely make this again!  I lowered the oil in the dressing to about 1 tablespoon to save a few calories and because BF is not overly fond of cilantro or red onion, I only put in about 1/4 cup instead of 1/2.  He still thought there was a bit too much onion but I didn't.:)  Otherwise, I don't think it needed any additional salt.  The two of us ate about 2/3 of it for supper with a salad, and I just finished off the rest of it for lunch.  Excellent!
Like a great candy bar.  I couldn't stop eating them.  Thanks.
These weren't the prettiest pancakes, but DH loved the taste.  They were quite dense, but moist and tasty.  Thanks!
I LOVE Nimbu Pani and live on it in the summer!  This is how I make it, although I use limes instead of lemons and I use regular sugar.  Thanks Roja!

I found this on the internet site 101cookbooks.com. I really enjoy this recipe. It makes a good meatless entree or side dish.  I have made this many times now.  I often eat it for lunch.  It is good with and without the tahini dressing.  I make instant brown rice while I am making the rest of the dish.  It comes together very quickly.  I have yet to toast the almond slivers.  It is good regardless.

You've got a great recipe here, so you get a full 5 star rating! And although I DID cut the amount of red pepper in half, since I don't like so much heat, friends were raving about the taste while at the same time suggesting that I should have added a little more heat! Can't please everyone all the time, but I can rate this recipe according to the raves! Thanks for sharing!

This was excellent, I cooked the chicken in the actual marinade and it was wonderful.

Thanks for sharing

This was pretty good soup, easy to make.  I made this to use up some asparagus so I didn't have a full bunch, used bouillon for the broth and, to cut down on calories, I used 2% milk for the cream and didn't use near 2 tblsp of oil.  It didn't thicken up much (probably b/c I didn't use the cream) so I added some cornstarch which didn't help much.  It was a good recipe, though, something I may make again.

I found the texture was a bit dry and crumbly.  Also the icing was quite runny.  However, the taste was very good.  I made double recipe and had enough batter for about 28 cupcakes.  I made a single icing recipe (for 12 cupcakes) and had more than enough to frost all 28.

This was incredible!  I, too, only made it for 2 servings (chicken breasts).  It was an excellent Saturday night dinner.  I served this with corn, pasta and apple/blueberry crisp for dessert.  I'll be making this again.  Thanks so much!
Excellent Recipe!!!

Super good.  We used this as a marinade for chicken and shrimp kabobs and they were both wonderful.  They were left to marinade for about 30 hours.  We also saved some to have on the side after they were made.  Everyone at the dinner table loved these and finished all of them, Even though we thought we had made way too many.

Easy, pleasy, tasty, this is going into my permanment files! I remember my mother making mayo, but it taking a long time and was had to get it just right. Not this recipe! Added the paprika this time, will try the rosemary next time to go on some potato salad. Thank you!

Loved it!  I did change it a little.  Instead of 2 lbs of hamburger, I used 1 lb hamburger, 1 lb sausage, and 1/2 lb ground turkey.  I also added seasoned salt.  It turned out wonderful!  I have made many meatloafs, and never used parmesan.  That must have been what made it SO good!

This is a great recipe.  Now I can make gravy almost as good as my Mom's.  I did add some black and cayenne pepper to spice it up a bit.  I also added a little cornstarch to thicken it, but if I had had enough time it might have thickened without it, we were just ready to eat.  I agree with the other person who said that you should use unsalted butter.

This recipe is ridiculously easy to make. It even works if you only marinate it for 2 hours. But it shouldn't be listed as taking less than an hour to prepare because of the four-hour marinating time. Still, I will TOTALLY make it again.... and again and again and again.

This was soooo delicious!
I kept the cooking time, but reduced it to 380 F.
I didn't have enough cream cheese, so I added Ricotta Cheese to the cream. I didn't have white wine on hand, so I substituted water plus lemon juice and wine vinegar. I only used 8 oz. of Pizza Cheese comb.
I omitted salt and put Sicilian Seasoning (V. Taylor's) on the salmon. I used a combination of fresh baby spinach & Creamed   on top. And I also used a few chopped onion pieces on top of the spinach. Thanks for such a great recipe! I will do it again.

Delicious!  The cumin in the sauce really adds an interesting dimension.  I bet this would be good on green beans or brussels sprouts, also.
Thanks for an inspiring recipe.

Excellent! We did not use the fresh parsley as we were out, and added just a wee bit of crushed red pepper flakes. We also removed the shrimp from the saute pan and then made the alfredo using the same pan for easy cleanup and to incorporate the flavors into the sauce. We left out the nutmeg for personal preference. The cream cheese adds a wonderful unique flavor to this dish. Thanks for posting! :)

I loved this cake.  I made several other high rated chocolate cakes on the zaar and this one was my favorite, especially coupled with the chocolate butter cream frosting.  I gave my boyfriend's family a big chunk of this cake and they paid me to make another (whole) one!  Flippin' Sweet!
These muffins are delicious! To make them even healthier, I substituted 1/2 cup apple sauce for half of the oil. My whole family loved these!

The sauteed onions in this egg salad are so unusual, but so good. We really enjoyed this salad. However the 3 Tbsp of oil in the onions was much too much for me. There was too much unnecessary fat. I would also have liked a bit of crunch, maybe from a few green onions or chives. That said this is a good recipe to work on to adjust to personal taste and the fried onions were lovely. Made with real bacon. Thank you!

This soup truly lived up to its reputation!!  The story would have been satisfying enough, but the recipe is truly a treasure.  The only thing I did different was to use linguica instead of kielbasa, because that is what I had on hand.  Next time, I will use the kielbasa, in order to remain true to the two old queens, who obviously know what they're doing!
Crispy and delicious.  The addition of the red pepper adds just the right amount of heat.

This was awesome and easy!
I used healthy request cm soup and daisy light sour cream (because it is all natural) so the points were a little bit more.
My Crockpot cooks fast too, but I know that so I always adjust. 
I also used whole wheat noodles....will be making this over and over and over and over:)

I enjoyed this shrimp dish and it was very filling. I would have liked to have it with more spices such as a bit of garlic powder or more crushed red pepper flakes than what Bird put in it (as I love spicy). Overall, this is a good dish. Thank you for posting.

I have no idea how to pronounce the name of these pancakes, but my family is calling them HEAVENLY!  I got the "Are you kidding?" look when DH & DS found out we were having oatmeal pancakes for dinner.  But it turns out the oatmeal is the special ingredient.  It's texture is just perfect to create a fluffy but slightly chewy pancake.  We actually ate more of these than normal pancakes.  I did not add raisins as the boys wouldn't like them & we ate them with butter & maple syrup.  We'll be saving this recipe to make again & again.  Thanks for sharing, Iceland!  This precious baby was adopted from the PAC Spring 2008 orphanage.

Ok, this is the best brownie I ever made!
I did change a couple things though.
First I used pecans instead of the walnuts because I only had pecans in my fridge.  I will try with walnuts the next time I make these.
I also did not make the frosting and used ready made.  I ran out of time and needed them done but next time I will be making the frosting.
I found that these brownies cut easily for me and were just the right flavour.
I will be using this from now on as my recipe for brownies!
The best ever!

This was quite good; my husband and I don't really care for eggplant but are trying to expand our variety, and this is a way we will have it again.  I made some adaptations and some mistakes with the recipe. First off I did peel it, because the skin is way too tough and bitter for us. Next, my husband hates onion so I subbed a hefty dash of garlic powder.  I forgot to mix parmesan into the bread crumbs. The crumbs were Italian style so I didn't add more italian seasoning, but I didn't have enough of them so I added some flour, a bit of salt, and other seasonings into it.

The cook time was spot-on, but I did have to broil a little bit to get them to brown on top. I served with a bit of spaghetti sauce for dipping.

Despite my unintentional butchering of the recipe, this was pretty good.  We'll have it again.

We loved this soup on a cool, rainy spring evening.  Using rotisserie chicken and canned beans makes it come together so quickly.  It was great with a loaf of crusty garlic asiago bread.  yum.  I took leftovers to work and everyone wanted the recipe. :)

I have eaten a lot of pho (beef) in my life and absolutely love it... but have never tried a chicken version... I had some homemade chicken broth in the freezer, along with some sliced chicken breast, so this really did come together quickly. I used cellophane noodles ( bean thread) and found it a really nice change from the rice vermicelli I usually use for beef pho. 1 oz of noodles was a little skimpy for us... we like them, so I used 2 oz of the dried cellophane noodles soaked in very hot water, but they were still not soft enough and ended up dipping them into the broth before pouring into bowls... I made the full amount of soup and loved the balance of flavor... the fish sauce is crucial in my opinion... and froze the remaining broth in little containers for an even quicker fix next time... I also topped with bean spouts... yum! Thanks for a great, wholesome soup!!!

This is so good! I was craving vanilla ice cream with chocolate sauce with our current heat wave, so whipped up a half batch of this and was immediately satisfied! Rich and chocolatey, and so quick! Who needs hersheys, honestly! This is better with ingredients already on hand for a quick fix! Thanks for posting!
Oh heaven... Wonderfully decadent. I used a whole (small) head of garlic.
I followed the recipe exactly, but nobody was jumping for joy over this recipe.  It tasted like something was missing...I used a mild salsa, and that could be a factor.
Very tasty and FILLING!  I love the cardamom and may add more next time.  I, too, skipped the raisins, and served these with butter and maple syrup.  Made for Spring 2008 PAC Orphanage.
This is a really great soup. I smoked a turkey and had a lot left over, this was a great use for it. I will definetly be making this again. Thanks for the recipe!

Great taste and couldn't be easier to prepare. Next time I may add a tablespoon of water to the topping, and I will be making them again. Thanks for posting!
Made for PAC Spring 2008.

YUMMY!  I made this today since it was 103 degrees and we needed a refreshing drink.  I added frozen strawberries instead of fresh berries and ice.  I also used OJ since I didn't have guava juice.  I agree that this could be a tasty grown up drink with some vodka!
This is a great salad!  I love all the flavors with the fruits, nuts, and a sesame dressing.  I can't wait to have this again tomorrow!  Thanks for posting.

LOVED this recipe, true!
Added HEAPED teaspoon of garlic or two! :)
Used 8 tbsp orange juice and SPICED cracked pepper for today!
Pureed...am glad this LOW FAT recipe came my way!
THANKS!

Instead of making mini tacos, I bought the full size wonton wrappers and did 12 instead.

I loved the crunch, and everything tasted so yummy that I'm having leftovers for lunch!  Even my 5 year old thought this was a neat dinner.  Thanks for sharing and I'll be making this again.

Great stuff, but the nutrition information is COMPLETELY WRONG.

Glace de viande has hardly any fat.

The problem seems to be that the nutrition information assumes you eat all that goes in (most of it in fact gets thrown away).

1 cup of meat glaze weighs about 250 g (a tad more than water), NOT 1319 g.  It certainly does not contain more than its own weight in protein and fat!

Fantastic! I used half whole wheat flour and half bread flour, my oil was olive oil. I rolled out the first half very thin and let them rest for while. The second half, I rolled thicker and didn't let them rest. We liked the second batch best. I rolled them out on my counter without any added flour and cooked them in my ungreased cast iron skillet. My whole family loved them and they rival the expensive bread I buy at my local Lebonese grocer. It went great with my homemade hummus. Even my picky daughter and young grandchildren loved them. This recipe will be written down by hand in my recipe book (not many make it there). Loved it and thanks so much for sharing!
   After some thought, I finally realized that this bread is almost identical to "Flat Out" bread!  Flat out is an expensive flat bread sold in most grocers, at least around here in Michigan. Love the stuff. I'll be saving some serious money with this gem of a recipe! Thanks again!

I am a 66 year old male.  I have never baked a cake in my life!  This was fantastic!  Tasted just like my mothers scratch cakes as a kid.  I impelished the recipe a little, by using butter rather then oil.  Also added 1 0z of bittersweet chocolate to the melted butter, and used a mix of coffee and water, instead of just water.  It was rich, rich, rich!  Took me 10 minutes to make.

This is my first time having fried eggplant and it definitely won't be my last.  It was so delicious, although I did find that I don't care for the peel.   Such easy preparation and wonderful taste.  I used a baby eggplant and ate the whole thing myself.  The slices browned up beautifully also.  Next time I will be sure to have some marinara for dipping.

Great fudgy cookie! I did alter it a bit. I quartered the recipe and got 6 small cookie scoop sized cookies. Instead of 1/2 egg white I used 1 1/2 T. eggbeaters. When I calculated points on my recipe they came to 2 pts. each. I'l keep this recipe!
I totally forgot to rate this!  Made it quite awhile ago for DH, he loved it!  He ate it on tortillas, over rice, and just plain too.  Thank you very much!

I goofed in reading the ingredient list before shopping and bought fresh green beans. So I began by steaming them for two minutes then cooked them as stated here.  They were just fantastic, the flavors were just bursting forward but simple and clean enough for this to complement my grilled chicken.   Loved 'em and plan to replicate my mistake.
Great recipe.   I peeled the eggplant and followed the directions.  Crispy outside and cooked, but not mushy in the inside.  This will be a great treat for the summer.
Very easy, smells wonderful while cooking. Taste great.Followed recipe exactly.
My family really liked this recipe. I halved the cayenne and may half the black pepper next time because of our tastes. This was so easy. I used boneless, skinless chicken thighs. Thanks for posting.

These are awesome. DH was shocked that apples and carrots taste so good together. This is on the sweet side but makes a wonderful dish. I served it a long side a meatloaf dish. Very easy to prepare and looks great plated. Thanks for posting.

My 10 year old daughter makes this cake all by herself.  And she makes it over and over and over again because every time she does people RAVE about it and it is gone in a matter of hours.  She bakes it in a bundt pan and sprinkles it with powdered sugar. Amazingly delicious.

This was a great tandoori chicken!  It was so easy, especially since I didn't marinate it overnight.  Not entirely sure it was necessary, but then instead of chicken I used vegetarian chicken strips.  I omitted the jalapenos,  and reduced the vegetable oil.  I served it with a lemon-pepper rice and a veggie side.  If you insist on having a red tandoori, I suggest you add paprika:D  Thanks a mil for a great dinner!

I made this cake for our community group dinner at our house.  It got rave reviews from everyone!  Even my husband who says he HATES cake, thought this cake was wonderful.  Moist and delicious.  The only addition I made...a splash of Malibu rum!
This was very good and very orangy~a bit too much so for my husband.  I will try it again with a bit less of the oj.

I followed the lead of prior reviews & made a half recipe using 2 oz cream cheese, but lacked the right size sq or oblong pan & baked it in a 9-in pie plate. I whizzed the mixture together in min w/my magic bullet, but found it easier to heat the butter in my microwave to elminate the in & out of the oven step. This is buttery rich w/just a bare hint of sweetness from the honey & I esp like being able to control that by a choice of how to serve it. I dusted my taste test w/powd sugar & am sure DH will prefer his much-loved ice cream. Thx for sharing your recipe for this easy-fix taste treat w/us. :-)

The only thing wrong with this recipe is that one squash just isn't enough, unless this is supposed to feed only one!  Seriously, this is so good that you really do need to increase the amount of squash to feed 4.  Became an instant fave!  Thnx so much for posting, Kelly!

I made this tonight with grilled chicken.  My 2 year old even gobbled it up.  The only thing I did differently was slicing them into discs instead of lengthewise.  Then I put both the basil and discs in a foil pouch on the grill.  Served it warm, yummy!
I loved this! I used yogurt and would recommend it - it was still really creamy. I used red grapes. Thanks!

I can't believe I haven't written a review. This is my standard chocolate cake. I don't want to go back to boxed. Turns out rich and moist.

It just takes a couple of minutes more than making a boxed cake.
Just what we were looking for.  Nice and moist, I used two cups of rhubarb, added 1/2 tsp almond extract to the batter, and doubled the topping.

Very tasty! I only reserved about 1/2 cup of the crumb crust because I needed more for the bottom. I might make more of the crust next time. Really loved these they would be great for a potluck, brunch or whatever. Thanks! Will make again!

For the first time ever, my kids liked an asian dish. I was stunded! Usualy they don't care for anything oriental, but this time they emptied their plates. What more could I want? DH and I enjoyed this dish very much too. I did use regular frozen peas, but it tasted great. A keeper!
Thanks for posting.

All the kiddos loved it!  DH said it was alright - but it reminded him of sweet and sour - the sweet part.  He's not a fan.  I loved it!  The shrimp definitely isn't as big as the pic posted by Peter J - but there was enough for all to enjoy. :)  This was served with Lavendar Lynn's Lumpia - recipe 261401 for the May NZ/Aussie recipe swap!

These are right up there with the best wings we have ever tasted!  Delicious coating that tantalizes the taste buds and has you coming back for more.  This recipe will be passed around in my neighborhood and with my family for sure!  Prize winning recipe right here for the taking!  Thanks for sharing your recipe with us Lynn!

it was okay - then i remembered seeing another watermelon ice recipe in one of my cook books - it used pineapple juice concentrate - i think i'll try that next time -- i thought with the lemon juice it was too funky.

These are absolutely fabulous Geri.  You don't even have to be a date lover to enjoy these scrumptious little morsels of delishiousness.  Love the crust and just everything about them.  And, always a + in so easy to make.  The only thing I omitted from your recipe were the walnuts.  If it was for me, I'd have added them, but they weren't and so per preference, omitted.  I bet they'd be better yet with the added nuts:-)  Thanks for posting and so glad I tagged for Photoforum~

These muffins are so moist and have a wonderful banana taste to them.  However, I noticed they only take 15 minutes to bake, and they make 24 muffins which is wonderful.  Thanks so much for this delicious recipe.  I have already had some wonderful compliments.  I'll definitely make these again.:)

I've been doing "wedge" potatoes like this for a few years now and they are so delicious.  Another great seasoning to add to them is cajun spice mix - add it in with the salt and pepper and I promise you will love the flavour!

Please explain, I made a 1/2 recipe, which should serve 8, but my family of 5 ate it all up in one go?  So, who's wrong, me or you?  DELICIOUS recipe.  Very easy to make.  I am lucky to have access to really good plums right now (I used a yellow variety) and I'm very glad I chose to make this dessert.  Absolutely beautiful with coffee after dinner.

This is a delicious pasta dish from Giada de Laurentiis without your typical tomato or cream based sauce. It's easily modified to suit your tastes: If you don't want it as spicy, use half sweet and half hot Italian sausage, or even mild turkey sausage. If it's not spicy enough for you, add more garlic, plus some red pepper flakes. Vegetarians can substitute mushrooms of choice for the meat  and use vegetable broth. Manga!

This was a really good and hearty stew.  I followed the recipe pretty closely but I used chicken stock instead of chicken broth but added an extra cup of chicken broth for more liquid.  I used Great Northern beans for the beans in this recipe and probably a few extra cloves of garlic.  The recipe was tasty and comforting...but could have used slightly more flavor.  Both my 4 year old and 2 year old LOVED it and that's all I cared about tonight so for me it was a huge success.  It makes a ton and we'll have lots of leftovers.  Thanks so much for sharing.

I would give it 3 and a half stars. The pasta was very asparagus-y. I like asparagus, but not that much. I admit that I repaced the ham with some leftover chicken we had. That might have done something to change it, but not much. It was still a good dish, but I won't make it again.

I gave this recipe 4 stars. My family loved this recipe. I made 1 minor change to the recipe. I left out the celery as my families not crazy over celery. I used cider vinegar and next time I will try this with white vinegar. We will have this again for sure. Thanks so much for posting a yummy recipe. Christine (internetnut)

Easy to make, cheesey and a very kid-friendly risotto!  I say it's kid-friendley because it's so cheesey and kind of has that pizza-like flavor.  I made this as written, using arborio rice.  Arborio makes the best risotto, in my opinion.  Thanx for sharing this.  I'll make this again.

This was very good and super easy.  I added a small can of diced Italian tomatoes just for some more flavor and a soupier mix.  I also diced the sausages because the picture posted  looked so nice!  Thanks for the great recipe!

I love lamb and this dish just showcases it in a wonderful and tasty way. I didn't have enough regular potatoes so I threw in two sweet potatoes and it came out really nice. Definately a German recipe and one for my recipe binder. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!! Made for ZWT4 - Fancy Feinschmeckers.

This was a great, quick, weeknight supper  dish that my whole family really enjoyed!  We all love garbanzo beans and Middle Eastern flavors so assumed that we would like this as well.  Usually we eat garbanzos cold so I wasn't sure if everyone would like the hot dish and as my husband is a real carnivore I was worried about the "vegetarian" supper but all were completely satisfied and asking for it again!  Did I mention  that it was so easy to toss together!  Thanks Julie for a keeper.
This is an excellent simple dish, good hot with rice, or room temp.  I loved all the parsley--fresh flat leaf from the garden.  Thanks, Julie!

Made & reviwed for ZWT 4 ~ Kumquat's Kookin Kaboodles! I just HAD to make these as soon as I saw the word 'easy' in the description! They are so easy & quick to make & are totally delicious too. The ingredients are always inmy cupboards so this will certainly become a regular treat for us! I am keen to try them with ground almonds next time.... Thanks Sue for a great recipe :)

Yummy!  We have high altitude baking problems so I lowered the butter to 6 T and reduced the sugar by about 1/4 c.  It turned out light and fluffy and wonderful!  Baked it in a dark pan for about 33 minutes.
The dressing is sweet and nutty with a spicy kick. Make sure to throughly chill this slaw or else the strong taste of kale will overpower the dressing.

I was looking for a make-ahead dessert. I didn't know I would find such a fantastic recipe. I made it for my bridge ladies and they each copied the recipe before they left. I also added a layer carmel sauce on the ice cream sandwiches before adding the Cool Whip. I added 2 Butterfingers instead of one. Next time I will use three. The ladies wanted more Butterfingers. This was the best!
My whole family like it.  it is a keeper
Incredibly simple and very tasty!

AWESOME potata's mama!!!! Absolutely LOVED them!!! I did peel mine per request of my hubby, but next time I'm sneakin in a few of the skins! ;) Sshhhh!!! ;) I prefer them in there, and he's just gonna have to learn to like em that way! ;) :) WONDERFUL!!!!! Made for the ZWT4

DH and I served this for dinner a few night ago.  It was a delicious and different way to prepare lamb chops.  We enjoyed it very much.  I didn't have a red pepper on hand, so I used a combination of yellow and orange bell peppers.  I think it enhanced the presentation of the dish and made it more colorful.  DH suggested that next time, he would chop the green olives to better distribute the olives.  Thanks for posting this lovely dish.  Served Recipe #62136 as a side dish.
Mmmmm, that was good.

very delicious, especially the topping! really love it! :) very easy also. anyway, what's the lemon juice for? I couldn't really taste the lemony flavor.. but it doesn't matter much. I sprinkled some cinnamon before serving but I didn't think it improves the flavor much as the cheesecake is already too delicious. lol. thanks heaps, Bev!

Good recipe! I tried using low fat Miracle Whip instead of mayo and the tangy taste overpowered the eggplant. Definitely better with mayo. Added a bit of pepper to the crumb mix too. Very good! Thanks for sharing :)

I love this recipe!  I don't like using cake mixes but I wasn't sure where to start when my daughter requested strawberry cupcakes.  There were so quick to make and were a huge hit at the bbq I took them to.  This recipe worked so well I've started substituting...instead of strawberries and strawberry gelatin I used lemon gelatin and added a little lemon juice and rind to the batter.  I finished them by filling  with lemon curd and topped off with a lemon cream cheese frosting.  Awesome!  Thanks so much for sharing.

Thank you for a quick and delicious recipe. The name sounds complicated but it's actually not.  It's so kid friendly that even my neighbors'  5 and 8 yr old kids can even make them.They simply mixed everything except the raspberries which they pressed on a pan, placed the preserves on top, then covered it with the rest of the mixture and voila! 30 mins of baking and it's done. That easy! How do you describe something that just makes the children smile, smacking their lips,  raving, "delicious!" several times while licking their chops and rubbing their bellies? Was it supposed to be 36 bars? I dunno but I think it was just enough for 3 servings! I only got to taste them since they finished 2/3 of it and gave 1/3 to my neighbor's other brother. They had the right sweetness and  it wasn't sickeningly sweet considering it had confectioners' sugar in it. In fact, it's excellent and a keeper from now on. Thank you!

This is so easy and quick to make.  And delicious!  I will definitely make this again adding some other veggies as suggested.
Thanks!
yummy and so easy to make.  i did do it on a stove top adding bits at a time as per a classic risotto because i wanted the extra creamines.

These are delicious and very easy to make.  I followed ingredients per recipe except I didn't have any yukon golds so I used russets.  We served it with recipe#229692 for a great German Dinner for ZWT4.

This is the same recipe I have always used for pasta salad and it always gets rave reviews at cookouts and gatherings.  I use the Cavatappi pasta and lite italian dressing, I also always add green and red peppers.  I have never tried the mozzarella but that sounds delish and plan to do so next time I make this!  Thanks for posting!

I was in the mood for gnocchi and I'm so glad I made this recipe.  These were really delcious.  The ricotta chesse made them especially light.  I loved them served with just the herb butter, my kids had them with some marinara.

This is an awesome soup.  Really quick and easy.  Lots of flavour.  We'll be making this often.  We'll be making this often.  Thanks for a great recipe.  To my second bowl I added a spoon of  sour cream because I like cream soup they are both delicous.
This was really fast, really easy, and really good! I served mine with some sugar snap peas for a light lunch. I do suggest seasoning the potatoes with salt and pepper, though.

Yep ...another 5 star review.  Made as written and topped it with sprouts.  Excellent.  Going to try a beef version next.  Thanks so much for posting.  I love Pho but would have been intimidated (and time challenged) to make the 'real deal'.  Wouoldn't even attempt it now as this was so good.
From "The Barefoot Contessa Cookbook" Excellent flavor and super easy to prepare!

Loved these! They had a nice tanginess from the cream cheese, and turned out smooth, rich, and creamy. Garlic flavor was not too strong. Browning the top added extra flavor. Made for ZWT4 Kumquat's Kookin' Kaboodles. 
Thanks for posting! 
~Sue

Loved this one!  It has a punchy and sour flavor with a bit of heat - perfect for those more sensitive tongues - but hot heads could even add a bit more jalpeno. I really liked the way the lime added an acidic balance to the dish in a way that brought all the flavors together.  To speed up the marinading time, I cut the chicken into pieces and threaded them on skewers before popping them on the indoor grill for 2-3 minutes.  I reduced the oil in half as well.  Made for ZWT4.
Very, very easy and quick to make!  I had to make mine in an 8x8 dish.  It is already gone!    I will definitely make this again.

For me this was just the right amount of spice.  It was enough for my lips to have a bit of a tingle but not to blow my head off.  I skipped the oil and used a fat free cooking spray to soften the onions but other than that stuck to everything as written and enjoyed it a lot.  Made for ZWT4.
This looked and tasted truly gourmet. What a great combination of colour and flavour! I'll definitely be cooking this when guests come over :) Cheers!
I dont have a clue as to what went wrong here.  Carrots were fine, but the "glaze" turned out to be a frothy mess.  I'm not sure that I'll try to make these again

My grandmother used to make German meatballs when I was younger as part of her German-heritage repertoire. I've been trying to find a great recipe for German meatballs for years now, and this is the one. Very similar to her original recipe, and very easy to make. Turned out absolutely great the first time I made them, and I'm no chef. Thanks!

So easy to make  in no time at all ~ I chose to put strawberry sangria jam in ours.  This will be a favorite of ours and looking forward to experimenting with different jams.

oh oh so good and definitely not difficult to make.  Spices are quick to measure and it was delicious.

Made this in my pressure cooker and threw in all the ingredients and set the times for 30 minutes. My electric pressure cooker begins timing as soon as the pressure is reached.
