Blows my mind that no one has reviewed this yet.  You have no idea what a great meal you're missing.  I had one whole chicken, so only made 1/4 of the recipe (just in case I didn't like it), which was the perfect amount.  I  flattened the chicken (spatchcock style) then put it and the marinade in a ziplock bag for about 5 hours.  I baked as instructed, and was REWARDED with the most flavourful, moist and tender chicken I've had in a long time.  I served it to company tonight and they were extremely pleased as well.  NC Gal, this is fabulous, and I'll be making more than just 1/4 of the recipe next time.   Honoured to make this as a "Thank You" for voting for Lawrencetown, Nova Scotia in the 2010 Kraft Hockeyville Competition.

I love cilantro and I love this rice!! There is so much flavor in this it's ridiculous. YUM! I added like 6-7 jalapeno rings which my dad had made and WOW oh WOW did it have a bite, but oh so good. I too made the rice on the stove and added the cilantro after the rice had cooked to keep its bright color. Great recipe! Thanks Laura Lee

My grandson was home from college for a few days (quarter break) and I always try and feed him well!!  This casserole helped me accomplish that!!!  We're not big sausage fans, so I cubed some ham and used that instead.  I read some of the reviews and saw where a few had a problem with the crust browing to much -- I didn't find that at all.  In fact, it was perfect with baking it for the 10 minutes.  I did find when I returned it to the oven after adding the filling, I had to bake it a bit longer than the 30 minutes -- probably a good 10-12 minutes longer.  It was wonderful.  This would be a perfect dish to make for an Easter brunch (or any other holiday for that matter).  I've had this marked to try for quite sometime and I'm so glad I finally got around to doing it.  YUM YUM!!!

Wonderful recipe! I used 3 large potatoes instead of 5, substituted one 14oz can of coconut milk for the coconut cream and added 1ich of peeled and grated ginger. Delicious! Worked well for 4 people and went great with rice and chapatis.

These were fantastic! I omitted the stock and sauteed the spinach and onions in olive oil, left out the dill, and added a bit of garlic powder for an extra pop of flavor. All in all these took about 20 minutes to make, and were completely eaten up 5 minutes after that!

I agree with Loula - these are wonderful scones!!  So easy to put together, too.  I halved the recipe, and used pecans instead of walnuts.  Instead of the splenda to sprinkle on top, I had some left over cinnamon sugar that I wanted to use up, so I used that.  My maple syrup was Canadian Amber, unfortunately not sugar free.  And admittedly, I added in some cinnamon chips, because I'm on a bit of a cinnamon chip lovefest right now.  :)  These are truly lovely scones, and will be added to my regular scone rotation - we eat scones for breakfast most days, so it's nice to have another one to add to the variety!  Thanks, Annacia!  Made for 1-2-3 Hits.
This recipe is superb !!  Not only delicious but easypeasy - I actually made a dozen cookies of the 'handful' size.  Crispy and chewy in all the right places.  A must for an energy boosting snack.
DH and I had never made ribs at home.  I found this recipe and he thought they were great!

This was a great idea - I'd never thought of doing chicken cordon blue in my Nu-Wave oven.  I had to make a change because I didn't have any string cheese so I used a slice of Borden Swiss Cheese Singles instead and it worked just fine.  I thought it was absolutely delicious!  Better than the frozen Chicken Cordon Blue you buy in the store for such an outrageous price.  My husband, who really doesn't even like chicken that much, asked me to make it again next week.  Thank you very much for this recipe.  I'll certainly be trying your others!

Something unusual happened last night at dinner - everybody liked it.  I used half & half instead of whipping cream to lighten it up a bit so it was a little runnier than the original recipe would have been.  Next time I will cook the bacon first since I like it a little crispy.  Only spice I added was pepper but I have a similar recipe using some basil that might be good.

SO, SO Good! It's really too bad more people haven't rated this recipe. It really is a keeper. My husband isn't a swiss fan, so I used cheddar and the stuffing was incredible! I will definitely be making this again and again!!
I made these into muffins.  I had the same issue as another reviewer.  the outside was slightly overdone and the inside slightly underdone.  Really like the flavor though.
Loved this! I would reccomend using veganaise instead of mayo.

This was fabulous!  I made it as directed, but for my 6yo, I picked out the potato and meat, pureed with an immersion blender then added the meat and potatoes back in (I knew he would not eat it if he saw the other "stuff" in it).  We all ate our soup, thoroughly enjoying it.  When I was putting the leftovers away, there was a bit of the pureed soup left so I tasted it.  OMG - it was out of this world!  I thought it was excellent to begin with, but blended it was so much better.  Very pleasing texture and flavor.  So much so that I picked the meat and potatoes out of the rest of the leftovers and pureed it before adding back in.  That is how I will be making it from now on.  I will have to figure out a way to have the meat and potatoes in there but easier to remove.  Cheesecloth maybe?  Hmmmmm  Oh, and I might add more kielbasa too!

I knew this would be good before I even prepared as I've yet to taste ANYTHING Kitten has submitted that wasn't just the best :)  The only thing my husband and I both thought after dinner was it needed more curry (for our tastes) I used a teaspoon but will add more the next time - we really like curry.  Thanks Kitten.

I made this as posted today and it was delicious!  I can just imagine it with crawfish or shrimp...can't wait to try it that way.  My sauce didn't get as thick as I would have liked, but that was probably my fault....I may not have reduced the broth wine mix enough in that step.  Thanks for a fabulous lunch today!
WIll make again. Thanks

Very good and very easy. I made this for church leadership meeting. I had put the canned fruit with it but they were better without it. note: I tried to shortcut by mixing all the last parts of the recipe at one time. Do not do this. I could not get them to blend well.

Clear five stars - this is wonderful, better than the alcoholic and dairy one!!! I didn't taste the coconut at all, it was just creamy and coffee-y and I could adapt the sweetness so it didn't become as sticky as the original. This will definitely be a keeper!! Thanks for posting!
Made for PAC Spring 2010.
Tried this tonight with one change - lacked apple juice so subbed orange juice -  was delicious with a nice citrusy taste  -  definitely will make again
I have been looking for this recipe this past year. Its not on the box anymore.I made it alot when we were first married !!!Family favorite!Thanks so much!

Thank you so much for sharing Rita.  My dh & I loved these tasty treats.  They were awesome, crispy, tender and full of flavor.  I loved the addition of the olives to the dish.  They take the flavor to another level, really complimenting the potatoes. This is an excellent recipe that I will make again and again. :)

This was so yummy... thanks for the great recipe!  We topped our burritos with guaucamole, salsa, and light sour cream.  VERY TASTY!  I also used a can of black beans insetad of the refried beans.  I didnt have tomatoes on hand and so I used a can of garlic roasted diced tomatoes.
This is the recipe I have been using for a few years.  It is a must try and everyone loves it!!

This was good but I also made some changes to the ingredients which I think following exactly would probably be 5 stars in my book. Mine turned out 4 stars. I used plain rice milk to be dairy free but could not simmer it with the ginger as I find it separates when that is done. I used brown sugar which was good for this and just left it a longer time to steep removing the orange pekoe teabag I used, when I saw fit. I may make this again before PAC ends with dairy but I am really trying to stay away from that as it gives me health issues. Made for PAC Spring 2010.
Very good moist chocolate cake! I used 2/3 cups hot water and made cup cakes with the batter and had no trouble with the centre falling.This was very good with a Vanilla Icing!

Just realized I forgot to review this.... This ia a great way to use up all that stuffing and get an entirely new dish!  I used monterey jack cheese instead of swiss and a 4 oz can of mushrooms since I didn't have fresh ones on hand.  I'm sure I'll be using this one every year...very good!

I don't know what "andthebrave" is talking about. They must not know how to follow a recipe. But this recipe was delicious!! I think its the best chocolate I have came across yet. Thanks so much for sharing.

Finally, a cole slaw recipe like my grandmothers. Grated cabbage and no mayo.
I omitted the cucumber, for obvious reasons. And I used Cider Vinegar.

I used less sugar but it's great.
I could eat it off a spoon. LOL
PJ.

Dee-lish! My boyfriend gobbled this up like it was nobody's business. I didn't use the suggested seasoning... However, I did use "Emirl's Essence Creole Seasoning" that Chef #649527 posted. I served this with two basted eggs on top and some tomatoes on the side. I love breakfast for dinner! Thank you! :)
This is really good.  I love the stuffing.  I have leftover stuffing and I'm going to use the rest to make burritos tomorrow.

Really good, thanks for posting!  Cut the slices thin.  I also made extra breadcrumbs, which I used to coat some pounded flat chicken.  I baked the eggplant and the chicken at the same time!  Perfect meal timing!
I chose this recipe for PAC 2010. Dh loves blue cheese so this was for him. Great flavor, simple recipe and perfect companion to any host table. Will keep this one !

I made a three layer cake with this recipe for Thanksgiving with Kittencal's chocolate icing recipe and fresh raspberry sauce. It was a huge hit! The cake it amazingly moist! I snuck in just a peck of ground red pepper to give it a tiny punch. Only a few people picked up on it, but those that did loved the extra something. Thanks!

Let me see.....moist, tender, flavourful, easy, and just plain DELICIOUS :)
I made exactly as written, except for making muffins instead of the bread.  I ended up with 10 good sized gems which took 25 minutes to bake in the toaster oven.  I'm thinking next time I might try chopped fresh cranberries for that 'tart-sweet' effect.  Tink, this is a real winner. Honoured to make this as a "Thank You" for voting for Lawrencetown, Nova Scotia in the 2010 Kraft Hockeyville Competition.

These were great!! Although the consensus was MORE CINNAMON...hehe  I added Cinnamon extract even, next time I'll add some ground cinnamon to the batter. We loved these, moist and wonderful, Thanks for the recipe! It's a keeper!

Originally I was gonna cut this recipe in half for 2 of us, but then decided to follow the ingredients 'almost' faithfully, but did use just 2 large chicken breasts (which amounted to 1 lb of chicken)! BK, you have done it again. this is the best take on scalloped potatoes that I have ever tried (even DH gave this 5 stars with a smile!). I made a half recipe and it cooked a lot fasted than I had expected even at 300 degrees so it had to sit a bit before everything else was ready and sadly it lost the "fresh from the oven" bloom before it was pic time. That however, did nothing to diminish the outstanding flavors. There were no leftovers I assure you :D. Yes, its a little time consuming but most of that time is baking time and it really does come together very easily. Try it, you won't be able to stop eating until it gone.

Rather than using oil I used shmaltz and even added some of the grebenes to it. It was really wonderful fresh and slightly warm on matzah. We didn't care for it as much as a leftover. I'll make this again. Thanks for posting.
We love these cookies - each one has a whole heap of choc chips & raisins.  I cooked for 12 minutes & came out golden & perfect. 1st of 3 recipes to review for PAC 2010

I made these for a July 4th cookout and followed the recipe as written, except that I made these in a crockpot.  I prepared the chicken as you would for the oven, but I layered the wings in my oval crockpot and then poured the sauce over the wings.  I cooked then on low for 8 1/2 hours and they turned out perfectly.  They were a big hit at the cookout and were gone almost immediately.  Made for ZWT4 Family Picks.

If you're a 'crispy freak' like me, this cookie will do the job.  They are quite sweet though. The coconut and nuts are wonderful.    Jubes, I may have messed up.  I weighed the 125g of butter which equaled 1/2 cup.  I poured half of the butter/sugar mixture over the dry ingredients.  Anymore than that and you'd be able to drink it. I must have done something wrong.  These baked in 12 minutes in my oven, and yielded 40 cookies.  Honoured to make this as a "Thank You" for voting for Lawrencetown, Nova Scotia in the 2010 Kraft Hockeyville Competition.

Made this last week, my second attempt at cube steak. Such an easy recipe, and really good. Both my husband and 4 yo daughter loved it, I was the iffy one. Made gravy from the pan drippings, which made the cube steak even better. Will be making this again

Very yummy!  This was so simple to prepare, it only took me about 15 minutes.  I keep to the recipe, even used a Tagine and the directions was easy to follow.  The flavours was really yummy, I served it with cous cous and made a perfect meal.  Thank you mersaydees for posting the recipe.
This tastes just like the commercially-made bar.  Mine did not stick together enough to make a bar, but I'm quite happy to eat it as a "granola"

This recipe has the potential to turn my beloved DH into a rabbit.  He LOVED the carrots fixed this way.  Not too sweet, nice shiny glaze, piping hot and fork tender.  The dash of cinnamon is a must in my humble opinion.  Definitely THE finishing touch.  Thanks for a great recipe.

With but one exception, I made this recipe as written ~ For the French bread I did substitute half-slices of a very nutty, dense whole-grain bread, & we thought the whole thing was extremely satisfying! I particularly enjoyed the combo of 4 cheeses used, & will definitely be making this one again! Thanks for sharing it! [Made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in Pick A Chef]

This was easy and filling though not terribly exciting.   I subbed spinach for the peas but otherwise made as written.  I would likely include this in a vegetarian buffet or as part of a larger meal for vegetarian friends - however we are unlikely to make this again as part of the usual rotation.  I suspect this will taste better tomorrow.

Nice one Marie!!! Just what we needed today.  I omitted putting in the egg (as I didn't have any) and the buns turned out fine.  Next time we make these, I'll reduce the sugar a lot (as we prefer less sweet buns) and I'll let them rise a little longer than the recommended 10 minutes.  I add, I've been looking for a good hamburger bun recipe for years -- now I have one.  Thanks again :o)  PS.  Yeast is very reliable now and I recommend you give away the proofing time ... just put the ingredients together, mix, knead, etc.
Excellent soup. Even my DH loved it and he had eaten plenty of it when he was flying helicopters during the war!

Thanks again, Mizz Nezz, you are one of the top chefs on this site, IMHO, and I find myself thanking you again for such as easy, wonderful recipe!  I have posted a couple pics, it's gorgeous!  I bought the butt end of a ham, about 7 pounds, then I had some cans of pineapple tidbits and chunks.  I blended them together with the brown sugar (splenda makes a brown sugar that takes some of the guilt away - and you can NOT taste the difference)  Then, as instructed, put a few cloves in the top (shaped like a heart, how sweet!)  The ham took only two hours with basting every 20 or 30 minutes, I never ended up covering it with foil and it turned out fantastic.  A memorable easter brunch, giving thanks for all that we have and learn each day!  Thank you again, here's to another great Mizz Nezz recipe!

no white casles in OZ...
but tastesd great...
Awsome.  This is my  Easter ham recipes from now on!!!

Very tasty ~ like a spicy brittle!  The nuts were a big hit at our family Easter function.  I used all almonds and kicked up the heat a bit by adding 1/8th teaspoon cayenne, in addition to the red pepper flakes.  I did NOT drain away the lemon juice/egg white mixture ~ I felt the dry mixture would not stick to the almonds if I drained them for 5 minutes!  I checked the almonds after baking for 30 minutes and the almonds were not crisp ~ I baked them for a total of 45 minutes, but next time I will take them out at 42 minutes, so they won't be quite so dark.  Made for one of my Spring PAC 2010 adopted Chefs, and for Rosemary, Herb/Spice for April 2010 in the French forum.

This did not turn out very well for me. I didn't feel there was enough mango in it, and silly of me I didn't buy an extra one at Wegmans. It was also over all very bland to my family. If I make this again I will add more mango and seasonings, and probably use some mango puree or nectar to make a sauce.
One of the vegetables I made for Easter 2010.  It was a huge hit!  Thanks for sharing - a definite keeper.

Wonderful combination of flavors in this salad.  I had to sub iceberg lettuce for the romaine (Cos), but otherwise followed as written including the optional OJ.  I especially enjoyed the oranges and toasted almonds.  Thanks for sharing your recipe.  Made for Went to the Market Tag Game.

Wow, what an awesome cake.  I'm not a huge fan of chocolate cake but thought I'd make this for our family easter lunch yesterday.  Definately the best chocolate cake I've ever had and everyone else raved about it too.  
I greased, sugared and floured my tin which gave a lovely sugar crust to the cake which was great as I didn't ice the cake just served it with whipped cream.
Thanks for such a great recipe Marg.
Though my syrup didn't thicken, it was delicious. I have also made these just using maple syrup, mmmmm good! Thanks for sharing.

Oh I am in trouble now. I LOVE this kind of brownie. Nice and chewy, tastey and great chocolate taste. I didnt have Icing sugar so I made chocolate frosting using Recipe #251093. Thanks for sharing this recipe. Now if I could just stop making them and eating most of them myself.
Wonderful!  I made one change. Because,  I don't like tomatoes, out of season, I used a can of diced tomatoes.   Otherwise followed recipe as directed...delicious!   Thanks, "Uncle Bill"!
Fabulous!! Made this with a raspberry sauce filling and standard buttercream. I cut the sugar to 1.5 cups and it was plenty sweet.
even my hubby who doesn't like tomatoes rated these a 5!
OMG! this is by far the best twice baked potatoes I have ever had or made.  All of my dinner guest raved about them.
It was alright, the flavor didn't seem strong enough. Must be my fault though. I may try it again. My 2 year old ate it up though.
This was good and very easy to throw together. I followed the recipe except I didn't add the water. It took only four hours in my crock pot. It made for a nice dinner. Made for Spring PAC 2010.

WOW am I eating a treat for breakfast this morning!  I blew the whole "low sugar" thing by subbing the walnuts for caramel chips.  SINFUL I must say.  And man did these babies have rise! I will most certainly be making this recipe again!!!!  Thanks my friend!
I made this recipe last summer from the Ball book and it is FABULOUS!!!  I use it every morning in my steel cut oats, makes a very carrot cake like bowl of oatmeal.
This is a simple recipe with great taste,  I cut the recipe in half and I also left off the croutons. I like a cheesy crust on top! Thanks to cburke for posting, Made for PAC Spring 2010.
I have made this twice now, once with chard, and the second time with Beet Greens! I have to say, it is better with chard:)

*I* thought this was really good.  The kids ate it.  Dh was less than impressed.  Oh well.  I cooked my own beans.  I also added extra rosemary because i love the stuff.  Made for you, VIP of the veggie Swap 3/10!  Thanks for another great recipe, Sharon!

I have made these biscuits twice now. Great recipe. My family are so used to hockey puck biscuits they couldn't believe I made these. Soft and scrumptious. They were gone very quickly!

Thanks for the awesome recipe.

Nice replacement for store bought dip.  I only made enough for 1 serving and it was plenty.  I felt it a bit on the salty side so next time I might try Better Than Beef Bouillion.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.  Made for Spring PAC 2010.
This was good and so easy to do.  I used tilapia, and the end result was nicely flavored from the Italian dressing and cheese crackers.  The orange-red color was very pretty as well.
This was good and easy. I was able to roll it out for a double crust also. Thanks for a simple, delicious recipe.

I made this loooong ago, and family loved it.  Just made it last week for Easter, and we enjoyed it all over again.  I appreciate that it is so easy.  I did as someone else had suggested, putting a chopped apple, onion and dried rosemary in with it.  Made excellent gravy and a delicious dinner.  Will make this over and over and over . . .
Omitted the onions, but still fantastic!  Perfect for an easy, super quick side dish!

Loved this soup!  I had some recipe #186628 leftover so I used that instead of baking new potatoes.  The potatoes still had the skins on them but I don't think it altered the flavor any. By far the best chocolate cake I have ever had.  Made this for my sons 2nd birthday and it was a hit there was none left and I'm making it again for my father's 50th birthday.  Thank you so much for this fantastic recipe!!
This is wonderful!  I used chicken thighs and it was fantastic.  Not quite the same as real tandoori, but excellent nonetheless!

Yummy soup! My grandson had 2 large helpings, lol. I made this pretty much as directed except that I microwaved the potatoes as I was running short on time. Loved the flavor and the ease of making this. Thanks Chef #Selah Terry for sharing this great recipe. Made for PAC Spring 2010.

This was delicious and so easy to make. I wanted to add extra flavor to the mayonnaise mix so I used onion, shallots, chopped fresh basil and fresh garlic. My mom makes these muffins, without the blueberries, and substituting 1/4 c oil for the shortening.

As Elise says on her recipe - YOWZA!  Glad to see it posted on Receipezaar!

I made this for DH's dinner. He said he liked it and is looking forward to leftovers tomorrow but said this wasn't his favorite Mac & Cheese. He prefers a somewhat more saucy combo. Made for Spring 2010 PAC

Pretty Tasty! I added an extra teaspoon of ginger and some sliced mushrooms. I def recommend this. Its a refreshing and clean tasting soup. The cilantro really hits the spot in it.
This was delicious!!!  My husband & I LOVED it, it has a great flavor.  Will make it again!!  Thanks for sharing:)
Very nice fruit cake! I made this a few weeks ago, without the alcohol for a childrens birthday party so soaked everything in apple juice instead. I still have people asking me for the recipe now. :D

My husband made this yesterday for his fellow teachers they had "memories" day at school and were to bring something that brought out some sort of memory. From 9/16/2006: I haven't had a chocolate eclair cake in a LONG time. This was SO good! We used fat free pudding, but everything else the same. Yummmy!

I've made alot of chocolate cakes and although this one was good it wasn't great to us. I would recommend trying it however because I think with carmel glaze it's good, but it's not well suited, IMO, for a traditional iced cake.
These were wonderful!  I made them just as described and they were gobbled up before I could have a second one.  We have a 5yo that is a very picky eater, and he could get enough.  Thank you!

I am rating this 5 stars for ease - 4.5 for flavor!  They came out wonderful! I used a cheddar cheese on top and cooked it two minutes longer just like recommended!  This was soooo easy and tasted great!  Thanks for a great and EASY recipe!

Soo good!  I used this recipe in place of the cake mix for Better Than Sex Cake IIi Recipe #3595 and it was a huge hit.  I will definitely use this recipe again.  Really, I don't find it tougher than a cake mix, and it's so ridiculously much better.
Really really yummy!  We will make this again.  Thank you!

OMG, is this one beautiful tasting creme brulee.  I've just gotten back into making creme brulee, and this will definitely go into my special new cookbook!  Thnx for sharing your recipe. Excellent Cole Slaw!  As I was serving it with Pulled Pork I didn't wany any additional meat so omitted the ham.  It was a weekend of "omg I'm missing..." and I did not have raisins. Hubby loves pineapple upside down cake so decided to make these for him. They were easy to make.  I used lite canned peaches, splenda, canola oil instead of veg oil and Splenda brown sugar blend. We all enjoyed these. Made for Spring PAC 2010.

Excellent chicken.  I did use boneless skinless chicken thighs (our preference) instead of chicken breasts.  I liked that fact that these only need to be marinated 30 minutes.  Leftovers were great cold on a salad.  Will be making these again.  Thanks for posting.  Made for Zaar Cookbooks Tag.
This is a recipe my wife and I keep coming back to. Great flavor, easy to make.

Made this and used real thick pork cutlets and let them marinate overnight.  Then I  baked them in the oven at a low temp to give them a chance to be tender. I love key lime pie and this recipe didn't disappoint.  Wonderful flavor and was enjoyed by the whole family.  Made for PAC Spring2010.

I only had 1/2 an English Cuke, but otherwise halved the recipe and it came out AWESOME--and that was before I put it into the fridge.  I'm waiting now for the flavors to meld and to put it on my Chicken Gyros tonight!  Will def make this again!

4/18/10 - I have never been to a White Castle, but I have eaten their frozen mini burgers years ago, and loved them. This recipe made four 6" subs. I have been making/eating onion soup burgers since I was a kid (1lb beef with 1pkg onion soup mix). So I figured I'd like this recipe. I'm not a huge Velveeta fan though. I made one last night and added dill pickles. It was just OK. Tasted better once almost completely cooled down. I just made my 2nd one and added ketchup, it was a little better, but nothing great. I think I'll try this recipe one more time with Cheddar cheese instead of Velveeta.

Yummy macaroni salad!!  I made 1/4 of the recipe to have for lunches.  I followed as written with two exceptions, I didn't add the green pepper (I am the only one in the family that likes it) or the sweet pickle relish.  Really enjoyed this with some crackers!!  This brought back memories of my Mother making this while growing up.  Thanks for sharing made for Spring PAC 2010.

I used this marinade to make chicken kebabs and they were very tasty.  I did strain the marinade, boiled it, and served over rice. Next time I think I would use lower sodium soy sauce as it was quite salty.  Made for PAC Spring 2010.

Great muffin!  Tastes like Fall.  Very dense and moist.  Just the right amount of sweet.  I used dried cranberries and walnuts, and the combination of spices option.  I also made 6 jumbo muffins and baked about 10 minutes longer.  Made for Spring 2010 PAC.

Great vinegar!  Used it to marinate some asparagus for a lunch salad.  The only thing I would do differently is make more than 1 cup at a time :)  I think it would be good in an Asian marinade for chicken also.  Made for Spring 2010 PAC.
Very good and very easy! Thanks!

Oh My this is sooo delicious, one of the best spinach salads ever!! Made half a recipe for a starter for Sunday dinner for the two of us. The "Dressin" is fantastic, great flavour. We will be having this one often, thanks for posting.

I made this to take to the race track. Everyone always seems to end up our our racing trailor for food. Imade this as written and everyone enjoyed this. This was a bit of work for me but it was well worth it. Made for Spring PAC 2010.

This recipe is fantastic! It goes so well with so many dishes.  I follow the recipe as seen here, but also add about a tablespoon or so of ghee.  I often need to add a little more flour, but that's probably due to my own error rather than the recipe.  Anyway, it ends up turning out perfectly every time!  Thank you so much for sharing!
Great flavor but I forgot how fatty Short Ribs are.  I marinated overnight then slow cooked them in oven then finished on the grill.

I'm pretty unexperienced when it comes to bread, and find the whole process a little intimidating. That being said, this recipe was SUPER easy! Used only 3 tbsp oil and sugar each, and next time I will leave out the egg. These are pretty dense which is perfect for the sloppy joes I'm serving them with - 'cuz no one wants soggy buns, right!?? THANKS for the recipe. I'm going to try to make bread sticks with them.

I really enjoyed this pizza.  I would have never thought of the goat cheese/sausage/grape combination, but it really works!   I used Recipe #199332 199332 for the crust.  I probably used fewer grapes, sausage, and goat cheese than your directions stated because it seemed too much for the amount of crust I had.  Rather, I just eye balled the ingredients and used enough to cover my sized crust.  The only other change I made was that we grilled the pizza versus baking it, which was awesome!  Very nice recipe--I'll definitely have it again.  Thanks!
Easy and delicious.  I omitted the salt (personal preference).  I did, indeed, have leftover baked potatoes, so this was nice and quick to prepare.  Thanks for sharing!  ~PAC Spring '10~

Yummy! These were delicious. I usually don't get Castle burgers too often (thats what we had in New Orleans). I love them and try to get them when I go visit. These tasted just like them to me especially with the pickle and mustard, which i did not put on until we were about to eat. I followed the recipe exactly. My grocery store had potato rolls which are almost exactly like the white castle buns. Hubby loved them. Will definately make again and again. I'm so glad I came across this recipe.

Good! I made this just as the recipe stated. I couldn't believe that I had all the ingredients on hand, except for the bell peppers. I really enjoyed this with the different herbs and spices. Nothing was overpowering, just well balanced and tasty. I added a few crumbled corn chips, fresh tomatoes, and salsa for a wonderful taco like salad. This filling can be used for so many different dishes (nachos, tacos, tiny meat pie filling etc). Because of the amounts of bell peppers and onions I will probably use diced canned Mexican style tomatoes next time instead of the salsa picante sauce.
I made half a recipe and used yellow mustard seeds.  Will try black next time.
I enjoy this recipe, with many different names, because it's simple and good too! Thanks! Made for New Kids on the Block game.

I made only one insignificant change in this recipe, substituting as I did lemon pepper for the salt & pepper! Well, I did also use rotini instead of macaroni, but that's no big thing! This all came together very easily & made for a very nice mid-day meal! [Made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in the current round of Pick A Chef] Want to know more about PAC? Click here = http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewtopic.zsp?t=327498
Excellent!  Followed this recipe exactly, using Dutch Process chocolate.  Easy recipe, which is a plus.  Topped this off with Italian Buttercream and an Oreo filling.  Huge hit!

I can not comment on this one myself as I am not a gin lover I made this for my DH who said it was very good and light and refreshing. I took Amandas advice and used the lemongrass swizzle stick as well which actually makes for nice presentation as well. He said he would definitely enjoy this again instead instead of just a regular G&T. I will be making again next weekend when we are having company over for a BBQ. Thanks for sharing.

I can't believe I forgot to rate this!  I was looking for different ways to use up Thanksgiving leftovers and ran across this recipe....and I'm so glad I did!  I made it using a leftover root vegetable mash and they were so light and fluffy!  I'm keeping this one!

This was the recipe I used to make my first cheesecake EVER and it was simple and yummy.  Everyone at my family gathering loved it, I was so glad I made three of them, otherwise there wouldn't have been enough to feed everyone.  And you don't have to make the praline sauce if you don't want, I've used fresh fruit, cherries and I've even drizzled chocolate and caramel over it.
Fish Sauce is potent if you aren't used to salty food. I would reduce in half. Ohter than that the recipe would taste really good.
Enjoyed this pork recipe. Made for PAC 2010.
Great ginger cookie! For the mixed spice I used a mix of allspice, mace and a little cinnamon. They're not very sweet but very spicy, just how I like it. Thanks for sharing! Made for Spring PAC 2010.

Loved this, although I admit that I reduced the tomato juice so I could have more like a chile.  I had 8 ounces of hot Italian sausage left over, so used that, and I think that amount with the other ingredients it was sufficient.  I also used 1 tbsp. of recipe#66591 instead of chile powder, so with the extra spice from the sausage, and the heat from the taco seasoning I really appreciated the sour cream topping.

We really enjoyed this.  Great flavor 
Thank you for posting

Hi Tallie.  This was made for dinner tonight.  It was delicious.  I'm only giving it four stars, because I messed up and bought the wrong kind of beans. I grabbed Pinto beans, which are a variety of kidney bean.  Another thing, I left out the potato.  I thought it would be too much with the brown rice and the beans.  Other than that, everything was the same.  I sliced my baby carrots in half and some thirds.  This was also made for 2 servings.  I did my best on ingredient amounts.  On the side were just simple Saltines.  Thank you for the hearty Friday night dinner..... for Spring PAC 2010.

Fabulous! I made this an served over couscous (my first injera attempt missed the mark). Followed the recipe to the letter, using my dutch oven. Nice heat, wonderful appearance, flavor, and aroma! We ate on the porch, and our neighbors practically invited themselves to dinner after smelling my wat! Thanks for a keeper!

WOW!  I don't usually make dips but wanted to give it a try.  What a great recipe to start out on - it was fantastic.  I was excited to buy asiago cheese since we rarely have anything but good old St. Louis Provel rope cheese.  Made exactly as directed and it turned out great.  Making it again in 2 weeks for a big sisters get together.  Thanks!  Made for PAC '10.
Great Cake!

I made a trio of dips tonight as I was having several people over and every single one was an absolute hit. I had several people say how great this dip was how light and fresh it was.. I used a jalapeno pepper and also used half a white onion and half a red. I made extra of the recipe hence using a whole onion, as I was having so many people round. This is one of the nicest salsa combo's I have tried. I served this along side your Recipe#369631 and Mandy's Recipe#403579, Both a big hit as well. Fabulous recipes thanks for sharing CHILI SPICE

Although we definitely enjoyed this soup, I probably took the 'Texas' right out of it by using just 1 small jalapeno pepper as well as reducing the amount of red pepper flakes & Tabasco sauce! Still much enjoyed the combo of flavors in this great soup ~ Thanks for sharing the recipe! [Made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in the current Pick A Chef]

My girls loved the book, and it's my younger daughter's favorite cake. We use a GF flour cake for a GF/CF version and frost with or favorite GF/CF chocolate frosting. I bake as 2 8" rounds with frosting between layers and on the outside. Put strawberries on top. I used to put sliced berries between the layers, but the girls didn't like it...an oft-requested birthday cake in our house.
I made this exactly as directed and it is wonderful.  We had it with shrimp and beef tempura and it was a great dipping sauce.  Thanks for sharing.

This took NO time at all! I read through sooo many of the reviews and got really excited to make this cake and it still went above and beyond my expectations! I used 1 1/2 cups of sugar and 3/4 cup boiling water.. also added a tiny bit of instant coffee for a little oomph. The cake is actually still cooling down right now, but I used a bit of the batter to make mini chocolate cupcakes and those are DELICIOUS! Only took 10 minutes for those to bake, then I topped those with some frosting (89207) and chocolate sprinkles and oh man, I am so excited to share both the cake and cupcakes with everyone. Baked the cake in a rectangular pan (mine was a touch smaller than 13x9 so it only took like 32 minutes to be perfect) The cake hasn't sunk at all! Rose beautifully and it's still ginormous! Can not wait to ice it and dive in. I'll have to try a round layered cake next time too! Thank you so much!!! :)

I have used this recipe twice, with wonderful results! The cake is so moist and fluffy, not to mention delicious. I have cupcakes in the oven right now... I thought I'd steal your dad's idea and freeze them. ;) Thanks so much for posting this!

If I could give you 10 stars I would. have searched for a really good recipe like this for a long time, and have never found anything this good before. It also adapts to other spices and herbs, so its fun to try out different blends, but for me, this original recipe is the 'tops'. Many thanks

What a delicious cake.  It is not a spongy cake but firm and wonderfully flavorful.  I made it as my granddaughter's birthday cake and what an abundance of compliments I got on the taste of the cake.  It will definately be put in as one of my favorites.

We loved this substantial salad! Even my husband, who prefers bleu cheese dressing, liked the vinaigrette. I couldn't get to the store, but this salad survived substituting green pepper & scallions for the cucumber and American cheese for the provolone. A great way to use up stale bread, but you can bet that next time I will make it exactly as written. :)

wonderful cake! Easy and delicious! I wouldn't reccomend using this recipe for cupcakes they are really flat on top instead of round and pretty, but in a sheet cake it turns out wonderful! I used a whole cup of water and it stayed very moist! thanks for posting
Awesome! I didn't have the cardamom or the turmeric, so I just made everything else just as written and my husband ate nearly all of it himself!! This is a certain keeper!!

Ooh yum!  In cleaning out the freezer I found a bag of whole wheat mini bagels that were getting a tad freezer burned, and half a bag of frozen cranberries that was also almost past its prime.  So this was a great way to use them up on an unusually cool day.  I used skim milk and all egg whites, and half sugar/half splenda.  Instead of the pumpkin pie mix I used the equivalent amount of pumpkin butter and cut down on the spices since the butter has plenty of it.  This was very very good.  Nice pumpkin taste plus the tartness of the cranberries.  One I'd like to try again in the fall.
Very tasty! I really enjoyed the flavor and texture of these chops. They came out nice and crispy on the outside, and tender and moist on the inside. Thanks so much!

I made it this morning before going to work.  I liked that it was easy to do in just a few minutes.  This was perfect.  I loved the taste.  I omitted the salt and pepper.  Thanks Lori :)  Made for Holiday tag

I made 1/4 the recipe and had my evening snack of cucumber and celery with 1 tablespoon of dip. The entire recipe makes about 4 cups so the serving size needs to be adjusted for the calorie count to be more reasonable.
I figure (and my math is not so great) about 500 calories per tablespoon(?)
Well anyway it was delicious and if I watch how often I eat it I will be okay with the calories. Thanks for posting a keeper Pink Diamond.

Wow, what a great recipe! Tonnes of flavour and colour - the cheese was a great little twist, I'm like "cheese in a casserole, no way!" but it was a fantastic addition. Easy (Must say though, I think Italian pork sausages are somethng different here in Australia since they were raw and darned hard to cut!) and bursting with flavour, perfect when it starts to get cold outside. Outstanding dish!
Awesome!  This was a yummy treat to use up some leftover coconut cream and pineapple.  Thanks for posting. :)

Very good!  I never thought of putting kiwi and bananas together and it tasted great!  Also, added a few frozen strawberries.  Yum!  It's very versatile.  I added some yogurt, vanilla, and that tasted good, too.  Thank you.
My DH was all over this soup!  He loved it!  I thought it was ok.
This was sooo delicious!  We halved the recipe for a family of 4.  I also added a little lemon juice in the butter and a dash of cayenne in the breadcrumb mixture.  Yummy!

I really enjoyed this turkey!  I added some rosemary and garlic under the skin and poured HOT broth over the top, the heat tightens up the skin and locks in the flavor!  I also added one onion cut into rings and a chopped apple.  My crock pot bakes really hot so I only cooked for about 5-6 hrs.  Thanks for the great recipe, the flavor is perfect.
I made this for a baby shower and they were fantastic and pretty. I put them on croissants! Thank you.
Oops! I forgot to blend this tasty drink but I dont think it suffered. Flavor was great. Thanks:)

Delicious and easy recipe -- my favorite kind!  I used a low-sodium soy sauce and might decrease the salt next go round just to lower the sodium further but it is delicious as is.  I didn't need all of the dressing so with the leftover salad, I cooked up more noodles the next day, added them in to the leftover salad with the leftover dressing, and added grilled chicken to make it a dinner salad.  This is one fabulous and versatile recipe and amazingly is just as good leftover as the day you make it.  Thanks, Caroline, for sharing!
YUM!  I made orange peel, carefully carving off the pith so the pieces are quite thin, and crunchy.  Outstanding!

I also used Yoplait frozen fruit pouches (basically just has a bunch of raspberry, blueberry and strawberry), which had been in my freezer for a REALLY long time because the recipes they had on the box tasted pretty gross. I made it your way using Dreyer's strawberry sherbet and did a little less than 1/2 cup sugar. I made it another time and added a little less than 1/4 cup orange juice. Came out great!  Thank you!!!

I really liked this. But it had too much mayo for my taste. I added some extra vinegar and that made it much better. I don't particularly like mayonnaise, so I should have known that 1/2 cup would be too much for my tastes.

I really was fasinated by this combination of ingredients -  I, too, love pepper and I loved the recipe - Takes seconds to put together - give it a chill and there you have it a lovely lead in to breakfast or any meal or serve as a light dessert

I made many revisions on this recipe, and it was still delicious! I cut the recipe in half and used Ezekial 4:9 sprouted grain penne pasta, raw cheddar cheese (just cheddar - no parmesan) and I only had 1c. cream, so I used water for the other 1c. of milk. Plus, I added about 1/2 bag of frozen peas to the mix and topped with some more shredded cheese. It was delicious! And all my kids ate it up too!
This really is good. The sauce was delicious. Sweet with a little kick. I will kick it up a bit more next time, and there will be a next time. Thank you for sharing!

I love date squares but I've never made them.  It was my first time and they were perfect.  But I had trouble to spread the date mixture.  Maybe it was too thick.  I'm sure pecans would be great in that but I'm used to date squares without nuts.  The oatmeal layer is very good.  I used cold butter and had a hard time to cut in butter LOL  I cooked the squares about 28 minutes.  They're so yummy.  Thanks baby kato :)  Made for Holiday tag game

Sometimes you  forget how really great simple little things are...it's been years since I had minted peas,and I simply cannot remember why I haven't been eating them, as they are just delicious.
Thanks for the reminder!!!
Made for 1-2-3 Hits.

Wow, such delicious cake!  I find it so interesting that Annacia's cake turned out so much darker than mine did!  I used the ground coffee, and cooked it as described, but only got 1/4 cup of thick, rich, coffee flavoured milk from it, so I added 1/4 cup of milk to make up the 1/2 cup.  Like Annacia, I doubled the cinnamon.  This is such a tender and gorgeous cake, and reminds me so much of spice cake.  I love it!  I did realize this morning that I didn't have any round pans (well, I can't find them), so I baked it in an 8x8 square pan, and it turned out perfect in 30 minutes.  Thank you so much for posting this!  Made for 1-2-3 Tag.

This is like the Hershey's cake recipe I've been using for years, because I did use the regular unsweetened cocoa as I didn't have dark or dutch processed (can't wait to try that way) and DH doesn't like dark chocolate and it was for his bday.  Turned out yum as usual;  I halved the recipe and made it in a glass 8x8 dish for 35 min. and subbed almond extract for the vanilla (as I usually do) and added just a splash of vanilla extract.  It turned out just as good as when I make it in a 13x9. Thanks for posting!

I cut this recipe in half to serve 3 of us& also used a Vadalia onion instead of a red one! And, although I wanted my salad without the dressing I did put it together for my other half & our friend! This is a very simple & refreshing salad, & I particularly enjoyed the seeds (& I was generous when adding them)! [Made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in this Spring's Pick A Chef event]

These are fantastic and very healthy mashed potatoes. My BIL and his 14 yo grandson both had 2nd helpings and I had no leftovers. I did add 1 TBS. dry minced onions to the potatoes as I boiled them for a little extra flavor (no added calories!) Thanks for posting a winner Lori!

We really enjoyed this dish! I used didn't have cream so I used 1/2 1/2 (and thickened with a tiny bit of corn starch) and added green peas! Fantastic and easy week night dish. Thank you for sharing!!

Made this for the DS to take to his music recreation group were it was enjoyed.  Glad I spent $6.50 on a candy thermometer as it took nearly 30 minutes before mine got to hard-crack (300F) stage.  I did have to used golden syrup for the corn syrup as we can't get corn syrup here.  When making again I think I need to distribute it over two pans, for though I used the largest one I have (lamington/jelly roll size) I felt it was to thick.  Thank you wicked cook 46, made for 123 Hit Wonders.

OMG... this was so good, quick and easy.  The result is a lovely flavored toffee that is not too hard, just perfect, semi-soft and chewy, with a great flavor. We loved this.  Thanks for sharing wicked...I'll be making this treat again. :)
Wow, these were really good! I would have given 5 stars but they had too much fat, next time ill use some evoo, instead of butter and skip the boil and just cook longer.. but still a great recipe...

Fixed this last night for dinner and followed the directions except for adding some green onions along with the rest and sprinkled some on top.  Delicious!  Next time I think I will add some garlic (love garlic) but I can hardly wait to have some fresh tomatoes to use.  Thank you.  Made for Zaar Alphabet Soup game.

We enjoyed this flavorful frittata for dinner.  I would have never thought to add soup mix!  I also substituted frozen broccoli florets and used butter.  Thanks for posting.  Made for Went to the Market tag.

I have made this many times over the past year and every time I love it! I have used in snack towers and as a gift on it's own. I use a chiptole chili powder which gives the nuts a really nice smokey flavor. An added benefit is that the house smells great while they cook! My one piece of advice is if you are planning on giving them as a gift, wrap them quickly before you eat them all, they are very addictive!

I would not call them cheesecake, but they are great none the less. The crust reminds me of a lemon square bar. I will make these again and maybe next time use a graham cracker crust. May make it a bit more like cheesecake.

This was superb. We think cinnamon with meat is ick, so we left it out, and we wanted a one-dish meal so we added a minced  zucchini with the onion. Just the right spice -- enhancing the meat without overpowering it. The leftovers are even better.

Oh, yum!  This recipe is a real gem.  I only made minor changes- I started with raw shrimp, and added them with the bok choy, I also added salt with the peppers and pea pods, but just a little and I always season my veggies when they go in the pan.  I chose hoisin and sesame oil instead of the cooking oil and stir fry sauce- I really think the hoisin was key to making this such a treat.  
I also chose to add the optional pepper flakes, which I put in at the very beginning while the oil was heating, in order to carry the flavor to everything the oil touched.  This had the best qualities of a weeknight meal- fast, easy, and tasty!  Thanks for posting a winner!
easy, tasty kid friendly!!

The mayo turned out great, really enjoyed it.  I wiped my eggs with vinegar.  I think the soap might do more harm than good.  Also the acid in the vinegar would really make this okay to take to a picnic.  No potato salad at a picnic is a fallacy.  There have been quite a few research papers written on this subject.

This was an easy to make, spicy risotto, which we enjoyed.  I recently stayed at a vineyard B&B in Traverse City and we picked wild ramps growing in the woods on the property, which I used in this risotto.  We used more Italian sausage than specified, which I kind of regretted--too meaty.  I think the 1/2 lb is likely a perfect proportion.  Other than that, we made no modifications to the ingredients or directions.  Thanks!

I am extremely mayonnaise-making challenged. I've failed at it many times. This recipe, however, worked for me using my food processor.  It produced one of the smoothest and creamiest mayonnaises for me.  What I've learned is that the mayonnaise doesn't really begin to take shape until I've poured in about 3/4th of the oil.  I added 1 minced clove of garlic.
This works pretty well. I can see myself useing it again, however i wish the outcome was a litle more crispy. Used for eggplant sandwiches with provolone and tomato. Thanks for the recipe!
Gr8

The cake is perfect. moist, soft , texture is just what you want, it just melts in the mouth. i did have to keep it for 45 mins, i think its just my oven, and i used 3/4 glass water at the end.. on the whol;e everyone licked their plates even my  2 year old son.. 

i tried the buttercream frosting with regular sugar since i didnt have confectioners sugar.. came grainy, so next time will be doing just as per the recipe.. great for a birthday cake too will  be making the same for my son's 2nd.. Thank you for the recipe
My family really enjoyed this recipe.  Great flavor and very simple to make.  I didn't add a thing!

my bf likes pineapples so i'll attempt this again, but it lacked oomph and the peppers and onions were overdone.  i used tony's and sesame oil, but otherwise followed the recipe.  next time i'll add the veggies later and perhaps some chili oil.

The recipe has good potential, I felt more like I was making a soup than anything else though, and the lemon juice was a liiiiittle to bright for mine and hubby's taste.  What I might do next time is make the lemon juice be 1/16c and the broth 1/2c.  That might solve the brightness issue and soupiness, I believe it's a good recipe otherwise :)

Delicious! I had everything pre-cut, which made this come together super quick (plus I used my immersion blender right in the pot). I used low sodium chicken stock rather than the water and chicken soup powder. This was quick and very tasty, two requirements for a after-work meal. Thanks for posting!

This was GREAT meatloaf!  I've tried several meatloaf recipes here, but this is my new fave.  Love the addition of garlic.  I did add some onions and ketchup to the meat mixture before baking....personal preference.  And I put a LOT of ketchup on top.  My husband immediately said "mmmmm" and he is very picky about meatloaf.  Will be my go to for meatloaf from now on.
This is a great basic dip.  But to like it more, I would try to add some spices to it.  This could be great to dip some fondue meat.  Thanks Terri :)  Made for Healthy tag game

I scaled this back from serves 24 down to serves 4 because I needed a chocolate drizzle for recipe #408114 .  I really liked the consistency of the finished sauce.  On its own, for me, it was a little too bittersweet but adding it as a topping to a sweet dessert, it was fine.

Simple side dish that is delicious!  I love snap peas and pecans, so I knew this would be a great combo!  Next time, I will cut down on the butter a tad, maybe 2 Tbsp, but otherwise it was perfect.  Thanks Lori!  Made for Holiday tag.
I served this as a side with our Mother's Day dinner. It was very well received! I loved the fresh taste, crispness of the cucumbers and the lovely scent and taste of the dill. It was healthy, too!

wow- with 5 extremely fussy kids to feed this is one of my best find recipes ever! they all love it and it is good for them too.just add a side salad and it  works with a tin of tuna thrown in too. delicious!
I too had this as a child but had forgotten the recipe. I now cook for my Mom and she will be tickled to get this forgotten treat. Thank you so much.
I made this 3 times already.  Really good.  I didn't have enough butter so I replaced half of it with olive oil and it came out great.
Very Good Liver Pate, I made it with the Hard Boiled Egg and use it in the Individual Beef Wellington Dish.

Wow! This is a great recipe!  I used whole wheat flour with a little wheat germ and brewars yeast to make it a little healthier.  I also replaced the white sugar for 1 cup of turbinado (sugar in the raw).  Have made it with walnuts too.  It is always a big hit and a great way to use up the rhubarb.  A favorite at work and even with my pre-schoolers!  Thank you Kate, for sharing!!

Made this 2 weeks ago for while visiting friends, they loved it!!! Used a huge mahi mahi fillet and 2 sword fish steaks, only marinated it for about 40mins....but basted the entire time on the grill.  Came out great! Will be making it again for another friends Bday, will try to let it soak a bit longer this time!!!

I didn't think this recipe was terrible but I won't be making it again. The sauce was pretty heavy and overwhelming - even though I added a cup of water before tuning it on. It didn't taste like Thai at all to me. Some soy sauce and lime juice does not a Thai meal make. My husband and 3 year old daughter liked it though. It was super easy though - I threw in carrots at the start and they were pretty good.

Very easy to make, even with the kids around. My batch only needed 2 minutes in the microwave. The stirring every 30 seconds is a must because you have a crust around the edges that has to be stirred in.
The kids loved making this and played with it for hours.
Yum Yum! I made these as directed and loved them! Simple and very good. Soft inners and crispy outers. Thanks A Messy Cook for a nice treat. Made for Alphabet Chef Soup Tag.

Yum! These turned out like an eggy muffin. I didn't use olives because I had none on hand, and I actually used Monterey Jack cheese since thats all I had (I know, I know...the recipe is based on the manchego cheese :) ) Regardless it was good! Mine were done after 15min
Very good, and easy to prepare!  We loved the flavors from the bell pepper, onion, and chili peppers.  Thanks for sharing!

Yummy, yummy oatmeal!  But then again, oatmeal is my favorite breakfast food.  The combination of fruits is wonderful and I love the tartness from the cherries.  I did scale it down to one serving and will definitely make this again.  Thanks for posting this.  Made for Healthy Choices ABC.
These are simply delicious! Thanks for sharing.

Simply DELISH!!  My hubby's favorite dessert. His grandma makes it every year at Christmas and I've never made it until now, thanks to you!! This  very simple and easy to make, light and smooth after a heavy meal.  My hubby thanks you for this one!!
Great dessert.  Just sweet enough.  I didn't have ruby port, so substitute grape juice/lime juice.  No bad at all
This was a brilliant pudding, very lemon and good for non vegans who think vegan food tastes bad.

I am so bad... I have been making this for a long time and did not give it a review at all to give credit where credit is due.  I want to say this is such a great dish and that the hubby just loves it.  We switch the light rum for a dark (Captain Morgan's Rum specifically).  This is a great recipe!  We usually make this with a veggie or mashed potatoes.  Thank you so much!  This is a winner!
These were good but I found the estimated cooking time way off.  My bars were in the oven for 12 minutes longer than suggested, and usually my oven cooks things on the quicker side.
So very good!!! I also used diced tomatoes and added a can of pinto beans. We love this and it makes too much for 2 of us so plenty goes in the freezer. Thanks for posting.

Best cupcakes ever! My tins must have been a bit smaller as I got 15 muffins from the recipe. Definitely use the coconut milk! Well I found a way to screw this up big time, but I recovered it a bit.  I didn't realize that my can of chiles that I was throwing in was twice the size of what is stated here in the recipe.  When I tasted it straight out of the oven, it was so hot and spicy that it was barely edible.  I stirred in some sour cream and fat free half & half to tame some of that spice.  It worked pretty well, and it made for a delicious creamy version of this.  I want to make it again the right way, and just throw in a couple of jalapeno rings because I would still prefer that to my creamy version.  I was glad I could salvage it though :-) Great recipe for all of us cilantro lovers...just don't overspice like I did ;-)

Awesome!!!
These tasted fantastic, were gone so quick and I've already had to pass on the recipe.

Also, is there any reason you only use egg whites?  Do you think I could use 2 whole eggs next time instead?
Anyway, thanks for a great recipe Bev.

Flower - this is a nice sweet dressing and so simple to make.  I made as directed but just reduced the servings in half so I did not have so much leftover.  I have the remaining dressing saved in a sealed container to use later this week.  I served it over romaine lettuce with green onions and mandarin oranges and slivered almonds.  Made for your win in Tag Tic Tac Toe.

Boomie - this is a great idea and craft project to make with my grandson!  It took just 3 minutes in my microwave and that stirring process if most important.  It is so easy to do that making many colors is not an issue at all.  Keeping it in zippered baggies and it is still soft 3 days later.  :)

Easy to prepare and really delicious. I also replaced the onions with shallots and got very good results. 

Sauce has a great, rich consistency without being at all goopy or heavy. Will make this again!
My husband and I enjoyed this, and my dd did when she picked out the kale. Simple, healthy--will definitely make it again!
Works perfectly!
This was a big hit at Willies Rear....I added some Northern Fruits Leelanau Crushed Strawberries from Brownwood Farms on top before topping and cooked it in a big Springform pan...Turned out perfect.

When i got it right these were delicious! It was the first time i ever tried eggplant and what a great introduction. I only had enough parmeson cheese for my first batch and then when i topped up the breadcrumbs i added too much seasoning and was a little too overpowering and on my third batch i equalled out the seasoning and tastes much better but my overall verdict is its 10 times better with the parmeson and the right amount of seasonuing lol. Also when cutting the slices, thinner cuts are better than thicker cut. I served this dish with Recipe #211485. TY james i loved this

Delicious and moist!  I used Splenda in place of the sugar and love the fact that you use applesauce instead of oil.  I only had a large can of pureed pumpkin, so I ended up making 3 loaves.  I gave one loaf to my in-laws, 1 loaf to my son's family and took 1 loaf to work.  Everyone loved this pumpkin bread.  Made for May 2010 Aus/NZ Swap.

This was very tasty! I used light cream cheese and added chives and bacon.  Yum yum! Like another reviewer, I spread the cheese on both pieces of bread so it held the extras better. Thanks for sharing :)

I cut the recipe in half, used cream of mushroom soup and didnd't measure the cheese or sour cream, I just dumped it in. I also put my tator tots in the microwave for 5 minutes to thaw them and then crumbled them on top. I cooked at 350 for 20 minutes, then topped with a bit more cheese and let it melt. We all enjoyed this. I also served the green beans on the side.

Yum! I made these last night, mainly for DH and I. (my little ones are just to picky) We enjoyed these a lot, and had left overs for lunch today. I normally have the thai chili paste on hand so I added it. These things were spicy. So if your not a spicy eater, then these aren't for you! I loved them. Simple to put together, not time consuming, and just different from your everyday burrito. Thanks for sharing!

This is an unusual dish, and it's pretty tasty. Like others, I also changed it a little.  The cookbook I have has different amounts of salsa and peanut butter, so I followed that.  It's more salsa (1 cup) and less peanut butter (1/4 cup).  It works great with rice.
Made this last night for my boyfriend and he loved it!  Followed the directions to a T except doubled the sauce.  Thanks for a keeper!

This title of this recipe pretty much says it all! We used ground turkey instead of beef and chili sauce instead of ketchup, and halved the recipe (there's only 2 of us). Other than those changes, I followed the recipe exactly. It was delicious right out of the over, but it DOES get better over time (had the leftovers for lunch today!). With my changes, I calculated this recipe to 3 WW points/serving with 8 servings. Thanks for sharing, we will definitely be making this again!

I almost forgot to rate this recipe!  I used this on our green tomatoes last fall...great recipe!  I omitted the sugar just because I forgot and it was still very good!  My husband and I are addicted to this salsa...I liked it best after freshly made.  He liked it best after it was canned.  Thanks for a great recipe!

Indulgent treat!! Love my coffee, but this was a rich dessert to follow a good meal!!! Thanks for posting.
ZWT6
This is very good.  I wish I had stirred the glaze more before I served it!   It's actually thicker than it looks in the picture.  ZWT6

A sweet decadent after dinner coffee. There was so much flavor, I was able to add some additional coffee to make it last longer! Well, I tried anyway, it went down way too fast! Made for ZWT 6 by a fellow Unruly Under the Influence.

Fantastic!! Served gyro-style with falafel, tomato, red onion and tzatziki. If you are making these for Gyros I advise using the pan-method. Baked a few in the oven at first but they were not pliable or "bendy" like you want for gyros. So I moved on to using a pan and got great results. They were softer, more pliable, and prettier too. The trick for making "stuffable" gyro bread seemed to be to roll them very thin, almost too thin it might seem at first, before adding to the pan. They will poof up in the pan to the perfect thickness and the larger diameter is nice. Super recipe! Thank you, Najwa~
Really good! Maybe not exactly White Castles, but so easy to make and so tasty.

Very good!  The only thing I didn`t get the cherry flavor. The Grand Marnier overpowered it. Whipped cream would be delightful on this topped with a cherry a chocolate covered cherry. Thanks made for ZWT 2010.

Perfect chocolate cake!  I can't believe I ever used to use cake mix - this is worlds better!  I've used this recipe for cupcakes, tier cakes, and sheet cakes - all have come out wonderfully.  Perfectly moist and soft without falling apart when you work with it.  Thanks for a great recipe!!
Yummy drink! This was simple and smooth. Thanks momaphet for a nice treat. Made for ZWT6 fellow Unruly Under the Influence.

Yum! I made the non alcoholic version using just a little orange juice concentrate. Loved the cherry flavor(I eyeballed the amount). This is really yummy.  I made this recipe exactly as written and wouldn't change a think.  We loved the sauce....so delish.  I plan on making this again multiple times this summer.  Thank you for sharing this recipe with us.
Easy, tasty and quick to whip up.  The addition of the peas and coriander add a nice color to the soup.  The sesame oil is a wonderful touch of flavor.  Thanks for sharing!

I don't usually drink coffee in the afternoon, but on occasion I have an urge to drin it, and I decided to go the ZWT route this time. Never thought to combine these ingredients together, but I just love it. I like the idea of warming my milk for it, since I find cold milk will sometimes cool my coffee and this just helps keep it warm. Will be trying this again!

We really enjoyed this but I want to comment without stars.  We're serious "spicers", but the crushed red pepper flakes overpower any of the delicate flavors in this.  Fresh basil is lost in the wake of all that fire.  I WILL make this again because it's tasty and low-fat, but next time I'll just put a pinch of crpf or cayenne.  Thanks for creating such a healthy dish.

We loved this chicken recipe!! I used the herbs de provence because I served buttered noodles with caraway seed (#348013) with it and didn't want the rosemary to compete with the caraway. I'm sure it will be good with the rosemary too.
The fennel and beet were wonderful in this dish. I will be making this again, for sure. Thanks for sharing the recipe. Made for ZWT6.
If you like Blue Cheese these are just what you are looking for!  They went  fast at my last family gathering, and will be made again for sure!
Really good! I did make them with cannoli shells. I added an extra 2 teaspoons of cocoa powder to these, I think I could have done even more!
I do agree that the cake needs to be at least a day old to hold the icing well... I usually add 2tablespoons of melted butter to the icing. We love lamingtons!

As the previous reviewer said I had to leave it in the oven for an extra 45 minutes as it wasn't fully cooked. I did a twist on the recipe and used chicken loins and wrapped the bacon around it. turned out really yummy

My family wasn't thrilled with the onion, but skipping it alltogether produced an incredible easy to make meal. Served with young boiled potatoes, it made my family gorge themselves in a very unseemly manner :)

Great egg drop soup!!!  I loved the added flavor from the sesame oil which really distinguished it from other egg drop soups.  I made 1/4 of the recipe for my lunch today with fried rice.  I left out the peas, just not what is normally in the soup and I am not a huge fan of them.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!  Made for ZWT6.
A very different but nice change to the alternative.  Fresh comes to mind.  My husband loved it and it has been requested again.

This is DELICIOUS, and very easy. I was surprised that I could get such good depth of flavor from a soup made this quickly. A little tip: I add about a teaspoon of roasted chili paste at the end. It's one of my favorite Asian condiments, and gives it even more depth of flavor without making it too spicy. Thanks for the great recipe!
Tired of the same old peas and porridge? Ya need to try recipe #426144. Made for ZWT #6.

This is a very fragrant dish while cooking. Yummy garlic. But I found this symple and bland. Which is great for people like my DS that likes it like that. This is part of Menu #39593 menu.

I was also wondering about the noodles. Because they are normally soaked before adding to the dish. BUT this worked great!

This is a good recipe for those no eating flour. I did add low sodium soy for taste. Cilantro was a nice topper but I didn`t add till I started eating.  After photo was taken.  This has many possibilities.  Made for ZWT 6 . Thanks.

Yum!  I made this for dinner today.  I didn't feel like pie crust, so I used a tube of crescent rolls that I pressed into a circle.  I love ratatouille to begin with, so I knew I would love this recipe.  What I hadn't counted on was how much the rest of my family would like it.  Thank you for sharing this picture perfect recipe!
Yummy! Loved them and so did the hubby. Followed the recipe pretty much exactly plus cheese and served with cilantro and tomato. It's a keeper for us!

This was really easy to fix, which was a big plus as we were super busy.  At first I was really disappointed.  I had taken the chicken out of the pan and put onto the plates.  Then my husband put some of the soy mixture that the chicken was cooked in into a bowl.  We dipped our chicken pieces into that as we ate.  It made it a whole lot better.  So if you make this and think it doesn't have taste, try dipping your chicken into the sauce as you eat.  I cooked everything for the amount of time listed.
ZWT6: Sue - this was YUM-O!! I tried this salad in Germany a few years ago and this is dead-on! Delicious!
This was my first time cooking and eating eggplant.  Wow, am I glad I used this recipe!  Delicious!

I really enjoyed this pizza.  I mixed the olive oil with the garlic powder (and added parm) and brushed that mixture over the crust (used the pizza dough from Recipe #1005).  I decreased the cheese - a lot, I didn't even use a whole 2 cups, and found that + the ricotta (part skim) was plenty.  That was the only change I made, and I'm really looking foward to making/eating this again.
Very good and only 1 point per serving! This is a keeper, thanks for sharing.
Very good! I used 1 1/4 cups of sugar but otherwise followed the recipe. I think I'll use 3 cups of rhubarb next time. Very yummy if heated up a little and served with vanilla ice-cream.

OK I did only make plain apple sauce with the slow cooker option but I would love to try it with the spices next time just to eat on it's own. I used it in Recipe #408284. I was so hungry when I came home from town and this cooked up quickly so I could pop it into my tummy! Thanks for the treat! Made by a fellow Looney Spoon Phoodie for ZWT#6!

Excellent, easy waffles! I love a healthy breakfast like this that doesn't remind me of straw and sticks. The oats gave a slightly chewy texture and with the berries, it had the perfect sweetness. We will enjoy these many times! Thanks for sharing.

This is the easiest way to make rice pudding and, Wow, so tasty. The only thing I did different was I added 1 tsp orange extract and omitted the orange zest.
I thought it would have been runny because of all the liquid in this recipe, but it was not runny at all.
I will make this one again and again. Thanks for sharing Syd.
Wonderful and easy . My cake mix was vanilla and I did not do the drizzle - very yummy indeed.

I'm used to having this in a similar recipe, tinolang manok, which uses ginger, chayote squash and we usually add potatoes too.  This is a really nice simple version.  I did it as described except I used a roasted chicken from the grocery store, and added more veggies after sauteeing the garlic/onions.  I used broccoli, greens and potatoes.  I'm modifying as my husband didn't like the recipe as much.  Also i added some Bragg's for a bit more salt flavor.

This was so good that DH was already planning when we can have it next!  I cooked it in a casserole container in the oven at 180C and that was fine, also I used thigh fillets.  Served with cous cous.  Thanks so much for a definite keeper!
Lovely flavor and easy to make.  Well worth the time and effort.  Made for X-tra Hot Dishes.
These are so good!  I left off the pepper so it wouldn't be hot for the kids and added a little cheese with the cream cheese.  Definitely a hit with the crowd!  Thanks for sharing.
Very, very good recipe! Thanks for sharing it.
Excellent!!  And very easy to make.

DH was the only one who got a chance to try this.  I had planned on something else for dinner but didn't realize until dinner was being made that I was missing a key ingredient.  This was perfect because it had a short marinade time.  I did have to use 2 teaspoons dried cilantro and bottled lime juice because it was all I had on hand.  Even with these substitutions DH enjoyed it.  Can't wait to try it again with fresh ingredients.  Next time I will make it for everyone to enjoy! Thanks so much for a quick and easy dinner!

What a wonderful surprise. I was taken aback...this is not only easy to prepare but the flavor is so good... We really enjoyed it. I picked up a packet of "shrimp" Ramen noodles and decided to cut the recipe in half because there is just the two of us...an low an behold they come in 3 oz. packages. FYI. We weren't real crazy about this.  It was warm and satisfying for a very cold night we were having, but we thought it needed something to perk it up.  Sorry, everyone has different tastes.  Made for ZWT 6.

This was great and so easy. I used only 1/4 tsp of cumin for personal preference and I was out of corn. I wanted these more like a wrap so I did not use the enchilada sauce either. I know I made quite a few changes but these were fantastic so I had to rate them. Thanks for the recipe.

Fantastic!  I used canned chunk chicken (drained juices) and chose light sour cream and red grapes. All else was exact as recipe states including the blue cheese. The 2 TBS portion of blue cheese was perfect. You don't want it to be too overpowering but just enough to taste. Any more as others mentioned wouldn't have been too much for us.  Easy and fast to whip together. This is truly a keeper recipe we will enjoy for years to come. Many thanks for posting!!
This is a great marinade for lamb. The flavor is excellent.  Made for I Recommend Tag.
Very tasty! The whole family enjoyed it!

I made these quite a few months ago and never rated them. I just forgot to. Well I have 3 co workers coming over for lunch today. I am updating some computers and adding new software, so I will be at home. I told them I would make lunch.

Wow, I had never thought to make my own buns. However, one night I had one pound of hamburger in the fridge, a hungry son and hubby and no time for the store. I was amazed at these buns, they were so good! I made them again today, but shaped them into hot dog buns for brats and they were fantastic. I will never buy buns again! Thanks so much for posting.

Love fresh cherries, and I think I got some from the first delivery to our market!  Not a better way to fix them.  This will go into my "Fabulous Ways with Cherries" cookbook.  Thnx for posting, Syd.  Made for the Voracious Vagabonds for ZWT6.

These Korean short ribs were really tasty!  I had about 1.25 lbs of ribs, so I just halved all of the marinade ingredients, which worked well.  I had to sub 100% apple juice for apple cider as that is what I had on hand.  We marinated the meat for almost 12 hours.  It was very tender and delicious.  I can't imagine adding another 1/4 cup of sugar, so I think you were right on to just use the honey.  It was plenty sweet for us (without being overly so).  We served with grilled zucchini.  Thanks for an easy, enjoyable meal!  Made for ZWT6.
Very good, simple salad.  Thanks for the recipe.

Really enjoyed these shrimp; the flavor was wonderful! Quick and easy, 2 pluses in my book! I followed the recipe, as directed, but was unsure what to do with the sesame seeds, so just sprinkled them over the shrimp. The smell wafting through the house was amazing! Thanks, **Jubes**, for sharing a simple shrimp dish, that will go in my 'go-to' cookbook! :-) Made for ZWT.

This was just the fudge recipe I was looking for! It is sooo good! And no corn syrup either! Thanks for posting!

My husband also said that it didn't look too inviting, but not sure how I could fix that.

This was awesome!  I didn't know what to do either with so many spring harvested radishes so was searching for another way to eat.  This is probably now my favorite side dish and so good for you too.  I did also add the garlic and sauteed my green tops with a little olive oil and garlic, then sprinkled a bit of balsamic vinegar over top - added the brown crispy radishes and it was a favorite at the table. Absolutely no-fail chocolate cake that's moist and chocolatey. I reduced the sugar just a bit.
